The game's been fun overall, here are some of the things I like about it:
[list]
[*] Combat is visceral, the hitstop is perfect and you feel the weight of your swings and shots.
[*] Sound FX in combination with the above and it's just chef's kiss.
[*] Pretty visuals, doesn't look like a UE-made game at first glance. Nothing to say about the performance though since I'm on a somewhat powerful rig.
[*] Worldbuilding is good enough to make you curious. I love that the Shells are actually individuals tied into it some way or another.
[*] Shell system is good. Although I wish you could respec since glimpses are scarce.
[*] Tarstones (Materia from FF7) combined with the unique weapons allows you to be creative and OP not just in a "buildup the hemorrhage bar" kinda way.
[*] I like the way they did progression in this game, it works well hand-in-hand w/ exploration.
[*] The way they did consumables are also neat.
[/list]

But, I also have more issues with the game as of writing:
[list]
[*] The way enemy attacks magnet to you is too much, a slow walking skeleton can suddenly slide across the room into you. The game forces you to either perfect dodge and parry. 
[*] I played in night mode and straight up, some of the shells abilities get invalidated due to animation lock.
[*] I've encountered sound-related issues at interim. Having it happen after that nothing ending was kinda funny.
[*] Summons a lot of times will get stuck on geometry, even when you're on flat surfaces.
[*] Your gloom sometimes will spawn in inaccessible areas. God forbid it does this when you're inside a gate because good luck finding it again (I lost 100k+ gloom this way).
[*] Some dungeons feel like they were placed there for the hell of it.
[*] There's this environmental hazard you can find in libraries that also feels like it's a case of "we have it, let's just use it".
[*] More of a nitpick, but why is there no animation for cleansing corruption when its literally your character trait? It feels as if all the budget went into the combat animations (rightly so).
[*] Enemy variety is not a lot. It feels like a lot since they throw it at you at the former parts of the game but the dudes you've been fighting at the beginning will still be there one way or another when you're in the latter part of the game.
[*] Enemy posture is unbalanced, you either permastagger them or they just don't care getting whacked by 20 tons of steel. Enemy balance overall is all over the place, a Skeleton with a dinky mace hits way harder than a f*cking Grisha.
[*] Geometry at certain places will get you stuck, there's one near the place you find Egon. Your only option is to quit to main menu. There's also the issue of elevators making you phase through them.
[*] Controls sometimes feel unresponsive wherein sometimes my character will not block and my sidearm keeps firing.
[*] You gotta make the shrine after the Mammon Gate boss glow or something, I was there for like 10 mins finding that thing.
[*] There's not much incentive to do a NG+.
[/list]

Lots of stuff that needs fixing but I do recommend the game!

I do like this game a lot, but it does have a lot of small issues. These aren't enough for me to not recommend the game. However, there is one design choice in this game that I just cannot forgive and that is shell leveling.

In this game you get a limited resource called glimpse you can use to level up your shells. The limited part is the problem. Once you use your glimpse on a shell you cannot get it back. This is a major issue for 3 reasons. 

The first one being skills you unlock for the shells. Some of the skills have fairly vague descrpitions or lack of information. You have to unlock them by spending glimpse to know if they are good or not. I'm sitting on 29 glimpse myself right now. I'm too afraid to spend them on something that might not be good.

The second reason is that you don't have access to all of the shell in the begining of the game. You unlock them by finding them in the world. So now you are left wondering if you should spend your points on the current shell you are using or save them for the next one that is maybe more to your liking.

The 3rd reason is that you also use glimpse on summons. Now this doesn't effect me since I don't use summons, but for those people who do I would imagine this is not very nice. If someone needs to use a summon to beat a boss they now also have less points to upgrade shells. So the game is punishing people who are already struggling.

I just can't recommend this game for this specifc reason. I hope the devs change this.

After about 30h I hit the credits on Mortal Shell II, and I can recommend it only if you can get it for $20~30.

The map is too large and has too many winding paths leaving you wandering around with no real ability to orient yourself or plan a path, hoping to stumble upon a mini-dungeon or a rare bonfire. The enemy variety is not that great, and the balancing of some of the enemies is way off; in the same location you might find enemies that you can facetank a whole group of, but also you might find another enemy that will combo you to death in three hits. The areas are a big too large, so you will spend way more time plowing through hordes of trash enemies, and not enough time fighting the bosses, who are, while being an obvious highlight of the game, sometimes can be hit and miss, due to the game having no linear structure to guide you to a boss of an appropriate level. Because of that a lot of my boss encounters were very one-sided — either I get bodies, or the boss does. 

The game also suffers from the usual soulslike ailment of either adding features that no one asked for, or copying better games' features without also copying underlying systems that make those features good. Why does every bonfire needs a mini-dungeon that I need to clear? Why do I need to manually mark mini-dungeons as completed? Why most of the rewards in these mini-dungeons are just a sprinkle of upgrade materials and some pocket change. Why does the game allows you to refund the skill points allotted to shells, but not Glimpses? This makes one of the achievements only achievable by going NG+2 or maybe even higher. Why does the game forces me to use the tarstones I don't want to use just to accumulate enough tarcores to upgrade actually useful tarstones? Why do we still bother with upgrading individual weapons instead of allowing the player to experiment freely with their loadout? (I know you can smelt weapons back into upgrade mats, but that still wastes a bunch of Gloom).

The active/passive PP system is probably the only interesting innovation this game brought into the genre, unfortunately the entire system is also made moot by the existance of Welcaps and Grisha Remnats which immediately become a best-in-slot, with zero reason to ever swap to anything else.

The game is also very stingy with numbers, you don't get to know whether any status effects are worth using, you don't get to know which weapon does what amount of damage, you don't get to see how stacks of buffs or debuffs affect your or enemy stats, this left me feeling rather indifferent to most tarstones and shell abilities.

Okay, this game definitely overstayed its welcome.

Let me start with the good stuff, because there is good stuff. Tons of weapons, lots of build variety, combat feels legitimately satisfying. The shell powers are creative and the combat has actual weight to it, this was my favorite part. Environments are beautiful, story is fine. If you like Sekiro or Wukong, you'll find stuff to enjoy here.

But HOLYYYY, the second half is a slog.

Soundtrack and enemy variety is non-existent. You've seen everything by the midway point, after that it's just the same ones with inflated HP and damage so overtuned they'll one-shot you or stunlock you into frustration. And the late game areas are 90% filled with the most annoying enemy in the game, with maybe two others thrown in. Why? The first half was working fine. Who thought this was a good idea?

There's legit no challenge to bosses, normal enemies hit way harder and in most cases have way more movesets.

The sound queue for unblockable attacks is straight up broken, feeling cheap, some enemies spam the same unblockable combo over and over, and you get that same audio cue stacking on itself ten times in a row. How did playtesting miss this, did NO ONE get annoyed and dared to give some feedback?

There's also tons of bugs that: killed me while inside my shell, got launched into the sky and had to restart, bosses canceling moves mid-animation to hit me with something else out of nowhere.

I don't hate it though, I actually enjoyed a lot of it. But the late-game design feels rushed, and most of these issues seem fixable. If they patch it up, this could be a genuinely good game, imo, it should've stayed a bit more in the oven.

序章诈骗的典范，序章不错的手感，丰富的肢解和处决动画让你对这游戏充满了期待，让你能够容忍这游戏的其他缺点，然后就错过了退款时间。这游戏有三大罪：
1.地图设计很粗糙，探索引导几乎没做任何设计，以至于你说他是魂like其实并不合适，没有地图设计的魂like不就是劣质arpg吗？大世界的探索体验堪称折磨，篝火很少，血瓶很少。365里路是常态，没有辨识度的地图有时候让你365里路都不知道该怎么跑。地牢设计约等于没有，有些小巧思在里面，但核心的地图设计一坨狗屎，设计出来的地图结构要不然就是一本道，要不然就是大世界探索里面的分支套分支，毫无章法让人探索的一头雾水。
2.数值设计很粗糙，序章还算收敛，到了第一个大地图，这硬伤就凸显出来了，完全没有合理的数值设计。失去躯壳的你探索体验急转直下，敌人的数值并没有匹配上你当前的状态。然后拿到第一个躯壳后，本来以为体验会好很多，但事实上并没有，因为这游戏的数值曲线根本就没被设计过，秒脱壳然后秒死是常态，无论小怪还是boss。
3.Boss战体验很糟糕，数值问题之前谈过了，这里谈交互问题。这boss战突出一个没有交互感，boss来回两招复读，感觉根本没什么设计，然后大部分招式也是粪招，有反物理吸附追踪/大范围/超高频率/短后摇各种粪性质的排列组合，你也没啥输出机会，感觉体验如同坐牢。
总而言之就是一款有一些小巧思的粪游，你说他是魂like，我说地图设计没有半点魂like的样子，就是个套着魂皮的简化了动作系统的arpg，有一些闪光的小巧思，比如说这个物品收集系统，但是总体体验是一坨。

作为类魂代餐7.5~8的水平，偶尔一品还挺有趣的，适合没什么游戏玩的纯正M。
大概前中期的体验比较新奇，妙妙小道具放的到处都是，满地图闲逛摸躯壳余露石武器什么的挺好玩的，美术设计这块几个罐头人都挺好看的，战斗看演示感觉一卡一顿的实际上手其实也是一卡一顿的，动作之间的衔接或者后摇之类的没设计好感觉不是很连续，习惯了还挺爽的，精防和闪避给的判定都挺宽松，不同的怪也有不同的处决动画，不过处决伤害是真的低。
比较逆天的点包括但不限于：篝火少前期挨一刀两瓶血再挨一刀就偷着乐吧；小怪逆天n刀连段超绝吸附性；不仅堆怪还有神秘锁定；没有边缘保护喜欢悬崖边战斗的有福了；地图设计很乱，看似四通八达实则上半图充满了意味不明没用过几次的捷径；道具光点又透又亮，几乎和背景融为一体，死了留下的魂又小又不明显，有几次找了半天没找到魂；一些不可再生资源比如强化躯壳的瞬悟给的非常少和克制。
目前还不能洗掉强化过的躯壳，导致玩起来总觉得畏畏缩缩的。类似这样的武器强化也有这个毛病，如果不喜欢砍npc的话基本要到快通关才能洗掉武器强化，非常不利好什么都想品味的人。一周目基本只能品尝一两个流派，不过真的有人想玩多周目吗。也正是因为流派不能随便换，就得固定一直玩一样的套路，或者穿个白板在身上，所以很容易审美疲劳。
打久了有点无趣，毕竟成本也就这样了。大概到中后期bd成型后开始砍瓜切菜激情互秒，几个躯壳各有各的优点，每个玩家都觉得自己在玩轮椅。话又说回来，因为成本也就这样了所以后期纯套皮小怪纯加数值这块，叠两百层血还是会被小兵几刀送走或者精英怪两刀砍死这块，更别提神秘代码狂切宠爱几千层剑骸小big了。
bd成型以后基本上没什么卡boss的情况，大家全是电锯大人的减速带（盾斧大人？何时来的）。打到后期基本上全是重复性堆怪，小角落放一些没用小道具，没什么探索欲望，只想快点通关。不过点名一下最终boss，顶级血牛dps检测，加上雷霆大跳连续后跳前挥刀零秒投技，星疫机制杀。真打笑了，不拿护种人经文，纯靠立回基本不可能打赢，交互起来恶心坏了，评价为顶级大份。

'Required reading' for souls-like fans. 
The first MS was great, this entry is even better. The team has effectively improved on everything that made the first entry great. 
The combat is sublime, the brilliant 'Harden' mechanic is back (as well as Parry and Repost abilities) along with a slew of new abilities each Shell has, all varied and unique to each Shell. 
The world is open and significantly larger than the previos entry and NPC questlines are now present. Even the Lutes are back and have their own combat mechanics. 
The Shells now all have their own robust backstories told through interactive cutscenes. 
Difficulty is challenging but not punishingly-so, every death feels like a 'that was my fault' situation. 

I don't want to speak too soon before properlly finishing the game but so far this may be my top ranked souls-like.

Must-buy for both Mortal Shell fans and souls-like fans.

I've really enjoyed my time with this game so far, it has a really cool world and vibe, fun combat, and cool build variations. It also exacerbates another problem which is enemy abilities to lunge attack you from 50+ feet away and one shot you. While annoying it would be slightly less of a problem if there was more beacons to rely on. The last problem I had is the souls "gotcha" moments. You know the ones. The walk around a corner and get hit sideways into an exploding barrel that insta gibs you. That sort of stuff. Mortal Shell 2 is a great game overall, and I’m glad I bought it. I’d give it a solid 8/10.

There’s a lot to like here, but the biggest problem is that the game often feels frustrating rather than genuinely difficult. Those are two very different things. I’ve beaten Elden Ring, the DLC, and gone through New Game Plus, so I’m no stranger to challenging games. The issue here isn’t simply difficulty—it’s the way that difficulty is sometimes created.

There are an enormous number of traps, enemies and bosses that spam moves, awkward camera and lock-on behavior, and moments that feel designed to waste the player’s time rather than test their skill. Lifts not resetting properly is especially annoying, and the bugs only make some of these situations worse.

Playing with a controller also feels noticeably clunky. The controls and movement don’t always feel as responsive or precise as they should, which becomes a much bigger problem in a game where timing, positioning, dodging, and camera control matter so much.

At times, it feels like the game is trying too hard to prolong the experience by adding irritating mechanics instead of meaningful challenges. A difficult encounter can be satisfying when you know what you did wrong and improve. A frustrating encounter just makes you wonder why the game was designed that way in the first place.

Despite all of that, Mortal Shell 2 is still a genuinely good game with a lot going for it. I enjoyed my time with it, I’m happy I bought it, and I’d still recommend it to fans of the genre. It just needs some polishing and a better balance between challenging the player and frustrating them.

**Mortal Shell 2 é muito superior ao primeiro jogo**, e é impressionante ver o quanto a equipe evoluiu em praticamente todos os aspectos. O mundo aberto funciona muito bem e a exploração é fluida, enquanto as novas carcaças ficaram fenomenais, assim como a variedade de armas.

Apesar disso, existem alguns bugs e decisões de design que prejudicaram um pouco minha experiência.

Um dos principais problemas está no combate e no funcionamento de algumas habilidades. Em certos momentos, mesmo quando o golpe claramente não acerta o inimigo, a animação continua normalmente e você simplesmente causa 0 de dano. Também aconteceu várias vezes de eu estar de frente para um inimigo, usar uma habilidade e ela acabar sendo direcionada para o lado. Em um jogo no qual posicionamento e precisão são tão importantes, isso acaba sendo bastante frustrante.

Outro ponto que me incomodou foi o balanceamento dos inimigos, principalmente do meio para o final do jogo. A vida e o dano de alguns mobs escalam de maneira exagerada. Chega ao ponto de certos inimigos comuns, teoricamente de nível mais baixo, causarem mais dano do que alguns bosses. Isso deixa a progressão um pouco inconsistente.

A distribuição dos "faróis" pelo mapa também poderia ser melhor. Existem áreas enormes entre um ponto e outro e, em alguns momentos, precisei atravessar praticamente uma região inteira apenas para recuperar as Penumbras. Isso acaba prejudicando justamente a exploração, porque você começa a evitar determinados caminhos sabendo que não haverá um lugar próximo para descansar e recuperar seus recursos. Senti falta de algum item consumível, mesmo que raro ou limitado, que permitisse recuperar Penumbras sem depender exclusivamente dos faróis.

No geral, **Mortal Shell 2 é um bom jogo e uma evolução enorme em relação ao primeiro**. Gostei bastante do mundo, das novas carcaças, das armas e da direção que a equipe tomou. Porém, ainda existem problemas de balanceamento e algumas mecânicas básicas que precisam ser refinadas.

Com alguns ajustes e atualizações, acredito que o jogo pode ficar muito melhor, porque a base que construíram aqui é excelente.

This didn't change after leveling up my character and upgrading my sword.

Also, I feel like there are problems with feedback regarding getting hit, as I won't realize I got hit until I look at my health bar and I'm one hit away from death.

This game is definitely a challenge, and I hope that if you decide to buy the game you will have the patience required to master it.

Combat feels floaty and imprecise. Your weapon attacks have an exaggerated forward trajectory, and with a lot of combat sections taking place on bridges and cliffsides, you'll often be falling off edges. Enemies also have magnetic tracking attacks that lunge at you through/around terrain, so spacing isn't an option.

Enemy attack animations are not well designed, a lot of attacks have very little telegraphing, and some are almost instant. Enemies also have multiple different strings with almost identical looking wind up animations, and it made trying to learn their patterns frustrating. I've also experienced an enemy cancelling out of an attack into a command grab that I couldn't avoid, which felt cheap and unfair.

There are so many gank sections, you'll often be juggling 5 or more mobs at any given time, and it felt like a cheap way of raising difficulty. Any game is hard if you throw enough sh*t at the player. There's also no checkpoints at the start of dungeons, so say hello to tedious, time consuming runbacks.

I have played games more difficult than this, but there was no frustration because the challenge felt fair, and combat and encounters were thoughtfully designed. This just wasn't it for me.

i play a lot of souls like games. this game is ballsack. the bosses have 2-3 variation on attack patterns and sometimes they get coded special transition abilities but that happens rarely. the enemies are the same way there isnt a dynamic enemy attack pattern just the same copy paste lines of attacks which wouldn't be a problem if the gameplay was interesting but the sliding, tracking, 90 degree snapping of enemies when you are to the side of them makes the telegraphs annoying. they put a parry tool into the game that locks you into a parry animation and after successfully parrying with it you are stunned. the enemies get to continue their attack combo and hit you for free because you landed a parry.

Not to mention the game feels like slop, they created all of these great assets and animations only to throw them together in a way that makes every aspect of the game worse as you progress. by the time you get to the third beacon boss you realize the game isnt going to get any better and in fact most of the time you were experiencing the best part of the gameplay in the first 30% of the playthrough. 

What i heard about this game is it was originally designed to be a roguelike game and got crammed into a campaign and as soon as i heard it everything made sense. the builds, the enemies, the redundant dungeons and beacons. everything stems from creating a highly modular system then pivoting halfway through development to slap a campaign together to sell the game for 50 bucks. is this game worth it? if you like playing through games that get worse as they go then go for it. It's enjoyable enough but i was completely bored by 60% of the way through the game.

Mortal shell 1 was bad but it had more soul than this does. If they had committed to the roguelike element this might have actually been a much better experience than the current state of the game.

Перебиндил блок на правую кнопку мыши, и игра превратилась в Sekiro.
До уровня бабадзаки, конечно, не дотягивает, но вполне играбильно. У софтваров все локации разные, и сами игры не кажутся однотипными, в этой же игре враги на каждой локации одни и те же, просто меняется их атрибут, например, яд на кровь(справедливости ради первую половину ВСЕЙ локации мне игра очень заходила, потом моё "ЗАХОДИЛО" превратилось просто в "НОРМ"), так же некоторые локации не кажутся интересными, например, подземелья и пещеры(они вообще все одинаковые, такое ощущение, что просто везде один и тот же шаблон использовали). Один из главных минусов - нет того кайфа при битье мобов, как у бабадзаки, при ударах не чувствуется экшена, враги вообще на них почти не реагируют, а сами удары не кажутся такими тяжёлыми что ли, правда, не знаю как это назвать. На каждого босса уходит не больше 5-7 попыток, зачастую и одной хватает. Половина оболочек кажутся неиграбильными, в том смысле, что разницы почти никакой в них нет(Лично мне понравился варвар из таверны, остальные вообще не зашли). Почти все "тариты" бесполезные, думаю, тут объяснять не надо. Ночь не сильно сложнее дня, я всю вторую половину карты пробегал в ночи и могу сказать, что разница на обычных мобах в 1-2 удара(я сделал билд через криты и проклятье крови, может, в этом причина), на боссах не сравнивал, но они достаточно быстро умирали. Ночь могли сделать поинтереснее, не делать жирнее мобов, а добавить других врагов например или ещё чего, хз.
P.S. футфетишиста в крепости убил при второй встрече в оболочке варвара, а ♥♥♥♥ он отказывается их мыть.

Ну вот такой хотя бы должен был быть Мортал Шелл 1, чтобы я не считал его говном. Считаю справедливым переименовать Мортал Шелл 1 в Мортал Шелл 0, а Мортал Шелл 2 — в Мортал Шелл 1. Ну, типа, с вот этой игры я бы уже назвал хорошим старт разрабов. Бтв, и на первой они норм пожрали, ещё и вроде эксклюзивность у эпиков была, так что бабосики имелись, плюс ещё и крупный инди‑издатель у второй части...

Ну, драцлинг тут пиздатый: он и простой, но и в то же время забавный. Типа ты можешь комбинить атаки — что в целом и в Соулсах есть, — но при этом более круто интегрированные абилки, плюс прикольный самострел на любой вкус, разные виды перри, а перекраты даже разные у персов бывают. По боевке и геймплею ваще вопросов нет — это реально весело.

Понравилось, что на каждый вид моба есть своя анимация крита, и они все хорошие. И ладно было бы тут мобов 5 разновидностей, но их гораздо больше.

Ну, к слову о мобах: их не слишком много. Я хз, не считал, но сказать, что их штук 100 разновидностей, — это точно нет. Часто встречаются мобы, которых ты уже встречал когда‑то, а если вы играли в 1 часть, то и тут флешбекните со многого, но как раз‑таки в этом я проблем не вижу. Простить разнообразие могу. БТВ, разрабы это сами понимали и всё‑таки старались миксовать — спасибо.

Боссов немало, но и не много — в целом окей. Большинство боссов, конечно, — усиленные рядовые нпц, но хотя бы им дали чё‑то уникально — уже спасибо. Это я тоже могу простить, так как понимаю, что всё‑таки проект далеко не ААА, да и неизвестно, насколько он даже АА.

Масштаб мира считаю идеальным. Он далеко не миниатюрный, но и не здоровый, как Элдарик. Тут насыщено всяким контентом типа тарстоунов (таликами я их называю) и заточек и т. д. По сравнению с Элдариком, где большое количество всяких золотых фекалий и прочего дерьма, я считаю это хорошим решением.

А вот локации, точнее, просто про арт‑дизайн — скучновато. Спасибо, что в целом понадобавляли всякие замки, деревеньки — это прикольно. Но сказать, что я бы что‑то запомнил… Типа Грибная деревня запоминается, потому что она в начале, и интересные вот эти мобы с вдохновением из славянского фолькльора (бабки). Есть лока с красными деревьями, но сказать, что там что‑то было ещё, кроме красных деревьем, интересное, — не могу. Если будет ДЛЦ или некст часть, то я бы советовал делать арт‑дизайн попизже, чтобы ты запоминал ваще, чё где.

Музыка такая же. Хз, в трейлерах всякий металл показывали, а тут какой‑то эмбиент иногда играет на просто локах, а во время файта с боссами какой‑то одинаковый пердеж. Ну такое, если честно.

Анимации хромают у боссов иногда — это тоже бы на карандашик взять. Да и дизайн боссов, плюс сложность — такие се. Из ± нормального — дизайн у принца (муха такая с мечом и щитом в первой фазе), у Отброса или Отродья (не помню точно нейм), да и всё, хз. Ласт босс ваще с багами… Да и в целом баги есть, но прям критичного чего‑то по игре не было, кроме ток ласт босса.

Дизайн оболочек — круто.

По идее, НГ+ ещё поинтереснее и драйвовее играться должны. Ибо ты, по сути, можешь апать оружие бесконечно, плюс стакать пассивки с грибов и т. д. Вроде бы прикольно.

Наверное, самые главные аспекты я выделил.

Сейчас осталась, по сути, 1 ачивка (все воспоминания посмотреть). Мб в ближайшее время дозакрою и потом вернусь на фулл‑прохождение НГ+ и т. д., потому что вроде интересно вернуться.

На последнем костре (светоче) прикольно сделали, спасибо! :)

Mortal Shell 2 has quickly become one of my absolute favorite "Souls-like" games, and it’s easy to see why. It takes everything the original did well and elevates it into something richer, sharper, and far more immersive. This sequel feels like a studio firing on all cylinders — confident in its identity, bold in its design, and completely committed to delivering a punishing yet rewarding experience.

On PC, the game runs smooth, looks stunning, and feels incredibly responsive. The improved animations, lighting, and environmental detail make exploring each zone a visual treat.

The combat is the star of the show. Every swing, dodge, and Harden feels weighty and deliberate. Enemies hit hard, but learning their patterns and mastering your shell’s strengths creates that addictive loop where every victory feels earned. It’s challenging, but never unfair — the game respects your time and skill.

The expanded shell system is phenomenal. Each shell feels like its own playstyle, not just a stat tweak. Whether you’re leaning into heavy, tanky builds or agile, precision-focused ones, the game encourages experimentation. And once you find “your” shell, the game becomes an extension of your instincts.

Mortal Shell 2 is a powerful, atmospheric, and brilliantly crafted action RPG that stands tall among the best Soulslike experiences on PC. It’s challenging, stylish, and endlessly rewarding — a game that hooks you early and refuses to let go. For me, it’s become one of my favorites, and I can’t wait to keep diving deeper into its world.

TLDR:
1. The game is hard not because the enemies are smart and need a lot of thinking, but because player is intentionally crippled to the point of moving and fighting like an old-lady with a 30 kg crowbar.

3. No variability - the moves you find rewarding at the first hour of the game stay rewarding after 10 hours in

The game is literally crooked. The coding problems are present, the moveseet of ANY enemy if faster and more agile than yours no matter what type of weapon you use.
Enemies have lock-on on their every hit on you (and by lock-on I mean even if they in the middle of the hit and you evade the hit slightly off-time, they will automatically turn IN THE MIDDLE OF THE HIT THEY DO and hit you). 
The parrying and guarding mechanics are broken - the whole game industry used pretty much the same timings on those things and here they are different, even from the souls-like games. 
No predictable damage - you literally do not understand what would your next hit worth to the enemy's HP. 
No abilities - literally. You're bound to use one ability per shell. 
Two or more enemies - you're dead unless you run around like a maniac and use hit-and-run tactic - combos are only working when you're:
    a-with only one opponent 
    b-know his EVERY move. 
Seals are useless (at least the ones in the first half of the game) - as I mentioned, blocking-parrying-guarding-hardening timings are off and it will take a lot of time to re-learn this new pattern. 
No ability to tank damage at all - no matter what shell you use, you're paper thin even to low-level enemies. 
Targeting is uncomfortably lousy - when you hit something with any weapon, the actual place you hit is not the place you swing at. Had a lot of issues hitting one feather away to the left or right from the enemy. 
Old stupid die-and-run-for-10-miles setup for beacons. In the souls-like game. 
No stagger, even with the big heavy weapons, unless you use one specific weapon that has a knock-out move or use parry-guard-harden with wrong timing. 
Inability to use multiple commands simultaneously - every move has to be finished before you invoke the next command. 
Light weapons hit with the same speed as heavy weapons - literally, so there is no point in using then at all, because damage is lower.  The only thing you have is those shells - and there is like 8 of them and that's it, you have 8 different abilities for the whole game. 
Supplements-tarstones etc do nothing if you're not over-levelled - most of the times there are multiple enemies and you again have to hit-and-run with every one of them because there is nothing that will allow you to wipe even the low-level ones. 
Map is useless - the terrain design is more confusing than a real world so you HAVE to memorize every turn to get to your destinations. In 2026, ffs.
Consumables are useless - as I mentioned, if your enemy is on par with you on level, single use of a healing doesn't even restore the damage from one hit. 
When your shell is killed, after-death animation and "knock-out" expolsion is useless most of the times, because you're literally "thrown away" from your shell for a long distance, so every time you rise with this explosion, it hits nothing but terrain, because all the enemies are far away.
Mana for abilities is used for sidearms too and, if abilities are somewhat useful, range weapons are only damaging when you put all the charges into ONE enemy. 
Status effects (fire, poison) hit you, but don't have any significant effect on the enemy - it will take 10-15 minutes for every enemy to die from non-stop fire status effect or poison. 
No digits - no normal human-readable table or grid to see what your bonuses are.
Light in the game is sometimes too dark on default settings - in dark areas (dungeons etc) you may look straight into the enemy and don't see them because they are as dark as surrouding walls.
Dying and picking up gloom repeatedly for some reason gives you more gloom (not a significant amount, like +1 gloom per 1-2 deaths), but that's a rookie coding mistake. 
You can't jump! In 2026, after Elden Ring was presented to the community!
Randomly one-hit-one-kill non-rare enemies, like miners with little candles on their heads. You meet them in the early game and they can two-shot your shell and one-shot you with every hit and they hit a lot, because they have one-hand pickaxes and spam it.
You got staggered when you're hit and the enemy is not. Unless, again, you use one specific weapon with one specific move, it is impossible to stagger the enemy no matter their level or rarity.
Poor loot situation - it is an open world game, but so far I got literally 4 different loot items that are not tarstones or weapons. Nothing about craft-mixing-making anything either because of that.
8 or more different shells but in 12 hours, roughly, I am yet to unlock a single useful passive ability for the ones I got my hands on - so when you find a shell, you have X ways to fight and after playing and opening the 3 out of 4 tiers with it you still have X ways to fight and the changes to the skills are useless.

The game was actually fun but i had a bug which made my save file vanish twice. The first time it was after 2 hours the second time was after about 6. Tried all online recommended fixes but nothing worked. Since i've played over 2 hours Steam is refusing a refund.

I can't recommend this game, as much as I might've wanted to when I started. The opening is VERY strong and I was so excited to dive into this title, especially after an excellent open beta. I loved the systems and still do, especially the modding via Tarstones. 

However, I genuinely don't think it's worth your time, at least in its current state. 

Among the numerous issues, a few stand out as the reason I think you should skip this one.

- Enemies frequently move in absurd ways, closing the gap with regular melee attacks even though they're well outside of reach at the start of it. 

- Bosses do the same thing! So it's not a test of skill or learning the fight and instead hoping you can get through their glitched out nonsense. They simply slide towards you as though by magic.

- Boss fights are underwhelming, and are also either glitched or poorly designed. Without spoiling the mechanics, the longer you get into the game the worse the experience gets, especially for the major ones.

- Parry and riposte are glitched. Not only is the timing inconsistent, but sometimes you will still take damage from other nearby enemies during a riposte animation.

- Exploration is unrewarding. Some of the mini dungeons have cool atmosphere or interesting rewards, but on the whole you just end up finding a single upgrade stone. Cool?

- Animations start breaking down the longer you go into the game. 

- Stability issues. Admittedly I'm on Linux so you can put this one in whatever column makes sense for you. But launching it is so unreliable that it sometimes crashes the steam client after it lags for a while starting. Yes, I am fully patched and up to date on drivers, etc.

There's a lot more but in short, don't get this game. I wanted to like and still want to! But it's not that game. My clue was when I found myself wanting to just get to the next broken boss to finish it. It stopped being something I wanted to invest time into and something I wanted to check a box on. Maybe Mortal Shell 3 will finally get it right? But for now, this falls into Lords of the Fallen territory for me: a cool idea that doesn't execute.

I wanted to love this game, but the difficulty tuning is a mess. The bosses in the early to mid game are almost comically easy, but in between the bosses I wasn't able to get anywhere without several deaths to basic enemies. Every single normal enemy in the game that I've encountered can 3-shot you. Most of them 2-shot you. A few of the elites can 1-shot you.

In practice, what this meant for me is that I was engaged and intrigued on my first foray into a new corner of the map. Then, after several frustrating and deflating deaths, I would simply run through that area and "explore" while being chased by a pack of relentless enemies, which shatters tension, immersion, and breaks the entire contract of the game.

I know some people love this game, and those people probably aren't wrong (there are a lot of them). But to me, this is a game that reaches for a kind of "hardcore" that I don't really find fun at the best of times, and these are not the best of times.

Among my specific gripes:

- The magnetism on enemy attacks is truly wild, meaning it's hard to correctly position because you never know when a huge knight with a zweihander is going to snap 20 feet to you mid attack and clobber you for 90% of your health.
- Attacks from large enemies hit you several frames before the animation would suggest.
- Shell special attacks miss for no reason, leaving you vulnerable.
- Everything staggers the player, but seemingly nothing staggers even basic enemies.
- The camera is disorienting at best, nauseating at worst
- Basic enemy combos are endless and uninterruptible
- Basic enemy encounters are orders of magnitude more difficult than early and mid game bosses
- Upgrade materials are rare to the point that it punishes experimentation

Many of the tuning issues are a result of the game having no stamina, meaning you can dodge and attack without pausing. What this actually means is that the game is often hilariously lethal toward the player. If you've ever had the experience in other Soulslikes of rolling your eyes when you die to a boss because it felt cheap, that's the experience of clearing basic enemies on the way to bosses. Then you beat the bosses on the first or second attempt, every time.

My personal breaking point was the Infested Miner dungeon. It probably isn't the hardest area in the game, but it was where my patience for Cold Symmetry's bizarre sadism ran out.

Sadly, I've uninstalled. I'd love to reinstall someday, so I'll be keeping my fingers crossed for a 2.0 release that addresses some of the above issues.

As a souls fan, I thoroughly enjoyed the optimization (PHENOMENAL), sound design, art direction and just the variety they provide in regards to combat. A HUGE step up from MS1 and I hope Cold Symmetry capitalizes on this one with updates to bolster the game and continue to create great games like this!

To start, it's fine if you like this game!  I get how it could be a lot of people's cup of tea, but for me there were just a few choices that stacked up over time & eventually I decided I just wasn't interested in playing any further.  Let me be clear, I'm not complaining that the game was too difficult!  On the contrary, without hard mode making the enemies damage sponges it was too easy on the whole.  

I probably won't get the steam refund since it's been 7.6 hours, (if that's steam's decision no harm no foul.) 
Here are a few of the choices that bugged me consistently during my playtime: 
Small nitpicks

-I'll grant it was a cool moment, but giving us that first shell then taking it away annoyed me in a way I can't really explain.  I tried the tutorial area again three times to see if you can beat the Tar Golem to keep him, got him low on the 3rd try before a cutscene triggered and took the shell anyway.  Why even give me control/the illusion of being able to affect an outcome?  It would have been a much better choice if you lose that shell here by losing and can get him back later, or can skill check the boss and then get to start with him instead.

-The God of War 2018 elevators in literally every mini-dungeon... there's already a loading screen to enter & cleanse, why then add another elevator where I have to wait?  

-I bought the Sariel location on my first visit to the hub because I just perused which shell looked cool to me; thought I'd head out to get him first since the game essentially invites you to do this and it felt like where things are supposed to open up.  Quickly learned the first part of Mammon you can get into is full of enemies that take no damage and cut you in half in one swipe.  After some trying I understood I just wasn't ready for that zone, fair play I suppose, but it was annoying to waste 10k for no reason & really felt like the game was punishing me for trying to go any way but the intended one.  Why even let me go there?
Big nitpicks
-Sound design in this game was great, very crisp & crunchy.  The music was an earsore though, I can only listen to the overplayed droning brass notes so much.  Some life came into it with the guitars during the overly cinematic walking-to-the-hub title sequence... but that didn't last.  A lot of the areas would have benefited from just being silent, letting the regular ambience/sound design set the tone.  Not one memorable song throughout my playtime; it was like I went on youtube & searched "3 hour horror droning" then played the first thing I found.

-"Hard Mode" being the worst kind of difficulty spike, just inflating enemy health and damage.  Which is a same, because it seems to change enemy placements and add some npc's/enemies that you don't see otherwise?  Honestly I'd be fine with the damage bit, since you can parry- but the health is just honestly obnoxious.  I turned it off once I got to Magdalena (♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, so much health), but there were a lot of enemies before then that I was not threatened by, but just had to spend FOREVER hacking down.  From what I looked up it seems like you're just supposed to turn on hard mode when you find certain messages/at certain places, but again this feels like sort of a bait and switch/deception... it only tells you turn on hard mode to "increase rewards".  

-Checkpoint placement is all over the place.  This game REALLY needs the Elden Ring stakes.  No checkpoints in the minidungeons at times gets exhausting.  Sometimes there's one right around the corner from another, sometimes there's a mini-dungeon you find that with no checkpoint inside forces you to do a tedious runback.
-Enemy attack animations/timings, there are a lot of attacks where the enemy either spins on an axis, or slides forward to hit you.  This is dreadful for gamefeel, a lot of the time when I got hit it was because an enemy raised their weapon to swing, I judge they can't hit me from that distance, and then they slide forward to clip me anyway.  

-The frog shaman enemies that are A. Not at all fun/interesting to fight & B. Will stand 40 feet away and heal each other (PARTICULARLY with the hard mode quadrouple HP) are horrendous design.  


That's about it, like I said if you like this game I understand, it just isn't for me.  If you're looking for a soulslike, I suppose this may scratch the itch, but honestly the developers have made a slew of questionable choices, directly contradicting their inspiration- many of the games they clearly draw inspiration from did these things right.

В целом Mortal Shell 2 — хорошее продолжение для любителей жанра.

its... ok. 

Gameplay: it is alright, so long as you have low latency settings enabled on system and TV and avoid frame gen. Otherwise expect to get wrecked thinking you blocked/dodged something when the game thinks differently. Its a tad floaty, but that may just be a personal preference.

Story: it is a footnote at best. Most NPCs have 2-3 lines and the repeat those every time you talk to them (for at least the first 8 hours i've played). I literally have no idea what I'm doing other than wandering around and slaying what i find. There seems to be no goal other than "find eggs", Why "find eggs"? Who knows, nobody says why. For all i know they want to make a huge omelette later. I guess the shells have story, but its more a backstory,

World: beautiful, but also very depressing. Its typical grim-dark fare. Expect to see a lot of black, grey, and brown, splattered with green grass and bone white. Its also splattered with mini dungeons. not all of them are really worth doing, but you usually get something you can use, but sometimes that something is not particularly great (i.e., weapon upgrade currency). Also, be careful about accepting the "return to start of dungeon" after defeating a boss, as you may miss-out on items that are still in/adjacent to the boss room.

Shells: are okay. Other than 2-3 signature abilities that change their playstyle they dont really tell you much at all why one shell is different than another (i.e., this one has more HP, this one attacks faster, this one can doge better, etc.) leading to a guess and check annoyances.

Weapons: are similar to shells. Unless you actually try them, there is no way to see if X weapon is slower or faster or does more damage than Y weapon. More guess and check.

Graphics: standard UE5 fare, but at least the performance this time seemed to be decent for a new release. would have liked more guidance with setting up brightness since the world is VERY DARK, you may want to set it to at least 1.3-1.5 to see anything in the darker areas.

Audio: music is mostly absent, or at least it was unremarkable I literally cannot recall it being present. Sound FX and Ambiance is decent and do the majority of the heavy lifting from a sound design perspective. This may be why the world feels so depressing, its missing that something to bring it to life.

Bugs: yes, plenty. Animation Glitches, Enemy AI glitches, Abilities getting stuck and never completing their refresh, etc. do they happen all the time? no. do they happen enough to be annoying, yes. are some reliably reproducable, yes. do some happen randomly, also yes.

Overall Verdict: wait or skip. Wait if you loved the first one and want more of it. Skip, if you're wanting a deeply satisfying soulslike with an intriguing world.

Итак, игра полностью пройдена, все данжи залутаны, но впечатление от игры неоднозначные... хотя если просуммировать все, то я считаю игра стоит свеч.
Графика
Игра однозначно красивая, вблизи все выглядит довольно детализировано и гротескно. По игре разбросаны точки, где она сама намекает на скриншот (хотя на мой вкус не везде это уместно), но все биомы визуально узнаются и в целом ориентироваться приятно и без карты. Хватает уникальных мест мелочей которые запоминаются 
P.S. Почему вход в 90% данжей выглядит одинаково там конечно буквально одна комната со спуском, но очень уж сильно бросается в глаза на фоне остальной проделанной работы
Билдостроение
Тут у нас не классическая сосалик система. По факту 8 уникальных оболочек со своими абилками, пассивками и историей (простенькой, но за попытку и необычную реализацию лайк). я полностью изучил 4 из них и точно можно сказать, что все реально влияют на геймплей и меняют подход к бою. Более того каждая из них прокачивает и к концу игры (без специализированного фарма) я мог выкачать каждую оболочку в одно из двух направлений. В итоге 16 билдов с закосом во что-то конкретное, однако насколько я понимаю более 4 оболочек выкачать за 1 прохождение просто не получиться так как на карте заканчивается ресурс необходимый для этого. 
Так же в игре по 8 пушек ближнего и дальнего боя с уникальными паттернами атак и в каждую можно вставить артефакт на пассивку, активку и намазку. + 4 артефакт с пассивками на персонажа. В итоге получается довольно неплохое количество билдов хотя и не все из них реально работают. Хотя их прокачка опять же слишком затруднена... да их можно перекачивать чтобы попробовать все, но мне под конец игры без фарма золота хватило почти в притык чтобы прокачать только две пушки до максимума а процесс перекача не самый быстрый, да и цена на заточку излишне завышена...
Боссы
Они тут ВСЕ уникальные (господи спасибо, а то после элдена мне плохо стало от повторок). И они НЕ СТАНОВЯТСЯ рядовыми противниками! (за исключением парочки мини боссов, но это простительно т.к. количество уникальных врагов реально большое для такой игры). Впервые их количество хп не завышено (не считая ласт босса, обычным билдом его реально долго ковырять можно, но я нашел несколько сборок для легкого прохождения даже без пота и лишнего фарма). Несмотря на различные дизайны и в том числе боссов больше персонажа, 80% всех анимаций легко читаются и парируются после 3-4 траев. 
Баги
я играл по предрелизу и бог ты мой... такое количество багов я давно не видел... Где-то коллизия кривая и персонаж застревает или втыкается в нее. пару раз мобы взлетали в небо после отталкивания, пару раз меня зажимали и я взлетал в небо, оружие пропадало и чтобы оно появилось приходило менять его пару раз. С другой стороны это все 100% починят в ближайшие пару недель и снижать оценку за это я не буду
Минусы
1. Магнетизм, магнетизм и еще раз магнетизм... Абсолютно все атаки врагов притягивают к персонажу, хотя справедливости ради и персонаж своими атаками не хило притягивается к ним да. AOE атак у противников почти нет и видимо так разработчик решил нивелировать это.
2. Костры расставлены реально плохо. Иногда надо бежать по 7-10 минут до места последней смерти. А к главным боссам почти всегда нужно бежать 2-3 минуты и это плохо, потому что иногда босс буквально может убить первым же комбо из 3-4 ударов.
3. ХП некоторых оболочек при фулл прокачке оставляет желать лучшего... они буквально ваншотятся 1 ударом даже рядовых мобов и это уже не окей. Билды стеклянной пушки тут реально стеклянные и не прощает даже легкой ошибки
4. Камера.... в сосаликах так и не научились делать нормальную камеру, но тут это усугубляется тем, что 70% атак боссов довольно сильно отталкивают персонажа и все они бьют комбухами на маленьких аренах... в итоге после парирования 2 ударов последующие ты парируешь на чуйке
Итог
Игра однозначно не дотягивает до уровня AAA-проекта, но она им и не является. Игра реально приносит новизну в жанр сосаликов и делает это как минимум НЕПЛОХО. Лично мне не пришлось нигде фармить и за 30 часов у меня остались в основном положительные впечатления, но вот ценник в 2200 руб я считаю завышенным... 1500-1800 руб цена этой игре
P.S.S. ПОЛНОСТЬЮ НЕВИДИМЫЙ БОСС это абсурд... да я понял механику его арены, но 70% времени все равно сражаешься наугад и это НЕ ОКЕЙ, где хотя бы звуковые предупреждения об атаке. Единственный босс заставивший меня нажать alt+f4 и сделать перерыв
Reminder that there are two missable achievements in a playthrough and one achievement (not missable) needing special currency upwards of 2-3 playthroughs worth to complete, so take it as you will.

Not worth it in its current state.

The good  -

Art style
Certain Weapon move-sets. Especially the Great-axe.
Statuses seem reasonably strong (poison, fire, frost)
Shells are very interesting and varied. Despite limited numbers.
Characters are few but some are memorable.
Shell memories offer much needed depth
Performance seems solid.

Now for the hot garbage  - 
No checkpoints at start of dungeons, mines or wells. All basically dungeons in all but name.
No checkpoints before bosses in dungeons
No shortcut or instant exit after boss fights. Enjoy your long run back, likely death and loss of boss souls.

Many bosses are extremely simple, whereas overworld enemies are OP by comparison
Tracking on projectiles is appalling. The ranged machine gun will often miss most rounds from short to mid range.
Enemies love to ice skate like NHL pros when closing the gap instantly before wasting you.

No fast travel in open world, have to be at a checkpoint which are few and far between.
Light heavy and charged heavy attacks are equippable items lmao. Should be a part of the core movesets. 
Guarding and parrying are only gained from equipment as well. Cannot have both on at the same time.

Heavy weapons are absolutely useless. No hyper armour, no damage reduction during swings, No poise damage to enemies. Damage is low, extremely slow move sets often get you killed, mid animation.  Complete trash from top to bottom.

Tiels shadow strike (think stealthy Assassins Creed type attack) will often just miss enemies point blank. 
Lots of enemies get stuck in terrain.
Camera can be awkward and frustrating. 

No mini-map which makes navigation a chore. 
Limited upgrade materials for shells. 
Levelling often feels inconsequential as enemies still blow you away. 

The balance of end game enemies is all over the place. Some will one tap you and others seem to do proportional damage. 

Lots of cheap and lazy mechanics in this title. Feels like they cut corners wherever they could. Which unfortunately detracts from it's strengths.

Wait for patches and a Steam sale.
Wait for the much- needed rebalancing patches that will hopefully come. The infusion weapon limits make no sense, and status builds need a ton of work to be viable. Has great bones underneath.

다른 게임사에서 후속작을 내놨으면 파묻히는 그정도 수준의 게임인데 현재로선 나름재미있게 하고있기때문에 추천을줬다.

장점:
그래픽이 2026년 게임이라고 불릴만큼 그래픽이 잘뽑혀나왔다. 5080을쓰고있긴하나 최적화도 나름잘되서 프레임이 매끄럽다. 
오픈월드라고 자칭해도될만큼 맵이넓고 구경거리가 많다. 자유도가 높은편이다. 적당한 퍼즐난이도로 고민을하게하는것도 재미요소인거같다.

단점:
뭔가 타격감이 엉성함이있다. 처음에주는 대검으로 몹을치다보면 뭔가 뭔가이다. 이 타격감은 무기가 바뀌면서 좀 나아진거같다.  히트박스도 뭔가 가끔 이상한 히트박스가 있는거같다 (칼이 몹을 관통했는데 안맞은판정)
몹 재탕하는 그런건없으나 몹종류가 결국엔 생각보다 없다. 그래서 어려운난이도로가면 그냥 피통/공격만 늘린 몹들만 늘어나서 지루함이 점점생긴다.
요즘시대에 안맞게 맵이동은 불편하게해뒀다.
밸런스가 엉망이다. 공속이빠른게 장땡이고 공속느린 무기쓸이유를 못찾겠다.
재화가모잘라서 결국엔 다양한시도는 못하고 선택과 집중이 요구된다.


소울류 게임에 진심인사람들은 별로안좋아할거같고, 소울류 입문으로 하기엔 난이도가 상당히있는게임이다.
애매한 포지션에있어서 부정이많은거같다.

Resumindo o jogo até o momento. Ele é um jogo bom, um SoulsLike bem solido e bom. Gameplay é legal, gráficos muito bonitos, o jogo roda MUITO bem, mas tem problemas que precisam ser resolvidos. 

Tenho a impressão que os devs fizeram o jogo e não jogaram algumas partes, porque tem áreas que são GIGANTES, com MUITOS INIMIGOS, e não tem bastião para curar... Inimigos que simplesmente começam um ataque do outro lado do mundo, aí no momento em que o hit vai te acertar, ele DESLIZA UMA AREA ENORME PRA TE ACERTAR. Isso aí é paia. E o principal, MUITOS CRASHES. Varias vezes que do nada o jogo simplesmente crasha. Por exemplo, acabei de matar um boss aqui no jogo, liberei uma carcaça e o jogo simplesmente crashou............ 

Pelo menos o boss foi contado como derrotado, foi só eu voltar lá e pegar a carcaça de novo, mas isso aí é um problema que tem q ser resolvido o mais rápido possível. Mas recomendo o jogo sim! Não é um jogo de 350 reais, que a maioria das grandes empresas lançam. Se fosse isso, esse jogo não valeria de jeito nenhum, mas o preço é justo! Pode comprar pra jogar, mas tenha em mente esses problemas aí!
GREAT GAME!!!! Combat is smooth. Graphics are amazing. The different areas are interesting and there are so many hidden things to find throughout the world.
Casi le meto un bombazo al monitor con el boss final, por lo demás muy bien, he muerto aproximadamente 340 veces. Experiencia souls completa.
игра классная, в меру сложная, но багов полно, лучше подождать патча

La primera parte del mapa sin problema, lo he explorado a conciencia, y todos los bosses derrotados, pero la segunda parte es una mofada, los enemigos normales ya cuestan y llevo el hacha a +16 y nivel 23. Estoy ahora atascadísimo con el boss príncipe, la maldita polilla y lo dejo a casi nada de vida pero es que si te toca al hoyo. Algún que otro bug me he encontrado, pero mas allá de eso, un juegazo, tenia dudas si pillarlo y menos mal, llevo un vicio bueno.
The best! I love this game!

I say this with some warning: while it is a fantastic upgrade from the original, this one does have some rough spots, clipping, weird sound, and fighting glitches that take me out of the moment. The world is awesome, the fighting feels great, executions are fun, and the leveling and upgrade system feels solid. But it needs a little more time to cook; the devs shouldn't have rushed it out the door. If we like something, we will wait the extra few months it takes to iron out the kinks. This is a plead for all game developers, please don't rush a good thing out the door until it's ready.

Fun game but some of the boss run backs are not fun.
also a lot of cheap "ambushes/traps" or here have fun fighting a group of enemies with ground traps all around you.

Absolutely not rn, a lot of features simply do not work (key character abilities for example), no name enemies that can break guard on two hits (and kill you in as many), enemy attack range is so stupid as well with enemies out right teleporting mid attack animation to ensure their attack is landed and vice versa. 

its absolutely baffling it was released in this state even if we dont consider the game crashing.
Game's good. You should play it.

I’ve really enjoyed Mortal Shell II overall. The combat is satisfying, the atmosphere is great, music was dope, and there’s a lot to like about the game. That said, I think it would benefit from some balance changes starting around the mid-game to make certain builds and encounters feel more fair and consistent (especially the final boss). I’d also love to see more variety in the shells and weapons, since having more options would add even more depth and replayability. Right now it seems speed is king and it gets a little stale after a while. Overall, it’s a solid game with a lot of potential, and I’m looking forward to seeing how it improves. I'll definitely be looking out for a Mortal Shell III.
Yeah. Just buy it. It is good.

所有魂游我都是全收集，也算是硬核老魂玩家了，但这款游戏是唯一让我不想开2周目的，前期确实好玩，后期简直了，怪堆得毫无逻辑，个个千里眼，生怕你死里逃生，BOSS毫无交互，功高血厚不说，红光一个接一个，有些红光还是零帧起手，甚至连着放4.5个红光。做游戏只会填数值吗？中后期除了轮椅，想正常玩，简直就是找屎吃。打完一周目差一个成就，全躯壳的记忆，毫无欲望开二周目的游戏，开了个修改器拿了个白金，到此结束，滚出我电脑
Если из соулс лайка убрать полоску стамины, то станет ли он слэшером? В любом случае, мне дико нравится эта игра!

Some minor performance issues, not terrible but games crashed about 5 times on me in 40 hours of gameplay Inconvenient but not experience breaking for me (devs acknowledged the issues and said they are working on fix). Awesome world design and graphic style. Combat feels great. A lot of customization in the character build that I like. Have 3 defense mechanics to choose from, multiple shells each with a customized skill tree/talents, and just as many weapons to choose from to compliment your build and playstyle. Overall I really enjoy this game.

Так, ну прошел я энтот ваш сосалик без выносливости и могу сказать, что в целом оно было неплохо.
В не которых аспектах игра попукивала и кряхтела, но в целом да, оно съедобно и даже вкусно. Да не, 11 из 10 на кончиках пальцев, но и претензий на это не было.
Имеется у нас сосалик, с упрощенной системой развития(уровень поднимает характеристики в виду здоровья и шанса крита фиксировано и без выбора) и билдами, которые мы собираем на основе 8 тушек-персонажей, 8 оружий ближнего боя и 8 оружий дальнего боя. Дальний бой тут кастрированный, пользоваться им можно, но сложно и по сути не нужно. во все оружие вставляются камешки, которые дают оружию способности (вот камень с зачарованием на молнию, вот камень на прием с подпрыгиванием и ударом по башке супостата, вот камень на еще какую хрень, всего их 70+штук). В целом можно найти билд себе по вкусу и сравнительно весело разносить окружающее. Сравнительно ибо игра неровная, ведь мобы иногда проблемнее босса быть могут, да и боссы неровные, одни нормально сделаны и бить их весело, даже когда отъезжаешь от лещей, а вот в финале уже халтурка, которая больше бесит.
Мир нарисован красиво, кровавенько и довольно необычно.
Музыка вроде как есть, немного отдает под металл, но оно не запоминается особо. Просто музыка, не бесит, но и не восхищает. 
В целом игра являет собой просто добротный сосалик чуть выше среднего как по мне. Огромный рост по сравнению с первой частью. В принципе жду теперь третью часть с дальнейшим развитием идей. Студии добра.

The last zone is one big buggy mess: bosses chain skills without finishing previous animation, hit boxes are close to non existent, summon AI is broken (attacking invisible objects or the ones who are not active in the current fight), bridges are too narrow (you can fall easily while doing skill animation with some shells).

I pretty much agree with the negative reviews here already. The frequent crashes are especially annoying.

So far its been a very fun world to explore and the story seems more unique. Still has some rough bugs that require leaving an area and then returning to fix whatever messed up. The game looks incredible and the finishers are pretty sick. My current big complaint is the lack of any push back from your weapon hits. Most enemies will swing right through a light attack or two, even from larger weapons. This constantly leaves me feeling weaker than some random guy with a knife. I'll for sure be completing the game, but it would be nice to have a little more power behind the swings.

Я вообще не любитель Souls-like (так же как и писать отзывы). От слова совсем. Обычно меня хватает ненадолго: следи за выносливостью, жди, пока персонаж отдышится, перекатись, получи по жопе, повтори.

А тут, увидела графончик и атмосферу решила потестить бету и !внезапно! залипла.

Наверное, главное для меня — здесь НЕТ ВЫНОСЛИВОСТИ. Господи, какое счастье. Можно бегать, уворачиваться и махать мечом без ощущения, что персонаж после трёх ударов сейчас попросит стульчик и стакан водички. При этом игра не превращается в тупой слэшер: если полез жадничать и решил, что «ну ещё один ударчек точно успею» — не успеешь. Получишь пи*ды.

Очень понравилась система оболочек. Они действительно ощущаются по-разному, а не просто «у этого +5 к одной цифре, у другого +5 к другой». Можно носиться по карте как бешеный таракан, а можно взять кого-нибудь пожирнее и хотя бы переживать собственные ошибки. Плюс оружие, тариты, способности — есть что поковырять и подстроить под себя.

Мир тоже затягивает. Постоянно возникает это проклятое: «а что там за углом?» — и вот ты уже полчаса шаришься вообще не там, куда собирался идти. Правда, игра быстро учит подозревать буквально всё. Кувшин? Возможно, взорвётся. Кокон? Возможно тоже взорвётся. Подозрительная хрень с кнопкой «прикоснуться»? Я уже морально готовлюсь ко всему. Пропасть? Мой персонаж иногда смотрит на неё и принимает самостоятельное решение сократить прохождение хД

Боссы очень разные. Перед некоторыми стоишь и думаешь: «ну всё, сейчас меня ра***бут», заходишь — а там какой-то лох. А потом приходит другой красавчик, и спустя десять минут боя он уже почему-то не такой красивый, а просто душный му....дурак.

Игра не идеальная. Иногда хитбоксы вызывают вопросы, некоторые враги умеют дотягиваться до тебя так, будто у них встроен телепорт, местами можно заблудиться нахрен, а баги после релиза тоже встречаются. Но самое главное для меня — даже когда Mortal Shell II меня бесит, мне всё равно хочется вернуться и продолжить.

Для человека, который обычно Souls-like не особо любит, это, наверное, лучший комплимент игре.

Очень неожиданно понравилось.

Кувшины — 0/10.
Игра — рекомендую.

И от**битесь от моего Иконоборца.

Хороший, качественный соулс-лайк.
Жирный плюс за визуальную часть и оптимизацию. Играется красиво и приятно.
Механики боя типичные, из необычного - отсутствие стамины.
Система вооружения и прокачки, к сожалению, побуждает выбрать что-то одно в ранней игре и потом играть этим до конца. Есть способы респекнуть прокачку оружия и оболочек, но лично я ими не пользовался и как получил Проксиму и секиру - так ими и прохожу, т.к. в целом оружие по ощущениям не особо различается между собой по стилю игры.
Музыка и атмосфера - 3/5. Несмотря на отличный визуал, накала и эпика местами как будто не хватает. Музыка хотя и приятная и ненавязчивая, но частенько однообразная. 
После 24 часов  в игре прошел где-то половину контента, но это при том, что залезал в каждую щель и совсем не спешил двигаться по сюжету. Думаю собрать всё оружие и закрыть сюжет.

Probably the most 7/10 game i've played in a while. There's a lot to like about the game but also plenty of negatives that stop it from being just shy of being a great soulslike. I'll start with the positives!

((SPOILERS))

POSITIVES:
The shells are incredibly varied and unique, none of them play the same and all feel useful/powerful to a degree. Not to mention the character designs for the shells are extremely good in my opinion, so unlocking a new shell always felt exciting and special.

The combat is really solid, probably one of the better souls-likes in terms of combat, parrying felt great, attacks felt like they had impact, the riposte animations were stylish and brutal, character abilities flow into the combat really well. Plus plenty of tarstones that change up the playstyle of certain items and weapons leading to a lot of interesting combos.

The weapon variety is also pretty good despite there not being a huge amount of them, Each one was enjoyable to use and had their own depth and tarstone combo's to run, encouraging the player to experiment and try new weapons to find one that fits their build.

The soundtrack is surprisingly good, it's nothing crazy but it really helps set the mood, I'm especially fond of the scholar prince's theme!

The game runs extremely well, and visually looks great!

Okay onto the negatives!

NEGATIVES:
Level design was boring and bland, Very few areas actually looked different from each other. The games world was visually uninteresting and very drab, and not even like a dark souls drab, just an ugly boring drab which made the game appear soulless and dull at times.

Story and worldbuilding were largely uninteresting, Watched all the cutscenes read all the lore i could find, and exhausted every npc's lines and found little reason to care about any of the npc's or the games world (EXCEPT VLAS AND MERRICK THEY'RE GOATED!) All i really got was i had to collect eggs ,send them to heaven and kill "The Foul Passenger". I may have missed something or just not understood it, if so that's entirely on me! But i found the story and lore lacking.

Enemy design and variety could get pretty lacking pretty quickly, they LOVE to spam those worm/snake things, and those crawler guys who ♥♥♥♥ poison at every opportunity, Not to mention those weird spider-like things that charge you or the rolling spiky ball guys. It gets especially bad near the end of the game where they spam the ACTUAL spider enemies over and over again.

The games difficulty is EXTREMELY inconsistent, Some enemies feel unfairly punishing and artificially difficult, like their moveset isn't difficult to manage but one mistake and your entire healthbar is GONE. Where as other enemies that should be stronger feel incredibly easy to deal with. I went through about 65% of the game without many deaths, then i got to the later half and it became artificially difficult as they just reused old enemies but increased their health and damage to ridiculous proportions.

The bosses aren't interesting in the slightest with only TWO exceptions, Most are standard generic "Dude in armor" or "Big ugly monster" Without much done to make them stand out or be memorable. The two exceptions being The Scholar Prince, and The Malborn Offspring, both were incredibly fun and memorable fights. But there are some REALLY bad ones in here such as the Monolith and Zmey, who both just have an ABSURD amount of health and deal a ridiculous amount of damage meaning one mistake and that's 5 minutes wasted.

The whole ending area was boring and underwhelming and actively ruined the final half of the game for me, The final area consists of you slowly slogging through a lot of the stronger enemies in the game for about 15-20 minutes before fighting a boss. Now you repeat that 3 times in total. Not to mention the final boss feels like a let down. You go all this way only for the final boss to be a dragon with a sword and giant balls, with his strongest attack being crushing you with his nuts, And don't get me wrong it got a chuckle out of me when i saw his attacks for the first time, but it felt a little anti-climatic? It's probably on me for expecting a Gwyn, Soul of Cinder or even Nameless Puppet style showdown but i was let down as i probably wouldn't have minded if this boss was placed elsewhere in the game. But It felt more like a meme/joke boss than anything especially when considering the build-up for the fight was MY STEAM LIBARY!

Overall i think it's a decent game with plenty of flaws, it has plenty to like and plenty to hate, The areas it does well it does REALLY well, but the areas it fails in fail HARD. so personally i WOULD recommend it, but only if you're really REALLY into souls-likes and have already played fromsoftwares games or are looking for an alternative to them. It does a good enough job of scratching that souls-like itch for me but doesn't leave me craving more from this specific title.

The original Mortal Shell showed promise, but lacked in scale and polish. To call this an improvement is an understatement. Beyond retaining the title shell mechanic and metal fantasy aesthetic, almost everything has evolved to rival most great modern soulslikes.

Combat feels good, and there's enough unique shells and weapons to satisfy experimentation. Shells now have unique abilities and trees, and all of the ones I tried felt viable, though it can be hard to swap builds due to currency restriction. 

I had a lot of fun exploring the open world. The dungeons you find tend to be quite short but can contain some unique puzzles or areas. 

The scaling of enemies is very inconsistent and the game runs out of variety in the second half, though overall it was quite good. Some enemy attacks have huge gap closers without matching animations that make your spacing feel purposeless, though the game does have strong defensive options. 

I appreciate that it carves it's own style in a crowding genre, though landscapes appear too similar without much detail. The music we got was great, but there's not much of it, and the story mostly passed over my head. 

It has some bugs and gameplay issues that will likely get smoothed out, though nothing gamebreaking for me. It's an impressive sequel and solid action game most will have fun with.

I will start by saying I have played and completed many souls/soulslike games before (DS1-DS3, Bloodborne, Lies of P, Elden Ring etc.). Aesthetically I quite enjoy the world and enemy designs in this game. Mechanically this game is pure torture, riddled with bugs, awful boss encounters, and a myriad of other poor design decisions such as spacing out the bonfire between anywhere from 20-100 enemy encounters in a game where any enemy has the ability to 1-3 shot you if they feel like it. Making a mistake in this game is like getting your teeth pulled with no anesthetic, you will be punished not only by having your health drained incredibly fast but by the egregious runback needed to get back to some areas where you've perished. (i.e. there is a boss where you fight a 2v1 and to get back to this boss you must run up a jump platform, go inside the dungeon, and then ride 2 entire elevators just to get back to the boss. It got to a point where I just didn't even bother continuing with the encounter and proceeded with the rest of the game.) Boss encounters can also get pretty terrible pretty quickly due to the game introducing artificial difficulty where the boss (at least the main gate ones) will just get faster the lower it's health gets, or be able to just cancel chain moves into another with no warning. The Lost Child (pre-nerf) was a prime example of this, during the last 15% or so of it's health bar it would get so fast I would consider it's moveset to be unreactable by a human player, meaning that you basically had to predict what it was going to do next because you have a 1-2 second window to even parry anything all while each of it's hits would instakill you. I did go into this game with a bit of optimism but after playing it to near completion I can thoroughly say I did not have an enjoyable time with it. In fact upon writing this I have not even bothered defeating the final encounter due to just being exhausted with this game and it's terrible design choices. There are some bosses in the last area that feel like no play testing went into them or they just ran out of ideas, resulting in some truly miserable sequences. I probably have a lot more to say about this game (none of it positive). But for now that'll do.

7/10 — A big improvement, but still needs a lot of work

Mortal Shell 2 is a big upgrade compared to the first game. The overall design, the Shell concepts, animations, and combat are all quite good, and there are some genuinely great ideas here.

Unfortunately, the game still has a lot of issues that hold it back.

One of the biggest problems is enemy variety. In many cases, enemies feel like the exact same model with a different texture or color. The non-main bosses are also very disappointing. Most of them are either regular enemies thrown at you in larger numbers or recolored versions of enemies you've already fought.

The questlines are another missed opportunity. Most of them feel pointless because the rewards are either nonexistent or simply not worth the effort. It doesn't feel rewarding to actually complete them.

The enemy and boss attacks are also frustrating at times. For some reason, attacks feel almost magnetic, as if they're designed to hit you regardless of your timing. Even when using Genessa's second form and performing the huge dash, I often felt like attacks would still somehow connect. I still end up getting hit by enemies.

The game also has quite a few bugs, and some of the ones I encountered actually affected my gameplay. There are areas where the distance from the nearest beacon is quite large, so when a bug occurs, you have to repeat a significant portion of the game just to get back to where you were.

Enemy damage also doesn't feel consistent. Sometimes an attack barely hurts you, while other times what feels like the same attack can one-shot you. Some bosses also have hitboxes that don't seem quite right, making certain attacks feel like they hit you when they shouldn't.

Another issue is that some mechanics are reused far too often. What might have been interesting the first few times starts to feel repetitive after a while.

That said, there is definitely a lot to like. The Shell designs and concepts are great, the animations are well done, and the combat has a solid foundation. There are some genuinely good ideas here, and compared to the first Mortal Shell, this is definitely a step forward.

Unfortunately, there are still too many things that need improvement for me to rate it higher.

Overall: 7/10.

First off I would like to say that I loved this game. The art design is BEAUTIFUL, enemy variety is great and the combat feels refreshing and challenging. Huge improvement to the first game and I'd give it a 9 out of 10 personally. I just beat the game last night and would really love to feel like NG+ would be fun, but there's one thing that making me hesitate.

I feel that they are not encouraging build diversity when I cant get all my tarstones to max rank.

If I was able to farm them again in NG+ like the glimpses, I wouldn't mind really, but the fact that by the end of game you can collect 75 tarstones and only get 23 of them to max, and only if you use every single one in the game to at least level 2 and get the few you can to level 3. While the glimpses being forced to get again in NG+ is kind of annoying when you just wanna try all the shells out, at least you do have the option to max all of them out. The tarstone problem HAS to be an oversight because it really is depressing knowing I cant max all of them out. ALOT of the tarstones only get good at level 3 and there are ALOT of tarstones that only effect one weapon and makes it way better or just overall more fun so if you wanted to experience the one weapon with its unique tarstone and also have the infusion you want for it that only effects that one weapon then you already used 2 of your 23 maximum upgrades. If you did this for every weapon and every sidearm, you couldn't, because there are a total of 8 weapons and 8 sidearms, and most of them have a unique tarstone to go with them.  I really hope they fix this because its honestly just hanging dread over my head in NG+ trying to think of basically what I want my last item build to be, because I already maxed out 5 of the stones before it dawned on me that I wasn't getting anymore tarcores in the exploration, and the math wasn't adding up, and then I maxed out the ones I wanted for my spear build and now I only have 12 more available, basically enough to try one more weapon out to its full potential. Even if you have to farm them in NG+, not the best option of course like the glimpses, but at least it would be an option. NG+ doesn't feel worth it knowing I'm still not gonna have everything in the game no matter how many times I play. Please give us a way to max all the tarstones out.

The shortest way to describe the problem with MS2 right now is to say the release feels like a beta, and the beta felt like an initial release.

The beta had problems. It was a bit too easy in places, in others some enemies felt a bit too tanky. But the scaling seemed level and intentional. Also, it was mostly bug free experience for me; and what I did experience were minor graphical glitches. Point being, it needed some tuning. The kinds of issues a few early patches iron out. The beta gave an impression the final product was close, and in great shape.

Flash forward to the actual release, everything has regressed.

Most enemies have had their damage output scaled massively. But for some not at all... or down a bit. There doesn't seem to be any rhyme or reason. Same goes for their health. An optional early game boss swings a giant sword around, and did about 70-80% of my health per swing. A random mook with a pickaxe a little later in the level took 90% of my health.

Bugs are constant. In the UI, in game interactions. I can't think of a single part of the game I [i]haven't[/i] run into an a head scratching bug. Icons flicker on the map, cutscenes have a glitchy letterboxing. I've watched my weapon phase through enemies, and their weapons phase through me. Not common, but it's happened.

I'm not even through the content from the beta and I might call it. I'm barely tolerating what I'm running into already, and other reviews give the impression the early game has excellent polish compared to later parts. It's an unbelievable letdown from what we saw a few months ago.
