[b] I did not play the first one. [/b]
This game is more like the new generation of GOW/Bloodborne than a Elden Ring/Dark Souls style.

TL;DR:
[i] Game has good potential, have a lot of good things, mechanics, etc. However they need to patch this a couple of times to make it a more enjoyable experience. Not only fix bugs, but balance things and make less of a nightmare, it's fine to be a hard game (indeed it's a souls like) but some things just don't make sense. They also need to re-work some things or they might as well delete them because they are useless. Till now I had a lot of fun but I also felt stuck for different reasons. Power scaling NEEDS to be tweaked in both enemies and your own character. IMHO could have more items. [/i]
[b] Overall, game is good, has insane potential, it can be a different grip from the usual dark souls/Elden ring if they continue to make more content, more items, more shells, DLC and/or more games. [/b]

[h3] I have played half the game till this point and my current impressions are [/h3]
[b] The bad first, as I think they are the most important: [/b]
- The consumable mechanics suck, you rarely use them or need them (the leveling consumables is very interesting though). Also there is something that "spawns" a soul to help you, it get's instantly killed by anything that dares looking at it, useless, anything else that "spawns" something to help you is useless.
- (Till now) You get stuck in some mini-bosses/area bosses because of the numbers and nothing else. Given most weapons (till now) did not provide much AOE damage, it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks. You have to dodge and parry 2 big bosses/enemies and is not a fun gameplay because (again till now) the game doesn't give you enough resources to deal with groups of enemies.
- The edges of the game are really annoying to deal with, you will question if you should attack an enemy because he is in the edge and your attack will push you forward out of the edge, sometimes there is a force in this edge that prevents you to drop in your own movement attack, sometimes you simply go flying down the hill
- (Till now) ALL weapons are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slow, which defeats the purpose of the fighting style (which is mostly parrying, timing and "dodging") and it doesn't get fixed with damage, even if have a heavy weapon is not going to cover for that, the stagger is immensely different (which helps a bit, but doesn't seem enough).
- There is a ♥♥♥♥ ton of bugs. Those being: Enemies getting stuck inside walls, you getting stuck in places you shouldn't, you falling from a cliff and not somehow dropping into a rock that did not count as death zone, specific enemies bashing your head and the impact sends you in the sky, enemies sliding up rocks rather than getting hit and bouncing in the wall (or just not going into edges you can't reach), enemies getting invisible and still being in place (only got back to normal after re-starting the checkpoint a few times).
- The fall damage is weird as ♥♥♥♥, if you attack while falling it seems to literally negate all damage you should take, the game doesn't give you enough examples for you to get a grasp of what will kill you, I skipped a whole portion of 2 specific zones because I thought I would die in fall damage, after I figured how to ignore fall damage, I went there explored the area.
- The bear trap sucks, you spend too much time and resources disabling it (and you are ♥♥♥♥♥♥ because usually there is 10 of them in the same place) just because some enemy might push you into it. At least the enemies also trigger it.

[b] The weird stuff I personally did not like and would suggest overhaul/tweaking: [/b]
- Weapon scaling and shell scaling. Both have the same issue of you spending your resources into it without knowing the next ones to come (and how they work), you are left with either being weak and having resources or having to use a weapon/shell you clearly do not want/is not your playstyle. The scaling of weapons is also too simple, they all scale the same (I don't know about base stats) and they don't seem to have any special thing, is just a different move set/speed/stats (some stagger more than others).
- Shell scaling is also the same as above, they are really great mechanic, everything around it is hell of fun, but again, if you spend it early on into something you are ♥♥♥♥♥♥, you need to continue using it forever because you are never going to get enough resources to swap them and not leveling them is capping your ability to deal with enemies.
- On the above 2 again. I'm into the point to accept I'm going to be always a piece of paper and get one tapped. Because I need to know all shells before spending all resources into one single path.
- The amount of checkpoints and how you have no idea when the next one is close. You basically have to start an area and look around with your aim far away to find the next one, go grab the "checkpoint" and then start cleaning the area and exploring. The game literally punishes you for cleaning areas entirely and rewards you for speed running past all enemies (which has to do with the healing mechanics as well and the number of enemies making 10x harder to do anything)
- Needs a bit of performance balancing. I have a absurdly exaggerated hardware and I'm playing 60~90 FPS raw dog (no upscaling or DLSS, because they all make the graphics buggy, no news there). This game looks like Unreal engine slop and I dislike the ♥♥♥♥ out of it because of things like that.

[b] The stuff that is good (some could still get a tweaking): [/b]
- Map/level design
- Shells, their skills, the abilities you can use, the different kind of parries, many good mechanics in this game.
- Music design and it's timing (I personally would put a ♥♥♥♥ ton more, it really get's you going). The same for when you get in new areas and they take the camera out of you to show you the map while you continue moving.
- Enemies design also look hell of good (till now).
- A lot of mechanics are creative and enjoyable. Corruption, Dungeons, teleporting, passive stones, ranged weapons, how you use skills/ranged weapons/recharge them.
- Story line looks good till now (some things feel a bit lazy though till now).

[b] The stuff it needs a little tweak and it will be perfect: [/b]
- The camera position sucks in closed spaces. You get lost on what the ♥♥♥♥ you were doing because it zooms in any time you go trough a door.
- A few mechanics are totally counter productive, you get stacking stuff in a shell that resets when you rest but then you can't continue playing because healing sucks ass, consumables are useless and you never know when you are gonna be surprised by an area boss that will 2 tap you.
- Fighting mechanic needs some tweaking with the attack animations, everything is dead ass slow (till now, might change my mind when I get faster weapons if they are any). The direction of attacks also needs tweaking and target lock, they are kind of buggy and are often not correctly pointing to the direction of enemies, you are often in diagonal with enemies rather than straight into them.

[b] Specific things that I HATED (till now): [/b]
- There is a area with a boss that you already defeated, however, there are 2 of them. Is impossible to pass that (optional) area. You can't parry 2 at the same time, it doesn't seem right, the game punishes the ♥♥♥♥ out of you whenever there more than 1 enemy alive in front of you and news flash you can't instantly kill 1 those 2 bosses.
- Not having even a recommended direction of where to start, which forced me to get beaten to death a billion times for skipping an entire area.

This game is so good. the exploration is fun, the combat is sick, and the different shells and weapons you have access to are all so cool. Then you get to the latter half of the game and everything falls apart. You start to notice enemies magnetizing to you from miles away when doing their attacks and every little fodder enemy deals a ton of damage while also attacking super fast and being unstaggerable even with the heaviest weapons. 

There are a ton of tiny little annoyances that add up as well. For example, when you are on a ledge and trying to get away from a swarm of enemies, you cannot fall off the edge while dodging. One might say that's a good thing since you don't want to dodge off of an edge, but I strongly believe they don't care about that, because on many occasions I have attacked an enemy near a ledge and fallen off to my death because my attack animation launches me forward 8 feet, and even shoves me through the enemy I was attacking. It's not impossible to work around with luring enemies, but I really dislike the inattention to detail and inconsistency.

Regarding minor annoyances, I think the loot you get around the world is very lame. The tar stones specifically are underwhelming in most cases. A lot of the stones I was able to find had the least interesting effects, like 'if an enemy dies to a sidearm attack, increase your damage output by 20% for 10 seconds'. Fine, not every piece of loot needs to be good, and the melee weapons and shells are what I had a ton of fun finding anyway - but what adds insult to injury is the fact that a lot of the sidearms are so painfully weak that they aren't even worth using in the first place.

The absolute most egregious thing that encapsulates all of my problems is the monolith enemy at the end of the game. it has stupid damage attacks that launch at you from what would be out of reach, it has attacks that aren't telegraphed with hitboxes that don't make sense, and it deals way too much damage even on the standard game difficulty. I love a challenge, and this game has plenty of fun challenges, but things like this are not challenging, they are annoying and ultimately make me regret buying this game. I hope they fix these issues, because it's ridiculous and makes me wonder if they even had anyone play test the last part of the game.

I hope it gets fixed, because this game could be very amazing if it maintained the quality displayed at the start.

Its a great game that tries really hard not to be, because of very bad choices and lack of the developer playing the game and watching how basic stuff really frustrates whoever is playing.
- Can't jump, so imediatly you know that this game with a beatiful world will barely have any kind of exploration. The game exploration is just sightseeing.
- Each character has a skill, some of them are awful just because after you use it your character takes more time to pick up his weapon again than the time it takes for him to use the skill. So you can't really use it while fightning multiple enemies.
- Enemies kinda "Snap" to you when they attack, so even you zigzag left/right around walls, their jump will just follow you like a heatseaking missile. You will see they slide around just so they can catch you. That means, you are forced to play the way the game dev wanted: Its all about timing, you must either Dodge at the right time, or parry at the right time. You can't learn the enemy moveset and walk around it while you hit it.
- They made it so that target locking is 90% necessary (and I dislike targetlocking, you can't move to where you want while you do the actions you want), but sometimes it will just screw with you. (Playing on keyboard and mouse) You can't reliably control your character while attacking, when you attack, you character moves waaaay to forward, and you can't really steer in a way that you will hit your attacks. Than you must use the targetlock system, that will just jump to another target far away for no reason, and make you miss the attacks anyway. There is 1 boss that your target lock will just lock into INANIMATE OBJECTS and make you miss your attacks, parrys and Dodges because you are facing the wrong way.
Also, you have no cameramovement at all when target locking, and if you are with your back against a wall your camera goes over your head and you just can't see your character, or enemies around, so you are prety much dead, since you can't see what the hell is happening.
-Some bugs here and there. You get stuck in the walls, enemies get stuck in the walls. Cluster of enemies attacking will be a mess, making them climb over 1 another.

I feel like they made a great game, and then thougth "Wait a second, we forgot to ♥♥♥♥ it up!", thats why its a thumbs down. Everything bad in the game infuriates you in a way the good things just feel like its a waste of potential.

An unbelievable improvement compared to the first title in every possible way.

Combat feels great and is punchy, animations and different types of deflect all felt really good. I love how focused every shell feels. What I think needs improvement is enemy tracking, its ridiculous how magnetic some specific enemy attacks may feel. 

Exploration was surprisingly fun and rewarding, level design was also great. Felt like zones tied together into an open world map, so it had the best of both worlds. Dungeons were short and quick, always a blast.   Some extra checkpoint system close to dungeon would be a great addition.

Sound design and music were both great, parry sounds snappy and impact sounds are also well done.

Side bosses were average and below average most of the time. A lot of times it consisted of buffed mobs,  gank fights or there is one side boss that is repeated throughout the game. Nothing challenging here but it was fun.

Main bosses are where the games shines, most of them are really well done. There is one big exception, one fight is really horrible as per my opinion. I wont spoil which one. But overall, really good.

Story-wise I did not pay much attention so, no comment there.

I can definitely recommend this one,  I was not bored, combat is fun and there are not many frustrations except one-two fights, enemy tracking and maybe runbacks.

Pros: Great graphics and an interesting visual design. That's pretty much it at the moment.

Cons:

Projectiles fired from sidearms often fly anywhere but toward the target. This also applies to some character abilities, which becomes extremely frustrating and needs to be fixed.
About 80% of enemy attacks are poorly telegraphed, so they can sometimes be nearly impossible to deflect. For instance, an enemy starts winding up an attack, and 0.01 seconds later, it lands right in the character's face. Is it possible to react to? Yes. Is it fun or challenging? No. It just feels unfair because it becomes dependent on luck and whether the game decides to register your input. Overall, this inconsistency makes the combat flow feel bad and difficult to understand.
Bosses are the worst part of the game. They are not fun to fight at all for the reasons described above. Their attacks feel very clunky, and some can hit you even when you are far away, thanks to the game's "great hitboxes." Fighting them feels like overcoming theirs stupid and undeveloped move sets instead of getting in a combat flow.

Overall, this game is unfinished and will need 1-2 months to get the it's beta's state to become relatively enjoyable. I would not recommend to buy this  game at the moment and RIP to all of those people who bought the early accesses (including myself) and ruined their first impression and such an expected game.

At first this game looked great but every few hours, every new boss or enemy type made issue more and more apparent.
They nailed the visuals, creativity and weirdness of the world, story was something interesting too, and performance is solid.
But they completely dropped the ball at gameplay and combat. There are just a few problems but they are significant enough to ruin the experience:
1. Diving/teleporting attacks - one of the greates sins of souls-likes where enemies would move a short distance after starting the swing towards the player during the actual attack. Well here this distance is not short at all, if you try to sprint away from some enemies after they started their combo - they will get you no matter what. And grab attacks will just teleport them on top of you no matter the distance. This significantly reduces importance of positioning, and coupled with missing concept of stamina it basically turns a lot of fights into a glorified rhythm game.
2. No scaling on riposte damage - all those cool finisher animations you are rewarded with after timing parries, they do less damage than a normal weapon attack, starting around midgame, because they are not done with weapons and hence weapon upgrades do nothing for it.
3. Beacon (bonfire) positions in open world - these are either rare or placed so unevenly that you'll be exploring without healing flasks most of the time and have to either run back to previous checkpoints constantly or use something else for healing. It basically makes one of the shells a requirement to explore the world.
Overall I'm mixed on this game and all these issues can easily be fixed in following months if devs are willing. If that happens I might try NG+ with the hard mode and update the review.

Ngl the game has a good core, could become a 7.5 / 10 for me and I think I will revisit it at a later date for a NG+ run with other shells (if they get fixed, like Genessa), but the longer I play the more annoying this game gets. There are so many things that are making this, not a challenging or hard, but a tedious experience, but those things can luckily be fixed and the devs have spoken up about some of them already, so maybe they will iron the annoyances out. The things that take this game from a solid 7.5 action souls-like to a 5 for me:

1. Balance is all over the place. For a good portion of the game enemies 2 shotted me. Which, ideally, does not happen when you manage to dodge and or parry well enough, but you get ganked constantly. Several of your moves, like Tiel's Shadowstrike or the execution after an enemy breaks, leave you animation locked after you finish them for a good 0,5 - 1 second, where you can and will get hit, which is just so annoying. Let me move after I did the action. Enemies are bunched up so often and have a stupid large aggro range (which in and of itself is an annoyance), that this became a problem for me.

2. Weirdly enough, Bosses are way to easy compared to the random trash out in the world. With the exception of one of the three main bosses in the first half of the game I have not needed more than 1-3 tries for most of them, with a first try finishing most of them. Tough mobs are fine, but I have legit died more to the most basic foot soldiers then to main bosses.

3. Enemies stick to you like you got a magnet up your behind. If you think some of the Souls enemies have strong magnetization then you are in for a surprise. Some of them pull absolute ankle breaking moves to make sure they will direct their combo moves directly into your face or back despite you doing your best to roll or create space otherwise. Sometimes enemies teleport a good few meters to hit you, insane.

4. The world is really pretty. Very generic fantasy like and more like a theme park ride than a world that feels very immersive with internal logic why places are where they are and alive, but I don't really care that much about this. What I do care about is, is that it is boring to explore. Besides the same 8 stat items  (like fire protection, ice protection etc.), which you each really only need at one point in the game if at all, there is not much to find other than Tarstones (which give you certain stats for your weapons, but you will be set a certain point as you can't level all of them, so finding new ones isn't really exciting after a while) and the Shells/Weapons. That sounds like quite a lot but it really isn't. You will run around an open world with a very labyrinthian design (not meant as a detriment, but it really can be sometimes) and find not a whole bunch of interesting things. This is the point that can't really be fixed anymore but the combat is fun enough that it isn't that much of a problem.

In the end I feel like it is or will be a fine game, but in it's current state the annoyances and strange balancing choices are really grinding my gears. Currently I don't recommend the game.

This one is unfortunately a game of two halves. I will be very non-descript so nothing is spoiled. 

The first half covering the northern regions is a solid 9/10 for me. Graphics, atmosphere and enemy design were stellar. I spent a good 20 hours there just seeing what I encountered, exploring the optional dungeons and finding shells to try out. 

Bosses were well designed from an artistic and gameplay perspective with some brutal gory finishers thrown in. 

Some of the enemies you'll encounter in the field and in dungeons are disgusting. I mean that in the best way possible. They'd be at home in any horror game. Great stuff. Well done to the designers. 

I did roll my eyes a bit when even the most basic mobs all seemed to use 5-7 hit frantic combos while pivoting on the spot and lunging several metres to reach me, but it was bearable because the story and environment were very fun to explore. F*** the torch guys. This did force me to perfect parrying though, which ended up being a lot of fun. 

Performance is fantastic across the board. 120fps with DLSS quality. Very few stutters, with only minor ones when going between large areas. Sharp visuals with no aliasing. Fantastic lighting and effects, with sparks and blood flying everywhere. Same goes for the sound design. 

The reason the northern region is not a 10/10 is because of the combos with weird delays in the attack animations. I just don't like this, sorry devs. It's not challenging and it's just annoying in my opinion. A rabid beast would not craftily freeze before attacking, then turn the other way and swing. 

There is also a lack of 'bonfires' and run backs have returned. Elden Ring fixed this with the stakes of Marika. However, these are minor problems in my opinion. 

Now for the second half. I did not like it anywhere near as much as the first. A major issue came up here, which is levelling up just did not seem to have much of an effect on the gameplay. Damage output seemed to be the same as 10 hours earlier, even with a high level weapon. 

It seemed like I had encountered an artificial difficulty spike, exasperated by a few new enemies with unclear animations. Sometimes they seemed to teleport into an attack and other times they were obscured by effects. Eventually, I got the timing down for parrying everything but wow... it was not fun.  

I ended up speeding through the final 10 hours or so just to get it finished. The final two bosses were a nightmare and I almost cheated. The final boss' un-blockable attack was particularly grievous and it spammed the s*** out of it. 

It was a shame, because the environment was just as interesting as in the first half and the story of each shell started to get more interesting with each level up. Enemies started to get a bit samey after a point, with the old 'change the colour' refresh for certain enemies starting to creep in. 

Should you buy? That would be a tentative yes if you like souls-likes and I am sure many high skill players will breeze through with few of the problems I had. But if you're at my skill level (definitely not a prodigy), I'd wait for another balancing patch or two. 

If you absolutely must play it now, I'd advise you take your time in the first half and explore everything. Devs are proving responsive and have already patched the difficulty to be more like the beta (google that one...), so I don't think it'll take them long. They'll hopefully have it sorted by the time you make it to Mammon.

Uno de los mejores Soulslike que existen. El diseño de niveles, el combate, el sistema de cáscaras, la ambientación y como está todo tejido forman un juegazo de los que se recuerdan.


Pros:

- Diseño de Niveles, muy inspirado en Dark Souls 1, son los 2 mejores que existen. Se siente mucha libertad en elegir tu camino y cuenta también con mazmorras tipo Elden Ring.

- Combate, partes con un arma principal y otra auxiliar, se siente fluido y muy satisfactorio, gran sistema de parrys personalizables con los llamados sellos.

- Ambientación, es muy inmersivo y hace un gran trabajo en transmitirte la historia y una atmósfera oscura.

- Historia/Lore, creo que la premisa es muy buena y cumple con creces. Cada cáscara tiene su historia que puedes revivir a medida que subes su vínculo.

- Jugabilidad, uno de los mejores apartados del juego, te permite elegir cáscaras que cada una tiene su propia mecánica de jugabilidad, además de asignar puntos a esas cáscaras para adaptarla a lo que quieres hacer.

- Progresión, aunque es rígido a la hora de subir de nivel, no te deja asignar puntos en ese apartado, se centra más en el desarrollo de las cáscaras y es ahí donde radica su originalidad y donde pone el foco, se siente fresco y diferente.

- Dificultad, es un desafío para quienes llevan jugado mucho tiempo estos juegos y se agradece. Empieza fuerte (como el Dark Souls 1) pero en pocas horas ya te habrás acostumbrado.

- Sonido, cumple muy bien y añaden mucho a la inmersión del título.

- Variedad, el juego tiene muchas mecánicas de puzles y otros modos que hacen que la experiencia sea fresca y no resulte aburrida.


Cons:

- Bosses, aunque muchos me han gustado, si que se nota que algunos de ellos no están a la altura de otros títulos similares, tienen animaciones poco fluidas y pocos patrones. 

- Bugs, tiene algunos fallos que quedan por pulir y pueden hacer que mueras por esto.

- Checkpoints, el juego te hace correr de vuelta a los sitios donde has muerto aunque sea un boss, algo donde nos podrían haber ahorrado tiempo.


En definitiva un juego imperdible para los amantes del género y que a mi gusto personal es fácilmente uno de los mejores que hay a día de hoy

I had a lot of fun playing this, but the severity of the flaws and poor design choices make it difficult for me to recommend.

The game has very satisfying visceral combat. It has a great loop of building energy by dealing melee damage, and then choosing how you spend the energy: ranged attacks, character abilities, weapon abilities, etc. You have infinite stamina and no concept of carry weight. Falling damage can be negated by performing a plunging attack. The combat and movement feels very free and unlimited.

The balance of the game feels all over the place. Some enemies will kill you in one or two hits with a basic claw attack, command grabs have extreme tracking, and chasing attacks have so much distance that you can't outrun enemies if you want to disengage. I felt that some of the bosses had way too much HP, but they may have been balanced around having the right equipment setup to maximize your damage. Many of the enemies or bosses rely on spamming rapid attacks which feel impossible to dodge entirely. This may be a trade-off to having unlimited dodge stamina, but can feel unfair if you're not used to it.

The game is an open world game where you use a map screen to find your way around. The map is broken into areas which only show fog until you collect their corresponding map fragment. Throughout the game there are many instanced areas like dungeons. When you go inside a dungeon, the map no longer functions. For smaller dungeons, this is fine, but there are several mandatory areas which function as an instance, but are large, non-linear areas that can be very confusing to navigate without a map.

The fast travel menu is one of the worst designed parts of the game. You can't move the cursor on the map and click where you want to go. Instead, you have a list of tabs, in a seemingly random order, which have a list of rest points under them. There are no pictures available, so you have to remind yourself to check the name of every rest point you visit and commit it to memory so you can remember which one to warp back to. When hovering a rest point, it shows where it is on a map, but for any of the warp points inside the gates, it only shows the gate's location itself on the map.

If you die in a dungeon, there is no option to respawn at the entrance, or nearby. You have to run all the way back from the last rest point you were at. This can be not only tedious, but difficult because of enemies being faster than the player with lunging attacks.

The game features "tarstones": equippable items that augment your stats or attacks. It is one of the best features of the game which gives you build variety and customization. The tarstones you have equipped gain experience and level up. You need to bring them to a blacksmith and spend materials to upgrade them. This is fine, but one of the required materials can only be obtained by leveling other tarstones beyond their initial level. This forces you to remove the tarstones you enjoy, and equip unleveled ones to farm them for these materials.

[b]Other Pain Points[/b]
[list]
[*]Some actions like using abilities or being knocked down will force an unhelpful camera angle, and not allow you to readjust it in the process.
[*]Many scenic objects like wooden props have full collisions but cannot be broken, allowing for the player to become stuck mid-combat.
[*]Missing basic quality-of-life features like being able to decrement a numerical input to wrap to its maximum value.
[/list]

I'm going to get laughed at by "hardcore" gamers, but I don't really care.  I am not having a good time. 

I'm not a big souls-like person, I don't have extensive experience in the genre.  I got 100% in Elden Ring and finished the expansion.  I got 100% in Nightreign and did the DLC.  I've beaten Dark Souls 3, am close to beating Dark Souls 2, and that's about it.  Most other souls-likes I dropped part way through or never touched at all.  

I went into this one somewhat hopeful that I would have a good time.  And I think it genuinely has so much to offer.  However two things have sucked all the fun out of this game for me...

First is that the distance between beacons (this game's bonfire equivalent) is absurd.  It's frustrating having to go back through that much stuff after each death.  And I am far from alone in this complaint.  I don't want to bump into one every 50 feet, but there is almost none.  And you don't respawn at dungeons either.

The other complaint is the amount of nonsense that one shots you.  And I don't just mean enemy attacks (plenty of which do).  I mean walking into a room and finding out there is a giant boulder waiting to be dropped on your head with no warning.  Walking over a bridge only to be immediately swept off of it.  Walking into a room with explosives hidden right around the corner and a guy waiting to shoot them.  

These two things have been so extremely noticeable just within the first few hours, that I have zero desire to continue.  I am anticipating that this will be the "theme" of this game and I don't want to spend 30 hours dealing with this.  It's not enjoyable for me.  I am not having a good time, and if what I said sounds like a problem for you I would avoid purchasing.  Proxima's BBL will not carry this game for you.

If those things don't sound like a problem for you then you might love Mortal Shell 2.  The combat is satisfying (at least so far).  Executions are cool.  The shells and tarstones are unique.  The aesthetic is appealing.  It runs incredibly smoothly, kind of shocked it's UE5.  But all of that is weighed down too much for me by what I dislike.

Like I said, it has a lot to offer, it's just not for me.  Refunded.

I am enjoying this game so far, with some notes on what i think would make it even better, and maybe a couple gripes as is par for the course for me lol.

Firstly, what a marked step up from the first game in terms of quality. It doesn't feel bad to play in the slightest. It also doesn't suffer from that "unfinished" thought sort of vibe the way the first game did.

Your character moves fast and as there's no stamina you are not punished for sprinting everywhere - that's a major plus from me. I do not need to be stamina managing my jogging out of combat.
Where combat loses me are the attacks that can barely be seen, let alone responded to. Some of them are much too fast ([spoiler]I'm talking that giant crab looking thing just before the golden door towards Magdalena's area [/spoiler]), and there's more than a little bit of unparryable attack spam that can make commitment to a choice feel a little rough sometimes. Be aware that enemies have at least 3 hits worth of poise before they will stumble (and some have even more), so you can't just mow through mobs the way you might want.

Your weapons attack with various amounts of delay that takes some getting used to, but it feels more dialed in than the first game.
Your fastest weapon is about the same speed as a dark souls broad/short sword, and has about the same attack strength as the dagger lmao. Again, be mindful that enemies are quite a bit spongier than Dark Souls or Elden ring until you get some upgrades in.
You have 4 modes of parrying, with one of them being akin to an "easy mode" that disables achievements. The others are the Harden mechanic from the first game (which i didn't vibe with but have seen it used well), a perfect block system which feels balanced and fair, and then a slightly delayed parry that does advanced stagger damage (it's closer to a Dark souls shield parry with a bit of a wonky timing but that adds to the challenge). Having options is good, the devs really thought about who might want what and somehow managed to balance the entire game around these approaches. Nuts honestly.

As for music, while i don't think i can tell the boss themes apart, the guitar riffs you hear around the game are excellent. Some with your lute, some from characters in the world, and an intro that's genuinely cool if you're a bit of a geek for music like i sometimes get. Loved the way it transitions and the rain? Ah it's a vibe.
The rest is ambient or there isn't any, which is fine. Again, they know the games they're taking inspiration from.

The game walks a fine line between challenging and spammy with enemies, and i think it balances it fairly well. Mitigating the potential frustration there is that there's always usually a couple of enemies who will start attacking one another if they catch a stray swing. I think that's fun and adds a bit of consideration to encounters. When there aren't distractions though, enemies have a vision radius of a few hundred kilometres, so expect to be followed the moment you're seen lol.

My one gripe with the onboarding is that it doesn't really feel like anything is explained to you. Why you're doing what you do, where to go first, what Mether's pulse is or even how to heal - or even something in the menus to read all this basic information. Of course you learn by doing, but maybe a little tutorials section just in case you miss something might be a good consideration for future players. If Dark Souls never explicitly told me what an Estus flask was, i'd have had the same gripe too. It's not a major one though.

All in all, i'll see how it goes when i beat the first half(?) of the world and continue on from there. So far so good!

I wish if steam had a "mixed" review because that's how i felt about this game. It was an overall 6.5/10 experience. 

[b]The Good[/b]
-Visually, I think this game looks great. One of the best looking games released this year.
-Shells are cool. Each felt unique and different. 
-Main bosses were cool for the most part (Until the final boss, he sucks)

[b]The Bad[/b]
-Enemy variety is very lacking, which is my main complaint about this game. You literary fight the same enemies u see at the first few hours of the game till the end. 
-A lot Mini bosses are just re-skinned enemies you fought before.
-Lack of beacons in some areas makes exploring feel tedious rather than fun.

24/08/2026: As of now I am well into the endgame (Only final boss that I haven't reached yet) and I think I will write my review now. So the game is fine for first 70%. 

The difficulty spike in mid-late game is nothing new (Elden Ring - Mountaintops of the Giants), but overall I think the difficulty is fine, even too easy in the mid-game. Late game difficulty however is... something it's all over the place if you have solid build you dunk SO hard on enemies and they kill you fast if you make a mistake - fair, but without a strong build you might get frustrated with getting oneshoted non-stop (Tried to build a fun Genessa build and soon realized that her stray death prevention is fake, it's either bugged or has no grace period and multihits just kill you anyway, which is lame for such a long animation ability). 

Enemy density is acceptable: feels poor in the last few hours of the game, but reusing enemies is nothing new. 

Combat: Feels good and you can get into flow of it, though it is not as different for me as it might be to someone who play only Fromsoft titles, Tarstones are fine concept and interesting way of reworking tired rings/charms systems and add weapon abilities and infusions to it. 

Now the big thing: No stamina bar... eh I was worried about it and I think I was right, to combat Infinite attacks and dodge and parry spam from players enemies are highly aggressive (again fair), but positioning got hit with strays. Enemies cover a lot of distance with their attacks and tracking is very crazy, using smart positioning to your advantage is very limited and I found that some weapons have trouble hitting downwards on stairs or ramps while in lock-on.

Bugs: In first half of the game - minor, nearly non, in second half well I've fallen at least 7-8 times under the map, got staggered into wall and clipped through it, "die", but not really and could walk until I cleansed the Ova and died, died being in cutscene and lost Gloom and probably quite important bit of lore. Which is annoying, but not surprising for new games. BUT I don't understand how that went through QC mandatory boss [spoiler] The Monolith [/spoiler] is so buggy that I chose on a whim to show my friend the buggines of it and in a first run it's AI was broken and it just was walking into a wall. EVERY RUN (+-5-7 didn't count the tries) had a bug from detaching lasers through lasers staying on forever in the air besides it to literally not give a ♥♥♥♥ about the player for first 20s, again not gamebreaking, but it shows lack of polish to later half of this game. From what I heard the last boss is bugged too and doesn't allow you to attack if you have one of the passive items equipped, though I did not reach it so I don't know for sure YET. 

Story: It's either very laconic or I just didn't focus on it (though I like lore and stories and watched 1st game lore so I grasp the basic concepts), so I just don't know what to think about it, it feels lacking? Not in concepts or ideas, but delivery, Soulslikes have a very subtle way of exposing players to the world and story, but here it might be too vague? But I don't hold it against the game, at least not yet, maybe after playing some more I will change my opinion (I feel like bits of story are disconnected from each other). 

Performance is very good and game looks good - that's all. 

Overall I want to like the game, but clear lack of polish for last 30-40% of the game together with bugs soured my view of the game. After few patches I will probably change the review to positive. Sorry for wall of text.

Mortal Shell 2 is an entertaining souls-like that deviates from the standard formula in some interesting ways. The developers made a few intentional decisions to omit certain elements which I think really helps streamline the action, but it does sacrifice some strategy and character customization in the process (for example there's no stamina bar to keep in check and leveling up your stats is basically automated). The combat is clearly the focus here and feels really satisfying. The difficulty curve drops a lot mid to late game (with the exception of 2 endgame bosses), so take that as you will. 

Exploration is decent - the open world was fun to explore, but don't expect anything on Elden Ring's level. I did get a little bored with the numerous, repeating dungeons - some of which had decent designs, but most were lackluster and felt a bit cookie cutter. The graphics and aesthetics are great, but I wish there was more lore to explain the creepy, bizarre world. 

NPCs are disappointingly bland, and there are maybe 3 or 4 questlines that are totally linear. I'll admit, though, it was refreshing not having to worry about screwing up some convoluted NPC questline like I'm guilty of doing in basically every From Software title. 

Overall, Mortal Shell 2 still kept me highly entertained for 30+ hours. I'd recommend it if you're looking for an action packed souls-like with fantastic combat and minimal strategy/customization.

tl;dr: Not an amazing or even great game, but solid and passable--like an Elden Ring that leans more heavily on the ARPG aspect than souls-like elements. Solid gameplay loop (with boss timings feeling reminiscent of Khazan and Stellar Blade guard rhythms) but enemy behavior and level design are a massive drag to the experience. Music feels forgettably nonexistent, The RPG aspect (equipment and "classes") boasts solid build variation. 

Difficulty--as far as bosses go, they are much more forgiving compared to what is expected from purer souls-like experiences. Perfect guard and parry windows are extremely lenient--most attacks come out quickly and in short bursts, although there are a handful of hour-long wind-up attacks and/or boss command grabs. As a minor consequence, Night Mode is more or less the same experience; at worst, bosses will be tankier and can one-shot, but they are other otherwise the same experience.

Outside of the bosses, the real challenge comes from having to deal with the trash (and the environment, at times) standing in the way to the next boss. For the most part, enemies all have an extremely, extremely powerful "magnet" that pulls their attacks into you from the other side of the area you tried to leave them behind at, in such a way that purely sprinting is totally ineffective at avoiding their attacks. There is no real safe way of dealing with them--they have practically infinite poise to your lack thereof, and you will generally never become powerful enough to kill them with reliable consistency.

Level design--the overworld really feels like a re-interpretation of Elden Ring, complete with the occasional dungeon rewarding some neat trinket or weapon. On the other hand, the world feels like a massive chore to traverse--the verticality is completely handled by the environment (no jumping whatsoever), and fast travel points are placed at inconvenient locations relative to each other. There are a handful of NPCs to interact with in the overworld, but there is almost no incentive to go out and find them outside of just seeing them.

The dungeons are more or less 90% identical--sometimes they have some extra gimmick or minor puzzle to resolve, but for the most part, they are all near-linear paths starting from an elevator. Considering the dungeons all "load" on entrance, I'm not sure why they all have to have the elevator.

Music--honestly, the best I can vaguely recall is the main motif and maybe how it is reused for each boss fight? If the game truly had no music for its entirety outside of boss segments, I would totally believe it.

RPG systems--actually very fun. I found the Axatana immediately after the tutorial and stuck with it the entire game. The tarstone system has nice customization gimmicks, but I wish the more universal type effects (i.e. element/ailment infusions, most of the projectile tarstones) were available to all weapons instead of specific ones. Nevertheless, the cumulative variety of customization through Shells, equipment, and tarstones was the main reason why I wanted to play more of the game after trying the demo.

I would recommend playing the demo--it is long enough and covers a wide enough breadth to get a solid idea of what this game feels like.

Soft wishlist of features: a screen to show actual stats (i.e. effective critical hit chance, ailment resistances, estimated damage per swing, etc.), reduced EXP requirements for tarstone upgrades, Glimpses not tied to Shell Memory scenes (or Glimpses being resetable).

TLDR: More frustrating than fun, would wait 4-6 months for updates before purchasing.

On one hand, the game is enjoyable in bursts, and the devs have really designed some good systems:
- PP items, makes dealing with hoards of consumables so much easier
- Shells are unique and lead to fun customizations for a build
- Tarstones are pretty cool and really let you customize weapons
- Combat itself is fun, and through the seal system you can have 3 types of parry/block .

On the other hand, all of this just get countered by a constant stream of frustrations and poor design choices:
- Glimpses are limited per playthrough. I am somoene who only really does 1 play through, so I either save my glimpses until I find a shell I want to play or I am stuck with proxima/tiel and fully upgrading them. This just leads people to alt tab and google information about all shells and then selecting the ones they want the most. Completley breaks the fun and unique shell designs they actually came up with.

- Tarstones upgrade cost to lvl 3 is just stupid. You need a resource that is only obtained by leveling tarstones to +2/+3, which means its limited. This does not even reset at NG+. Overall they should add in a smelt function similair to weapons

- Enemy attacks lock on and cause enemies to appear teleporting/full 180 rotations just to hit you. Feels cheap and frustrating to play around
- Enemies respawning without touching a beacon. Unsure if this is due to doing a dungeon, exploring for to long, distance from enemies, etc. But nothing is more frustrating than clearing an area and heading back to a beacon only to be killed because an enemy already slain somehow respawned.
- Lack of beacons/respawn points. This is just frustrating when paired
- Ripostes just do no damage due to lack of scaling. Feels like ♥♥♥♥ when you parry/perfect block and get a juicy riposte only to see the enemy take less damage than 2-3 light hits.

- These above items then get even worse when there are infrequent beacons. Turns annoying/cheap deaths into real frustration when you have to run 3-5 minutes back to where you are. Could add something like dungeon entrances are respawn points, would allow for more respawn points when exploring and no need to have an incredibly long run back if you die in a dungeon when exploring.

Overall the good parts of the game are constantly interrupted by frustrations and lessen enjoyment. I put the game down after the 3rd tower cleared. I would rather come back in 6 months to 1  year and play either with fixes the development team made or mods than resolve issues.

I don't regret purchasing the title, however I cannot recommend people buy the game in its current state. Just enjoy all the September releases and check back around December steam sale time.

Fantastic game overall, with some caveats that I hope the devs will address without much delay:

-Some of the hitboxes for specific boss fights are a little ridiculous, especially in the late game. Specifically the end area with the very last four bosses, with the most egregious being the very last boss.  NOTE: Hexapod too. Dude, come the ♥♥♥♥ on. I should not die behind the boss when there's nothing hitting anywhere near me.

-specific essential items for the very last boss (devs know the one I'm talking about) need to be alluded to somehow. The need for this item is not communicated whatsoever, and it is essential. 

-at least two of the last couple bosses (ESPECIALLY the last boss) need to have the HP DRASTICALLY reduced. It's difficult for the sake of being difficult, and as a VERY seasoned vet to this genre, it feels terrible. 

-Upgrade items for weapons need to be a rare drop on endgame enemies. This shouldn't even be a question. The upgrade system itself is fine, but our options in the late game are FAR too limited. I shouldn't be forced to smelt my main weapon just to upgrade another. That or double the amount of these found in-game. Preferably just make thoracite drop. That would be the ideal option, here.

Some positive feedback:

- the fighting system in this game in general is *chef's kiss*. It looks and feels fantastic on the whole. I'm really excited for new game plus and future DLC content. That said PLEASE spend adequate time polishing this prior to release. The endgame bosses do make me just a little bit hesitant. 

- the design of characters, tone and settings of the game are perfect. It conveys the feel of the world very well and has it's own unique flavor. This is a huge achievement, and it should be praised. 

-each shell is it's own extremely unique playstyle, and most are viable in their own right. Again, huge achievement here. I'm really looking forward to additional shells in the future. Based on some environmental cues in the game, it seems like this is very likely to happen with future DLC. That's excellent. 


Overall: 
This is a fantastic game that is absolutely worth playing. I will absolutely continue to support this studio if they continue their effort in balancing and fixing things as they have been so far. I really hope to see some effort in fixing endgame balancing, as this is my biggest concern at the moment, and poses a threat to enjoyability on future playthroughs. I think this game in general is a huge achievement for a smaller studio, and I love the overall feel of it. With some minor adjustments I can see myself running through multiple new game plus cycles. 

Thank you for the fantastic game. Keep doing your best!!!!

Mortal Shell II é exatamente o tipo de sequência que eu esperava: mantém a identidade do primeiro jogo, mas expande praticamente tudo.

Joguei o primeiro Mortal Shell pouco antes de começar o II e, apesar de ter gostado dele, era evidente que se tratava de um projeto bem mais limitado em escopo e orçamento. Mortal Shell II parece o momento em que os desenvolvedores pegaram aquela ótima ideia e finalmente tiveram recursos para transformá-la em algo muito maior e mais completo.

A maior mudança é o mundo. Agora temos um mundo aberto com mapa que lembra bastante a estrutura de Elden Ring, cheio de caminhos alternativos, dungeons, áreas opcionais, chefes, armas, carcaças, NPCs, comerciantes, side quests e segredos. E o melhor é que o jogo realmente recompensa a curiosidade. Estou constantemente encontrando alguma coisa que me faz querer desviar da rota principal para descobrir o que existe ali. É aquele tipo de jogo em que você pensa "vou só ver o que tem depois daquela ruína" e meia hora depois está completamente envolvido em outra coisa.

O sistema de carcaças também está muito mais interessante. Agora existe uma progressão bem mais robusta, com vínculos, memórias e árvores de habilidades próprias. Armas e equipamentos também oferecem muito mais possibilidades de build. Estou usando Tiel com a Iconoclasta e já comecei a pensar em como combinar habilidades, pedras de Tar, itens passivos e outros sistemas — algo que no primeiro jogo era bem mais simples.

O combate continua tendo aquele peso característico de Mortal Shell. Não é simplesmente uma tentativa de copiar Dark Souls ou Elden Ring: ainda existe uma identidade própria aqui, principalmente nas mecânicas de carcaça e endurecimento. Só que agora tudo isso está inserido em um RPG muito maior.

Visualmente o jogo também é excelente. Estou jogando no PC em 4K, Ultra, Ray Tracing por hardware, e é um jogo realmente bonito, principalmente pela iluminação, materiais e direção artística. O desempenho também tem sido muito bom considerando a qualidade gráfica e o RT. DLSS funciona muito bem e existe bastante margem para ajustar qualidade e desempenho sem destruir a imagem.

Tecnicamente ainda existem algumas arestas e coisas que podem ser refinadas, algo até esperado considerando a dimensão muito maior do jogo em relação ao primeiro. Mas até agora nada disso diminuiu significativamente minha experiência.

Talvez o maior elogio que eu possa fazer seja simples: Mortal Shell II está me dando vontade de explorar. Não estou simplesmente seguindo objetivos para terminar o jogo; estou interessado em entender seus sistemas, experimentar coisas, encontrar novas áreas e descobrir o que existe no mundo.

Se o primeiro Mortal Shell parecia uma ótima ideia limitada pelo tamanho do projeto, Mortal Shell II parece essa mesma ideia finalmente recebendo espaço, orçamento e ambição para crescer.

[h2]Mortal Shell II - Casual souls-like?[/h2]

I never played the first Mortal Shell, but I tried the demo and was immediately impressed. From the first few minutes, I knew I wanted to play more.

The gameplay is classic Soulslike: sometimes easy, sometimes brutally difficult. The biggest problem is the balance. Early and mid-game bosses felt surprisingly easy, but the last 4-5 bosses were a completely different story. Some of them can basically one-shot you, even when you're exploring everything and upgrading your build. I even had a few moments where I wanted to quit and ask for a refund.

The Shell system and weapons are great, though, and give you plenty of ways to build your character. Combat is satisfying and has enough variety to keep things interesting.

The music is nothing special - it exists, but I rarely noticed it.

Despite the frustrating moments, I really enjoyed the game. If you like Soulslikes, I definitely recommend giving Mortal Shell II a chance. Just be ready for some questionable difficulty spikes.

8/10 - frustrating at times, but a really enjoyable Soulslike overall.

Pros:
-Beautiful looking world with a dark atmosphere and a variety of diverse environments
-combat that feels chunky in most instances (especially with the riposte attacks which are amazing) and fluid/smooth
-enemy design (not necessarily movesets while some do have cool moves, I mainly mean the enemies look cool)
-not overly difficult (which could be a negative in somes mind yet I see this game as a good entry for new souls-like players)
-interesting weapons that all have cool movesets
-really good performance and optimization given how great the graphics are 
-the available shells are great with their own stories and abilities that make it worth using each of them (yet it has been said that it would likely take numerous runs to see all of the shell memories) 
-exploration feels rewarding with beautiful vistas to see and items to find
-the devs seem to be well aware of the bugs and issues which is a huge plus
-interesting and fun tarstones to use that can greatly change how you play (while I do agree with many others that some of them are just useless to use and don't make much of a difference)

Cons:
-ENEMY DAMAGE: despite the Day 1 patch, enemy damage can still be absurd. There will be numerous enemies and as many have already said, the mid to late game areas house a lot of these enemies who can easily either one to two shot you or take 50% of your health. This comes particularly annoying and frustrating 

-SUMMONS: while I never used these at all I tried them a few times as I was curious at their effectiveness and found them to be rather useless. While I don't know their specific stats, their health pool and damage is nonexistent and there is really no point in even using them and I would rather tell a struggling player just to focus on learning a boss's moveset instead of relying on a summon to help

-BEACONS: there are numerous areas in the game with one example being the right region in Fanweald that severely lack any sort of checkpoints. While many might chalk this up as being meaningless negativity or complaints, it comes to a point where when you couple together the fact that a large majority of enemies deal a absurd amount of damage  and that regions often have chunks where a lot of enemies are concentrated in that area leading to a situation where you are left with little to no healing items and are forced to either trek back to a previous beacon or push through and rush to find a beacon before engaging with anymore enemies

-DUNGEONS: While I found many of the dungeons to be fun and with decent variety, what I didn't really like is a similar point that I made with beacons. If there are extensive areas with no beacons, going into a dungeon and possibly dying means that you'll have to run through an are with a large concentration of enemies just to get back to your lost gloom. This gets easier to manage as you get stronger but it can be vert frustrating. An idea that I think could work is something akin to the dungeons in Elden Ring where if you end up dying, you'll get teleported back to the start of the dungeon with a stake of Marika  

-AUDIO BUGS: I encountered numerous audio bugs that as far as I could tell, ALWAYS required a full game restart to fix. One of them was a very minor one in which if you opened the map while on a moving lift, the lift will continue to make noise as if its still moving even as its stops. Another one I encountered was a general issue where audio in certain corrupted gate dungeons would entirely cut out and this also occurred in other areas of the game but it appeared to be random (I never bothered checking to see if it happens consistently) 

I'd give this a 8/10 despite the issues. I personally did not find them severe enough to derail my playthrough and at most they were annoying. Given most people's opinions on souls-likes and the seeming over saturation of them in the market, I'd say this is a very solid entry and one that should demand your attention with it having enough diversity from others in the genre with overly better combat, exploration, and a "generally" more polished experience.

Here's my review after 30+ hours of Mortal Shell 2:

The Good 

Weapons and Combat: The combat is absolutely awesome. While there are a limited number of weapons and sidearms, each one feels distinct and unique. They are all very viable options depending upon your build and it was very refreshing that I ended up using everything at some point in my run. Some are better than others but overall each weapon and sidearm brings its own unique flavor to combat. 

No Stamina Bar: I think this makes sense for this game. Throughout the game there are various different enemies and bosses that have particular moves that are just impossible to dodge practically with a stamina bar. Knowing that you don't have to manage your stamina doesn't necessarily make the game easier; instead, it allows for more agency over what your Harbinger is doing at any given time. Even though you are still heavily committed to your actions, the cooldown period gives you that much more grace by not having a stamina bar. It's a good change and one I'd like to see in future soul likes if it makes sense for the game. 

The World: The world space itself could be described as bleak, demure, melancholy, atmospheric, and/or grim. This setting makes the world feel alive and real. You aren't the knight in shining armor bound to the tower to save the princess and defeat the dragon here. Instead, you're created to serve and simply duty bound to see your mission through. There isn't much merriment to be had (save for one particular place far to the east) nor are there really any welcoming NPCs to spur you on and give you hope. The journey is long and arduous and it's the world that really drives this home for me. But despite this, it is darkly beautiful in its own right. Between colossal towers draped in red flowers, snowy wastelands, rich, green forests, destroyed towns, ethereal planes and more, the world is a wonderful place to explore and get to know. 

Build Variety: There are many different items you can find to make a plethora of builds. Each build that I had felt like it had a purpose and I like toying around with all the different options I was given. Again, not everything is for everyone but the variety that is here is promising and effective. I found myself using different stuff all the time my entire playthrough and I was pleased to see that, while I did find some busted stuff, it didn't work on everything. Sure you can definitely brute force your way through with a single weapon, sidearm, and Tarstones but the abundance of items here made build crafting very enjoyable for me. 

Shells: I adore the Shell system in this game. It's essentially a class based system where you are the Barbarian or the Thief or the Paladin. Each Shell felt unique to use. Want a glass cannon build focused on ripostes? Eredrim is for you. Want to inflict status ailments on your foes while you beat the daylights out of them with your fists? Smert is your guy. Want to skulk around in the shadows and do incredible amounts of crit damage via DPS? Tiel has got you covered! But what was an even better touch was the memories you got to view about these Shells on how they all ended up dying and what their respective goal was beforehand. My favorite stories were Proxima's and Eredrim's but there are 6 others I didn't even see fully. And on top of this, each Shell has its own skill tree of sorts to make your Shell semi-unique to you. It is a great way to revitalize class based RPGs while still having enough customization within it to accommodate players privy to skill based RPGs. A well thought out and rewarding system. 

Dungeons: This is a real highlight here I think. Every dungeon I stepped into felt like it was handcrafted by a different individual. They are all so unique and different from each other they made exploration worth it. Not every dungeon was this 15-20 minute side quest that you did, in fact some were as simple as walking in, killing 5 enemies, loot the chest, and leave, but each one had its own distinct flair to it that made me want to explore them all. If you love exploration and dungeon crawling for cool loot, Mortal Shell 2 has it in spades. Very well done.


The Bad

Bugs: As to be expected in this day and age honestly but it still get flak from me. There are still a lot of little annoyances in the game that need to be fixed. Things like getting stuck on or between objects, game crashes (I only got one crash my entire playthrough but it did happen so...), audio glitches, Gloom not appearing after death (this happened to me a couple of times). Nothing game breaking but things that I imagine future patches should be able to clear up. 

Leveling: So this one hurts to write but it is a problem. Mortal Shell 2 has done away with traditional stat leveling and opted for a character level only. As you level, the diminishing returns get worse and worse to the point where past level 25-30, it's just not really worth leveling anymore. The soft caps are pretty egregious and even though I beat the game at level 46, I never really felt like level 46 was a medium-high level. It is serviceable but could have been much better than what it is. 

Build Restrictions: Look, I like to explore. I like to find cool gear. But I hate when that cool gear is resisted to certain weapons and sidearms. Honestly, this is the feature in the game I hate the most. It just limits the build variety for no reason, especially in a game that has no MP at the time of writing. You gave us the Slayer Seal that makes us a literal god but we can't equip specific Tarstones on anything we want to? That sucks. Thankfully, the build variety is good enough that this never becomes a major problem but as good as it is now, it could have been so much better if the Tarstones were treated more like Elden Ring's talismans. I'm hoping for this to be changed in the future more than anything else. 

Enemy Variety: This one is kind of neutral really but I'll explain why it's in The Bad. There are indeed many types of enemies in the game, true enough. The problem I have is that it's a long time before you see any enemies different from Knight, Big Knight, Fodder Knight, Priest, Fire Priest, Poison Priest, Walking Tree. You have to get into the mid game before more enemies are presented but then some enemies are only present a few times throughout the game while others are seen all the time. While the quality of enemies is good, the pacing of when you see these enemies is far too wide. I wish that they could have had more unique enemies at the start of the game as there were at the mid to late game. 


Final Thoughts

Mortal Shell 2 is a fantastic souls like. It plays to its strengths, is unapologetic in its difficulty, or lack thereof if using the Slayer Seal, has great pacing, a solid story, memorable bosses, interesting and unique weapons and Shells, a world fraught with danger and intrigue, and it's all wrapped up in a nice 20-40 hour experience. I would absolutely recommend this game to anyone who asks me and I believe it is well worth your time and money spent. Overall, 8.75 / 10

Mortal Shell 2 - A Somewhat Brutal, Beautifully Optimized Souls like

After about 30.7 hours with completing the game, I had a great time with it. The combat feels satisfying, the atmosphere is fantastic, and there’s a lot to appreciate for. I’ve seen and experienced a pretty substantial portion of what the game has to offer. There are still a few achievements left to chase, but overall, I’m very happy with the experience.                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                             
One thing that genuinely impressed me was how well optimized the game is for an Unreal Engine 5 title. Performance was consistently solid throughout my playthrough, and I encountered very few glitches. The handful I did run into were mostly instances of falling through the floor, but thankfully they were relatively uncommon and didn’t significantly impact my experience.                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                              
The enemy variety is pretty good, although I was disappointed that some regular enemies are reused as bosses. That felt a little lazy and took away from some of the encounters. The main bosses, on the other hand, were great. Their designs were memorable and their move sets were fun to learn and fight against. My biggest complaint with them was their health. Considering how frequently I was upgrading my weapon, I felt like I should have been doing noticeably more damage. Some bosses felt extremely spongey, which made certain fights drag on longer than they needed to.                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                        Overall, Mortal Shell 2 is a very enjoyable action RPG with great atmosphere, satisfying combat, cool boss designs, and surprisingly strong optimization for an UE5 game. Despite some spongey bosses, reused enemies, and the occasional floor glitch, I had a blast with it and would definitely recommend it

Let me preface this by saying that I really enjoyed Mortal Shell 2, and I can definitely see this blossoming into one of my top 10 Souls-likes, but I really can't recommend it until it's had a pass over by the Devs and a couple of patches.

Pros:
-I really adore the art style and the writing, it is a genuinely well written piece of fiction that I managed to lose myself in for the entirety of my play time, and a big part of that is the Shells that you come to inhabit and their stories. There is a slight downside to this, which I will explore later.
-The combat is usually quite enjoyable, with meaty sounds and a real feeling of weight behind your swings, and likewise most of the animations are stellar and full of character, especially from The Harbinger.
-The progression for the first half of the game feels very rewarding and fair, like you've earned every scrap of Gloom, Coin, and Materials to improve yourself and tackle greater challenges.
-The larger dungeon-style areas where you find and fight the main bosses of the game are diverse and stick well to the theme that they are given, a highlight of this was the first area that you had to fight through to fight Magdalena, the Shepard Boss was a delight.
-The variety and uniqueness of each of the Shells was a treat, the abilities are interesting and the playstyles are very diverse, I found myself wanting to max out all of them to experiment with builds and try them out, something that proved to be a challenge.
-I really enjoyed the two open areas of the game, I found that exploring all the nooks and crannies was very rewarding and exciting.

Cons:
-Some of the bosses are particularly difficult, not for the traditional reasons a boss is difficult in a souls game, but instead because the camera (The True Final Boss.) decides to throw itself into the bosses every time they make one of their massive "Jump across the map" attacks, and also most enemies have the terrible habit of canceling their animations mid-way through an attack and switching to another one with incredible speed and after I have committed to a defense against the previous attack. There is also a serious inconsistency in the timings and the I-Frames in some of the animations, especially verses against the larger bosses and most especially against the last boss of the game (Whom as of the writing of this review, I have yet to beat.)
-The limited amount of Glimpses is a serious bottleneck on my enjoyment of the game because I have found that certain areas, enemies, and bosses lend themselves to being fought with a certain Shell and their playstyle, but I am entirely incapable of upgrading most of them, and by my calculations it will take at least one other playthrough to do so, something that I am unlikely to do with the game in it's current state.

I have a few other points to make, both positives and negatives, but needless to say my opening statement holds true, If the game's quality stayed as good as it was in the first 75% I would have recommended it in a heartbeat, but in it's current state, I cannot.

Хоть у меня и опыт игры в соулс-лайк играх не особо большой, играл только в AI Limit, Code Vein, Lies of Pi и Elden ring, я могу точно сказать что игра в разы хуже того что я играл до этого. 
Но сначала плюсы
1. Интересная билдовка, персонажей можно собрать по разному и сами персонажи довольно интересны геймплейно
2. Приятная на глаз графика, и красивые анимации за которыми реально приятно наблюдать
3. Дизайн оружия и персонажей тоже интересный, особенно удивила базука арбалет и катана которая превращается в топор.
А теперь к минусам, их тут очень много
1. Баги. Не самое критичное, так как игра вышла не так давно, но блин столько раз падать сквозь лифт, и даже падать сквозь текстуры не оч приятно. Плюс иногда багается костер из за чего приходилось умирать для решения этой проблемы.
2. Таргет на мобов. Это я хочу выделить как самый огромный минус для меня точно. Во все соулс игры что я играл была с этим проблема, но по сравнению с тем что происходит здесь это просто были цветочки. Ты в упор спокойно промахиваешься из за того что цель меняется на долю секунды, если мобов больше двух можно сразу готовиться к миссам и горению почему я бью воздух. Из за этой же проблемы навык разбойника с невидимостью столько раз у меня не попадал что пальцев на руках и ногах не хватит. Плюс этот навык спококйно может не попасть в упор потому что мобик двинеться чуть чуть в сторону. Плюс он еще какой то смазанный и медленный во время драки с боссом. 
3. Урон и вторая форма. Честно, человек что придумал идею со второй формой просто решил поиздеваться над игроками. Это просто болван который и умеет что бить. А урон в этой игре просто отпадный. К моменту второй половины игры почти любой моб тебя убивает за 1-2 атаки, про боссов вообще молчу. Пока ты не получишь уровень 25 примерно, любой граб босса и элитки, убивает тебя и ты летишь в бесполезную форму. А доводка у мобов в этой игре неадекватно забавная, будто на тебя магнит нацепили, мобы могут завернуть 360 атаку и так далее. Плюсом мобы почти вообще не ловят стаггер из за чего еще веселее играть.
4. Странное решения ограничения кубов с намазками на определенные виды оружия, я не понимаю зачем это было сделано впринципе. Ладно умения, но стихийный урон?
5. К концу прохождения, играть реально желания нет, обычных мобов меньше чем элитных. Мужика с косой разрабы прям очень взлюбили к концу, пихают куда не попадя. 
6. Костры. Их мало. До ужаса. Ты приходишь на локу а костер у тебя в ее центре, из за чего бегаешь как полоумный чтобы понять как не сдохнуть от случайной тычки.
7. Прокачка вообще скучная, за тебя качают просто крит урон и хп. Я не могу например собрать стрелка с кучей решимости, или хп побольше себе взять. 
Минусы еще были точно но я уже не вспомню оставшиеся.
Ожидал хотя бы хороший средненький соулс в итоге полностью разочаровался. Если исправить странные решения разработчика допилить игру, она будет реально гуд но пока что точно нет.

Mortal Shell 2 is an absolute monster of a sequel. I went in expecting a solid improvement over the first game and instead got something that feels like it was built by people who actually listened to every complaint and then went twice as hard.

The combat is just *right*. No stamina bar means you’re free to stay aggressive without that constant little meter dictating the pace. It’s still punishing as hell if you get greedy, but the rhythm is so much better. When you start chaining perfect parries into resolve abilities and then finish with a brutal execution, it feels disgusting in the best way. The new weapons all have real weight to them too. That double-headed axe in particular has no business feeling this good.

The Shells are the real star though. Eight of them this time, and every single one actually changes how you play instead of just giving you slightly different stats. Finding a new one in some forgotten corner of the map and immediately wanting to respec around its abilities is such a good feeling. I’ve already swapped main Shells three times because each one keeps unlocking new ways to break the game.

The world is denser and more interesting than the first game by a mile. It’s not trying to be Elden Ring scale, and that’s a good thing. It’s compact, full of little dungeons and secrets, and every area has its own nasty personality. The enemy design is pure heavy metal album cover material. Some of these things look like they crawled out of a nightmare and then got even uglier on the way.

If you liked the first one even a little, or if you’re just looking for a soulslike that actually has its own identity instead of copying homework, play this. It’s special.

I only have one real complaint:

Resources for upgrading weapons are fully refundable (pending a payment of some xp/gloom, with cost scaling with the quantity of the refund), making weapon upgrade materials effectively an unlimited resource. 

However, Glimpses and Tarcore, which are used to upgrade Shells and Tarstones respectively, are not refundable, and are very finite. This makes experimentation with upgrading both shells and tarstones a major risk (within a single playthrough). Glimpses and Tarcore should be refundable like weapon-uprade materials (at the cost of xp/gloom).

You could easily lock yourself out of fully upgrading any single shell if you experiment with upgrading too many of them even a little bit.

Frustratingly, many tarstones can only be applied to one or two specific weapons (even if they have quite generic effects). This confounds tarstone upgrade experiementation since, again, the upgrade resource is finite and non-refundable; if you already have a similar tarstone fully upgraded, but which can't be used on a weapon you'd like to try, you might forgo trying the weapon altogether because of the cost involved in upgrading the tarstone that can be applied to it.

Many Shells and Tarstones are found quite deep in one's playthrough; without reasonable experiementation options, players will likely just ignore new shells or tarstones once they have a build their comfortable with, for fear of "wasting" the precious few glimpses and tarcore they have left (on the chance something potentially better that demands those materials shows up).

Good: Combat feels way more fluid and aggressive than the original, the world is now a large interconnected open world packed with secrets, and the Shell-swapping system finally has room to shine — it hands you a plethora of tools and trusts you to figure out how to use them. It's more accessible than the first game but still lets hardcore players ramp up the difficulty if they want.

Not so good: Resource/progression pacing can feel a bit stingy and confusing early on, and there's a handful of bugs plus a somewhat thin story.

Verdict: One of the best soulslikes of the year — atmospheric, brutal, way improved over the original. Worth it if you like the genre.
