As of this review, I can't give this game a thumbs-up. I would consider changing my opinion if they can patch the issues because it's just a lot of small things that are adding up to a terrible experience. The core of the game is good, but it's very obvious that this game was not ready to release and I feel deceived by the demo.

I have only been playing on night mode and I haven't yet finished the game.

Good stuff:
+The game runs really well, probably the best performing UE5 game that I've played.
+It's pretty and has great atmosphere.
+Full key remapping if you prefer to use keyboard/mouse.
+Level design is amazing; the world is a joy to explore.
+Fluid combat with no stamina.

Not so good stuff:
-Rampant bugs and glitches: enemies disappearing through walls (sometimes they come back, sometimes not), enemies move cancelling, enemies getting stuck on nothing (the ground looks flat), archer enemies that fire with no animation and sometimes double fire arrows, enemies (including bosses) somehow ending up on my head during combat, repeatedly being launched into the air so high that I can't see the game (I eventually come back down, one boss did this to me twice), there are probably other things that I'm forgetting because there are a lot of issues.
-Very large areas with lots of enemies and no beacons.
-Enemies have a ridiculous aggro range and will follow you forever.
-The camera is awful regardless if you use Immersive or Action.
-Very questionable attacks from some bosses (some attacks are probably 2-3 frames and you get hit before it looks like you should).
-RUNBACKS
-Infinite Seal doesn't feel useful because of the long recovery.
-I feel hesitant to try a new shell and weapon because it's so expensive to upgrade.

I really hope that the devs are listening to feedback and are able to fix the game, because I want to love this one.

I am blown away at how many people are recommending this game. This was one of the worst souls-likes I have ever played, and I've played almost all of them.
This is like a much worse Lords of the Fallen. I'm just gonna rapid fire the terrible parts of this game because I don't think I can give this game another second of my time.

The soundtrack is terrible. It's like they took a sample of an electric guitar sound and just looped it for every single boss fight.

Weapon selection. Abysmal. These weapons are sluggish and feel terrible to use. Movesets are akin to Dark Souls 1 or Lords of the Fallen, in that you get heavy and light attacks, and maybe a useful ability for the weapon.

Bosses. Inflated health pools, 5 moves, and insane tracking. I seriously doubt these devs could beat their own game without some sort of cheese build.

Speaking of tracking... That might be the single worst aspect of this game. Most enemies have attacks that magnetize to the player with crazy tracking. Sure, it can stop you from speeding through zones, but when it comes to figuring out spacing and positioning while fighting, forget it.

The story is just there. We're some alien baby getting eggs scattered around the map. Only cutscenes are boss intros which are like 10 seconds long.

The balance is all sorts of out of whack. One shot grab attacks by bosses, pitiful healing items, weapons that do no damage, taking forever to level up (which doesnt even let you pick stats.)
Want to go for deflecting and ripostes like Sekiro? You'll do barely any damage since your riposte doesnt scale with anything. 

Number 1 time waster might be the awful runbacks. Some of these are on the level of Bed of Chaos, or like, double the Orphan of Kos run. It is torture.

Bugs. Now, I'm actually a VERY forgiving gamer when it comes to bugs. But this game just has too many actual game breaking ones. Examples like, interacting with a scripted jump mechanic that can just launch you off or under the map; Abilities being actually unusable that part of a characters kit (Stray Genessa); Colliding with invisible objects or getting stuck on unseeable geometry... It is just too much.

The UI is just not good. Long delays to get to your inventory to change weapons and equipment, and even when going through the fast travel menu. UE5 really shines here huh
-----
The ONLY good thing about this game, is the unique animation for every enemy when you riposte them. Even though the riposte does no damage.
-----
I'd give this game a 4/10, and a 5/10 if they were to patch a lot of the BS. Seriously wait for patches and a sale.

Pros:
Solid combat options and plenty of depth with each shell, and weapon combination choices.
Overworld Exploration is fun.
On DAY mode, enemies don't feel super bullet spongey. 
Some bosses are genuinely interesting mechanically. 
Great visuals and combat weight.

Cons:
There are dozens of weapons and sidearms, but you can only reasonably use one or two. Also, most of them are uselessly outclassed by a few meta weapons.
The stamina system is replaced with a "resolve" system that forces you into melee combat regardless of your build.
Enemies have comically insane tracking. You need to learn to parry everything because maintaining distance isn't a realistic possibility, especially with how many tight corridors this game has you fighting in.
There are only like 10 types of enemies in the game aside from bosses.
On NIGHT mode - enemies have 3x as much HP, and every single enemy in the game will one shot you even at level 50 with the most durable shell equipped. 
There are no passive upgrades that increase survivability that don't depend on getting kills first. And basically no bosses have adds.
Balance is all over the place with upgrades. Some weapon upgrades and statuses are just ... bad. Like challenge yourself to beat the game with this garbage bad.
Build choice is an illusion because of the lack of passive tarstone variety.
Combat rules arbitrarily do not apply to some bosses and enemies. Some are immune to knockback/flinch. Some aren't.
Riposting (breaking stance on bosses and enemies) does not scale as the game progresses. It is ALWAYS optimal to AVOID riposting and just hit characters with light/heavy attacks while they're downed. Late game riposting even with characters with nodes dedicated to it do PATHETIC damage. 

The first half of the game is fun and enjoyable. The second half/later game is a SLOG. Do yourself a favor and stop playing before you enter the mammon region. And DO NOT enable Night mode. Even if you're challenging yourself, all it does it make enemies bullet sponges and every encounter threatens to kill you in a single hit. 

As someone who beat the game on Night mode for my first playthrough, don't do this to yourself. It just kills the fun of the game. Safe it for NG+ or just read what fights you need to enable it for to get hidden items. (Spoilers: There's nothing important locked into night mode)

If you do pick up the game - you can only fully upgrade 3 characters in a playthrough. Fully invest in one of the first characters you find, then be more selective with the second two. 

Negatives greatly outweight the positives, so I wouldn't recommend this unless you REALLY want a fromsoft experience before the next souls game drops.

开头很惊艳，尤其是在玩demo，看见一个现实世界里真的存在的剑柄打击动作的时候，我毫不犹豫的购买了。但是越玩到后面越觉得制作组的技术没有办法撑起这个游戏的野心。层出不穷的bug（包括但不限于无法攻击、音乐音效消失、卡墙里出不来、捡不了东西、怪物不攻击我、飞天等等等等）和特性（说一个很有意思的：游戏底层应该设定的是玩家在遭到投射物攻击后会被击退，但是并没有考虑过投射物投射的方向，所以如果你背对着一个像你袭来的投射物，它会把你扯过去，因为你被“击退”了），能看出来制作组的野心，8个躯壳8种主武器8种服务器，构建了不同的玩法，但是得益于狗屎一样的数值设计，大部分武器以及躯壳机制其实就是玩具，后期的数值只能玩bd，如果老老实实跟boss立回我都不敢想得有多享受，其次是地图设计，感觉是想做开放世界但是其实这个开放世界确实没那么开放，开局南边的数值根本就不是人打的，其实只能去北边。最后是奖励，感觉到最后不知道该塞什么了，地牢后期（南边）都没啥奖励了，基本上就是强化石、钱什么的，大大减少了我的探索欲望。
    但是我依旧要给个好评，其实能感觉制作组设计某些部分的时候很用心，个别地牢和解密机制让我很惊喜，boss设计还算在线，地图虽然有点绕但是我探索的蛮开心的，玩bd的话玩的比较舒服。

The foundation here is great, but the game desperately needs a balance pass.

A clear example is the Lost Child boss: the first 80% of the fight is clean and readable, but at 20% HP, it suddenly shifts into non-telegraphed, erratic attacks that can instantly wipe you. Clearing 4/5 of a health bar hitless only to die to an unreadable burst isn't rewarding difficulty—it's just frustrating.

As a Soulslike veteran (Plat in Elden Ring, DS1–3, Lies of P; cleared Sekiro, Bloodborne, Wukong, Khazan, Nine Sols), I agree with reviews pointing out tuning issues. Keeping it Positive for now, but hoping to see dev patches address these balance spikes soon.

综合评价7/10，动作设计、各种bd都相当不错，怪物的设计总体不错，但是种类不算丰富，后期填充大量的换皮怪，前中期图地牢设计明显有想法，然而并没有保持住，后期几乎都是一本道加堆怪，并没有什么乐趣，最终图的氛围渲染好，但是抽象的数值设计使得角色和怪依旧在激情互秒，玩家大喊一声谁敢杀我，随便一只路过的小怪就会说我敢，然后两刀拿下；虽然是开放世界，但本质是多个箱庭区域，地图设计中规中矩，探索体验还算不错，可惜后期物品种类少的缺点掩盖不住，使得探索像通马桶，也就捡捡强化石和金币相关道具
接下来全是槽点，余露石的经验设计已经限制了强化的速度，但还要用核心来卡能强化的数量，改成给经验减少肝度还差不多；同样的还有瞬悟，在已经通过限制每周目获取数量的基础上，还不允许洗点去强化别的躯壳，相当于让一周目爱探索的玩家白探，能看不能玩；虽然补丁调高了金币掉落，但是不去特意刷一周目依旧只能强化一把主武器一把副武器，连商人道具都不能做到随意清空，而据说多周目金币获取倍率并没有增加，更是压制了我玩多周目体验不同bd的欲望，在大量换皮怪的基础上还要反复刷金币，实在是枯燥让人提不起兴趣；收集品道具种类少，从而增加要收集的数量，与刷金币的理由相同，依旧无趣，总而言之，虽然设计了多周目，但是怪物种类、道具种类少，金币获取慢等因素让终盘的探索玩法并不有趣，此外还有大量堆怪，想跑图只打boss体验也一般，只能期待后续更新boss连战

REVIEW IN PROGRESS (7h)

I am really impressed by this. Small team managed to achieve something that feels fresh and unique enough in comparison to many other souls-like games on the market. Looks and runs great, sounds meaty and the OST is metal, gameplay is fun and provides a very decent amount of variety (also NO TYPICAL STAMINA, instead you have a bar for special abilities and attacks, I love it), and the game in general is MUCH better than the first one, what an improvement on the core ideas of the last one. 

The biggest cons might be the running distance from beacons to points of interest like some people have already mentioned, and I have yet to see about the enemy variety because some repeat more often than I'd like (those exploding poison guys are annoying as HECK), but other than that it is a pretty polished and memorable experience so far, can't stop playing and trying out different shells and weapons. 

Recommend!

本人流程是正常探索流程，黑夜模式拿隐藏，剩下的流程走的白天标准难度，打完欢欣平原三boss再去的马蒙，没有拿任何的越级装备。

提尔、斧匕、霰弹枪开局，搜集到的资源资源全交提尔和这两把武器，其他躯壳和武器一点资源没有投入，一张地图没买，一个躯壳没定位，终盘的时候剩下将近60个瞬悟。

游戏流程中只有前期打林中女士是bd未成型受苦的，20级以后基本以后所有boss都是背刺两到三套输出循环解决战斗。后期技能大成以后直接背刺双暴流派，咒血霰弹枪暴击速射的伤害谁用谁知道。（最后梅兹龙二阶段有点肉，而且转阶段的时候被吸进去处决了，记得好像打了5轮技能循环）。

背刺挂易伤加主武器暴击砍2~3刀，决心基本可以100%回收，推图几乎可以全程技能起手打群怪。MS2是一个主打角色技能驱动和武器模组构筑的游戏，需要学习角色的技能机制，记弹反和韧性伤害，这样玩下来才会比较舒服，压制得敌人无法还手。

这游戏我自己觉得主要问题在下半区的地图设计。地图探索上半区难度是很小的，下半区难度略大，主要是拿地图的地点要是运气不好绕半天也拿不到，这游戏探图没地图的话是真的挺难受的，这游戏开放世界看着大跑起来小，战点就会比较密集，没地图的情况下跑错路是真的坐牢。

Игра отлично начинает, но к середине полностью теряет темп, превращаясь в нудный и невознаграждающий рутинный процесс.

Плюсы:
Сильное начало: Первые часы игры действительно затягивают грамотным расположением чекпоинтов и неплохой атмосферой.

Минусы:
Отсутствие прогрессии: Скучная система прокачки и бесполезные награды за сложные активности.
Слабый баланс: Из всего арсенала и доступных классов реально эффективны лишь единицы.
Ужасный левел-дизайн к середине: Длинные и нудные перебежки с назойливыми врагами, преследующими через всю карту.
Глупая экономика ресурсов: Стрельба конкурирует за ресурс с ключевыми навыками.

Боевая система и баланс:
Разнообразие арсенала оказывается иллюзией. Из 8 видов оружия ближнего боя и 8 оболочек (классов) реально играбельны максимум 2–3. Дальний бой выполнен в виде странного гиммика: выстрелы расходуют тот же ресурс, что навыка персонажа и камни прокачки, из-за чего стрельба становится абсолютно бессмысленной.

Прогрессия и награды:
Развитие персонажа максимально казуальное (просто линейный рост уровня). Поначалу полученные камни прокачки радуют, но быстро выясняется, что половина из них не имеет ценности. Награды за подземелья выглядят смехотворно: за убийство сложного босса тебе дают один предмет прокачки, когда для апгрейда нужно минимум пять.

Сложность и искусственное затягивание:
На уровне сложности «Ночь» сложности как таковой нет — враги просто превращаются в «губки для урона». Расстановка маяков (костров) к середине игры становится ужасной, а бэктрекинг — мучительным: мобы не отстают и агрятся через всю карту.

ИТОГ:
Игра страдает от плохого баланса и затянутости. Если в первые часы она интригует, то ближе к середине игра превращается в скучный фарм с нудными перемещениями и неинтересными боссами.

Game forsure has a ton of jank and missing info for some things, but the rule of cool is definitely in play here for a lot of in the game. 

Performance is amazing. I have an exceptional PC and I run everything on Ultra settings with no dips in framerate. The loading times are great which is becoming rare in modern gaming. The fast travel system from the tower looks amazing and loads quickly. 

One thing about the hub world. Everything in it is very cool, but the way you have to get to the launch pad is a little silly. It should have been in the Gloom room location and the Gloom should've been another room back. Running that far and taking an elevator EVERY TIME you have to go to a shrine you haven't cleansed or have to upgrade a weapon, stone, is very tedious after the 30th, 40th time. Fixing this would be a major change in the game and I don't see it realistically happening, but the fact that it wasn't caught in early playtesting is a little odd. Maybe I am the odd one when it comes to this.

The shells you inhabit have AWESOME abilities, but it's not really encouraged to level up more than MAYBE 2 in a playthrough. I haven't beaten the game yet but I have put in alot of time and because I experimented early on with one shell and leveling it up, I can't level up a shell I found later in the game that I enjoy more. Seems like reallocating the levels you put in shells would solve this issue, but I can't say for sure. 

Very fun game but very irritating for some enemies. The blocking system is EXTREMELY punishing against enemies who attack very quickly. It's not the blocking, dodging, or parrying that is the issue with it though. It's the inconsistencies with enemies magnetizing to you. You can never tell when an enemy is going to slide towards you so holding block or dodging are your only options, which holding block gets your meter built up if they do decide to cha cha slide to you. Not knowing when attacks are going to hit takes away player agency in deciding what option is best suited to deal with it. Some boss fights with multiple does are the worst offenders of this issue. There is a fight early on where you fight 2 Grisha's that CONSTATLY teleport through eachother to hit you with unblockable and hard to dodge attacks. One on one the beasts are not that hard to fight, but add 2 in a small room? Hell to manage. 

There is another fight where you fight a massive head called the Last Child. This has got to be the worst fight in the game. I played Tiel the assassin for this fight. The amount of times I went invisible BEFORE he launched his poop attack just for him to randomly hit me with the projectiles not even close to me was frustrating. The next issue was the collisions with this boss. I'm sure you've seen the videos where people get launched into the sky when not even close to the boss, And while funny, it is incredibly annoying to have a good run ruined by getting launched so high his health resets. 

All the boss fights are very awesome. The gate bosses at the end of all the extended areas are extremely interesting and very well designed(EXCEPT ONE^). I haven't fought one yet where the flavor was bad or the difficulty too unfair. Tweak some stones try a different shell or weapon, they all have weaknesses. 

All in all I am having a great time playing the game with brief bouts of frustrations caused by jank and confusing enemy attacks. I would definitely recommend getting it and trying it out. If you like the SOULS games you'll enjoy this.

A solid sequal to the first. Multiplayer is fantastic and adds a ton of additional fun being able to play with others. 

Still some growing pains in early access though. Writing this review as of 08-14-26 and I find that the game's encounters feel a bit more "specialized" compared to the first in a bad way. It feels like MegaCrit wanted to punish people who go too hard on a particular build, but in doing so, have made the fun of stacking absurd combos that made the first game great, feel a bit more bland and frustrating. 

For example, there's one particular epic combat that makes your power cards damage you when you cast them. Playing the defect with a power-focused deck? Sucks to be you. 
There's a few encounters that add status cards to your deck when you attack. Running a shiv deck with the silent? Sucks to be you.
There's a couple encounters that just do massive damage on turns 1-2. Don't draw a block card on those turns? Sucks to be you. 

STS1 felt a little more even keel. Maybe less dynamic enemies, but you never felt punished for finding a combo or theme to your deck, which seems to be common in STS2. Winning is a combination of building a cool deck, but ALSO avoiding the few random encounters that will absolutely end your run. 

I also feel like every enemy in this game just ramps up in power in ways that are a little more punishing to "patient" builds as well. Feels like every enemy has an in-built power escalation loop where they either give themselves strength, load you with statuses, or afflict you with debuffs in ways that you can't really counter, so you're always on a clock to win by a particular turn, or they'll simply outscale you. It's pretty frustrating to be running a defensive deck, slowly accumulating powers and synergies, and then eventually just get womped for 45 damage by an enemy that's been gaining 2 strength every other turn for the whole battle.

Ultimately the game is awesome and the new characters add a lot of fun new dynamics and ways to play, but I think there still needs to be some tuning of the combat and encounters to reach the endless replayability of the first.

Players of this game can roughly be divided into three groups: casual players who just want to have fun, challenge-oriented players who seek difficult content, and those who fall somewhere in between. Good game balance should accommodate both ends of the spectrum by raising the skill ceiling while lowering the skill floor.

I believe that's what players actually want: the same deck build should be able to breeze through lower difficulties, while higher difficulty modes should impose restrictions that make powerful builds much harder—or even impossible—to assemble, preventing strategies such as achieving "infinite" combos.

However, that's clearly not the approach the developers have taken. Instead of simply making powerful builds harder to achieve at higher difficulties, they weakened the cards themselves while simultaneously making enemies stronger. This goes against what many players expected from the game's balancing philosophy.

As a result, casual players struggle to clear the game, while challenge-oriented players who want to take on tougher enemies with powerful, carefully crafted decks are also restricted from doing so.

I typically don’t write reviews this early into playing the game, but I felt like doing it this time. Slay the spire 2 is a very fun game, coming from someone who has barely touched deck builder games before. It’s nice and challenging, runs flawlessly, and is definitely worth its price. If you are unaware, the reason it says “mixed reviews” is due to 2 waves of review bombing. The first being from the Chinese playerbase due to the buffed door maker boss (which I believe is now removed) and the nerfing of infinite card combos, and due to heavy restrictions on Chinese social media, steam reviews were used as an outlet to vent frustration. The second wave of review bombing is due to the name “Anita Sarkeesian” being listed as a consultant in the credits for sts 2. Anita Sarkeesian is a feminist and founder of the website “Feminist Frequency” and was the target of a 2012 harassment campaign due to her stances and critiques on how women are portrayed in pop culture, specifically video games. (Source: “Anita Sarkeesian”, Wikipedia) overall the game is really fun and it sucks that it has been review bombed for pretty stupid reasons. I highly recommend checking it out. (Also, sorry if I got anything wrong)

As a big fan of roguelikes, a lot of people have told me to play the original Slay the Spire. It was praised as basically the perfect game, the best of its genre with unmatched depth and design. Then I finally played it and I wasn't terribly impressed. In my opinion, it was just a fine game that wasn't much better or worse than its contemporaries.
Slay the Spire 2 feels like the game that everyone had been describing to me for years. The amount of depth in the decks you can build has increased dramatically, the art and animation is significantly better (low bar to be fair) and runs generally feel a lot more varied. Enchantments are a brilliant addition, the new ancients replacing the old boss relics are much more fun and creative, the alternate act 1 keeps repeated runs from getting stale and every character has a lot more paths to build into.
Mega Crit has accomplished all of this in a version of the game that's still in early access, with its biggest content additions like new characters and a 4th act still on the way. I can hardly imagine what this game is gonna look like when it hits 1.0, because at this rate it could very well become the roguelike GOAT.

Nothing compels me to write a positive review about a game like a *certain* entitled group of people that complain over nothing.

That being said, this game's great! I played close to 900 hours in the first game and this is a fresh experience while still being familiar. Anthony's done well to take out dominant playstyles from early in the game's life (see: infinites) and they're continuing to put out some great updates to keep things fresh. I especially like the ancient relics in this game. There's so much variety and it feels like each of my runs can play out so differently.

My biggest complaint for current version is Aetherlense. I personally dislike late-game bosses being hard counters to certain playstyles, especially when A10 makes it far more likely you see a particular boss. It pains me when I see a cool shiv card in Act 1/2 and I know that it's a massive risk to take even if it fits really well with my deck. It feels boring in the similar way to how certain cards are too dominant.

It doesn't help that Aetherlense is boring aesthetically compared to Doormaker. I wish they had just reworked Doormaker's kit to keep the cool theming. Hell, I think Aetherlense's mechanics fit Doormaker better (playing too may cards could "alert" him to your presence). I guess Doormaker being in the game at all was just too much for *certain* players.

With all this being said, I'd really like if they followed Monster Train's example and showed you which bosses you'll be fighting in every act from the getgo. It would be a net good for players of all skill levels.

Overall, I'm happy with the game and excited to see where the game goes, especially since we still haven't gotten Act 4!

In short:
When the game clicks, I love it as much as STS1, and it does multiple things better than its predecessor, namely animations and game feel, but the game's low points thoroughly hinder my enjoyment and are too prevalent to recommend the game in its current state. Sadly, my confidence in the direction of this game has eroded due to updates making the experience overall worse rather than better, which is why this is a review instead of an F2. I'd wait until Act 4 is implemented before giving this game a shot (I'll change this review when the game improves significantly or exits Early Access, whichever comes first).

In long:

The difficulty design, in its current state, is awful. The majority of the difficulty comes from the first Act, which means getting a good Act one allows the rest of the run to be on cruise control while getting a bad Act one might as well be a reset; you're getting stonewalled by Decimillipede or Hunter Killer in Act 2 otherwise. This leads to there being a "reverse difficulty curve" which doesn't work for the kind of game STS2 is, so a standard difficulty curve feels needed but isn't present currently. Hard-pool fights generally are too similar to Elites in terms of difficulty, but only give the normal card rewards and gold, so whenever you have the choice, avoid Hard-pool fights; not because you are necessarily ready at that point to deal with all the Elites you could be facing, but because not doing this puts you way too far behind in terms of resources while being left on similar amounts of health. This wasn't an issue in STS1, as the hard-pool fights, while challenging, were a noticeable step down in difficulty from Elites, making them a viable choice for when your deck isn't ready for Elites. 

Some bosses, specifically Vantom, Lagavulin Matriarch, and Knowledge Demon, are great: They have clear, thoughtfully designed patterns that encourage picking up specific kinds of cards to deal with the fight without requiring them, encouraging creative problem solving and rewarding player knowledge, which is the essence of what makes Slay the Spire great in my opinion. The rest of the bosses don't follow suit, either being boring damage races that "stat-check" you in some way, or are Aeonglass, who does too much too quickly relative to the power of cards and amount of resources the average run provides you, making it so you have to build your run from floor one with Aeonglass in mind. This is way too restricting for a boss that you aren't guaranteed to face every run.

Ascension Level 3 (Poverty) and Ascension Level 6 (Inflation) together are the worst part of game currently. It's the STS2 equivalent to Blue Stake in Balatro, being problematic for the same reasons: It's not the most difficult thing to deal with, but it makes the game consistently less fun; it doesn't ask the player to make better decisions or new kinds of decisions, it just reduces the number of possible decisions, restricting creativity and making every fight in the game feel worse just by existing. Entering a shop with 500 Gold should be a dopamine rush, but instead I walk out with a potion, a relic, and either another relic or a remove, but not both. in STS1 on A20, that same situation most of the time has me walking out with 3 relics, a remove, and either a potion or a discounted card. I know STS1 has Ascension levels that also restrict Gold, and I don't like it there either, but at least they're much less broadly restricting and the amount of gold reduced is way smaller (A13: 25% less gold from Bosses only and A16: Increases the cost of all Shop items by only 10%). I would rather A3 and A6 in STS2 be reworked to something entirely unrelated to Gold, but if it has to be Gold related, then making them exactly like their STS1 counterparts would be fine. I just hate when half the reason I'm even engaging in combats, and THE resource that is used for the only reliable means of pivoting a run and making major alterations to a deck beyond just adding a card, is made less available without the rest of the game being altered (in a manner favorable to the player) with this change in mind. 

Trying to build a deck is stymied and unrewarding; it feels like I get punished for not building towards "the meta" both in terms of winrate and in terms of fun factor on all ascension levels, not just A10. This makes card reward RNG, an inherent downside to the way STS is designed, even more volatile than it should be. With Ironclad and Necrobinder in particular, it really does boil down to 'did you find "the cards"?' due to their awkward card pools that, at times, are borderline dysfunctional into the challenges the game throws at you. 

Card upgrades across all card pools feel less impactful than they did in STS1, as the percentage increase in the numbers of each card is generally smaller (for example: more 2 Damage/Block increases on Commons instead of 3 Damage/Block increases on Commons compared to STS1) and most of the really impactful upgrades either got nerfed, patched out due to the base card being reworked, or is attached to an Ancient Reward. While this issue will be alleviated by the difficulty design being addressed, STS2 will still be operating on a lower power level where the power of your deck increases slower and the ceiling is lower. That's not inherently a bad thing, but I prefer STS1's approach, where upgrades generally gave big increases in the power of your deck, but the Acts are balanced with that power scaling in mind; I really enjoy that design paradigm.
The more baffling part is that STS2 already has a potential solution to this: Card Modifications. Via certain relics or events, a card can be given an additional effect unrelated to its upgrade, but can still synergize with said upgrade depending on the card and the modification (Card draw, +1 Energy when played, more damage, more block, damage increases per time played in combat, etc.). These are awesome, I love this addition. It adds another layer to the gameplay that dynamically changes a run and bolsters on-the-fly decision making. It's a shame then that, despite being an addition that feels like a core mechanic, it is extremely underutilized. You'll go entire runs without seeing a single opportunity to modify any of your cards, and the average number of times I've come across those opportunities per run is ~1. Major missed opportunity on what is my favorite addition to STS2 besides the animations.

One final note to the devs specifically: please stop listening to the top 0.1% of the playerbase when it comes balancing difficulty. I know they are loud, and I know they seem like good candidates for this kind of feedback, but the majority of them only speak from what they would like with complete disregard for how that would effect players of all other skill levels and without having a clear idea as to what state of difficulty would be ideal or how that would be reasonably implemented. It's "X is too good, Y is broken, Z is underpowered". Reactionary takes on perceptions regarding a "meta" that only the best can truly participate in and asking for these changes without considering the ripple effects. 
I'm not saying the opinions of these players are valueless, but if they continue to get as much sway as they have over recent balance patches, then the game will become a balanced experience that most players will quit before ever becoming good enough to appreciate the balance. Please prioritize fun over balance whenever those two goals come into conflict.

0.99和0.111版本几乎已经完全是两个游戏了，从删牌变贵，杂技升蓝，放血升蓝，再到最近的压缩不抽牌，我感觉到制作组在有意的打压小卡组循环和无限玩法，从而鼓励玩家多尝试均卡思路和打法。但这不仅破坏了一些小卡组的游戏体验，更破坏了本就对过牌能力需求更高的中卡组和大卡组的游戏体验。卡牌的改动也不全是尽如人意的，例如亡灵契约师的灵魂风暴，本身数值孱弱甚至不如玷污，灵魂体系又被沙漏整的痛苦不堪，这张牌就成为了不能当过度数值卡，也难以当输出终端的一张弃子。

First of all, despite the controversial balancing in the last few months I'm willing to recommend it just on the basis that it is a really fun game [i]if a build works out[/i] (and I still think there are a lot of different builds that can work well even after all the nerfs). Also, both steamrolling and a clutch win can be a real dopamine hit.

However, there are a few design decisions that I don't agree with, so I think the game could easily be even better, and I do hope the balancing becomes a bit less harsh on the player before the game leaves early access.

It's fine that the game is hard and I enjoy the challenge of climbing ascensions, even though I'm really not that good at it. My main gripe is rather that a lot of enemies are made in a way that isn't necessarily mechanically challenging but just annoying to counter unless you have a very specific build. Most of the time, if it's not an elite or boss that counters you by bad luck, a build will still be able to beat those enemies, but it just takes annoyingly long to do so.

A good example are the carapace bugs in act 2. They are annoying for single target builds from being a group, but they also take max 9 damage at once so even an AOE build is capped. I don't find this fight hard except if the build was doomed to fail anyway, but whittling them down is just so tedious and boring most of the time. And there are a quite a few other enemies whose gimmick is only to draw out the fight in one way or another. To make it worse, a lot of these enemies are in Act 1 or early Act 2, so the early stages of a run can really drag out unnecessarily.

The developers have designed monsters with mechanics that certain characters simply cannot overcome using their inherent abilities, while at the same time increasing enemy attack power exponentially through nothing more than inflated numbers.

As a result, clearing the content feels less dependent on actual player skill and more dependent on luck unless you manage to abuse some ridiculously overpowered strategy, it becomes nearly impossible.

It honestly makes the game feel like one of those cheap, number-inflation-driven games where difficulty is created simply by making the stats bigger and bigger. It even makes the overall game design feel crude and unsophisticated due to that reason.

Please reconsider the direction of the difficulty design. This kind of difficulty scaling simply increasing numbers and creating mechanics that certain characters fundamentally cannot deal with feels like something designed at an elementary or middle-school level rather than meaningful, well-designed challenge.

[h1]Slay the Sprire2のゲーム体験を分ける『カギ』は、1ゲームごとにどれほど重きを置くかに拠る[/h1]

過去作に触れているという前提で、2をやってみて感じたのは「敗北数の多さ」である。得意キャラでアセンション10をクリアしていようが、5、6アセの1層負けなんてのはザラ。言い換えてみると、ローグライクとしての一側面が強くなっているように思える。

そこで喧々諤々と話題にあげられている「ゲーム体験の快・不快」と照らし合わせてみると、「ローグライクなのだから、数十回の試行錯誤は当然」という方と、「運で何もかもが決まってしまう上に、ナーフされるのでクソゲー」という方に分かれているようだ。

レビューを見て買おうか迷っている方に助言するならば、このゲームは『ローグライク』である。
ドローのヒキ、マップの構成、取得できるカード、ショップの販売アイテム……一部が上手くいかないだけで、戦略は簡単に崩壊する。そのうえ、事前に強くなることは出来ない。

その都合、やはり試行回数は稼いでナンボという考えがなければオススメできないのが本作だ。
しかし裏を返せば、それらが噛み合った時の快感はいかんともしがたいものがある。
またどのキャラでも、噛み合いまくれば「出来ることの上限値が見え透いている」なんてことにはならない。最高難易度のボスをワンパンというのも別に現実的な範疇だ。
試行錯誤の最中、「あの時足りなかったアレ」「その時来なかったコレ」が、勝利を導くように合わさった時の無敵感。
それは近年のローグライクでも指折りの成功体験となるだろう。
そういうわけなので、我慢強い貴方もレッツスパイア！

总的来说，目前的塔二就是扩充了的塔一，可以说是塔一的DLC也不为过，也出现了很多全新的东西。
但是自从塔二开始测试版之后，明显感觉到的就是安东尼更新的太水了，一直在调整平衡，拖延了几个月才上新创意工坊，你说杀戮尖塔也不是一个竞技的pvp游戏，身为一个单机游戏，不在测试版好好的研发新东西（地图、事件、角色），一直在调高水温，原本更新通知里早就说好要研发的新角色，至今才说八月底要休假了，连正常更新都没有了，才决定把重心放在新角色上，那前面等待的几个月算什么，算我很有耐心吗。
即使是这样仍然有很多的老辈子们用爱去接纳安东尼的错误，希望能听听广大玩家的意见，不要再搞什么正确与否了。
塔二确实是一款好的系列衍生作品，虽然不敢大刀阔斧的进行改革，但确实推出了新玩法新花样，正是因为我们爱着杀戮尖塔2这个游戏，所以更不希望安东尼用自己的想法去教大家玩游戏，是我们自己在玩游戏，不需要你指手画脚的教我们玩大卡组，希望安东尼能好好做游戏吧。
面对忠实的塔一老玩家，建议有能力就可以买一份品尝了，绝对是一种全新的体验；而面对那些观望的玩家，不要被引战言论和差评误导太多，建议买一份塔一看看适不适合自己，亲身经历比言语更有说服力，短时间内应该不会有折扣一说，还不知道测试什么时候才能完成，把握好生活节奏。
希望安东尼能够不辜负玩家的期待吧。

Sadly not as fun as Slay the Spire 1. The first game felt a lot more linear with its difficulty scaling and enemies didn't just get mass amounts of strength buffs every turn or get a huge boost to their basic attack out of nowhere (I fought a specific enemy in act 1 and it did about 16 damage at most per hit without buffs, the same enemy in act 3 now gets 2 more enemies in that battle and they each do between 15-22 damage per hit without buffs which is a crazy spike in difficulty considering these are regular enemies and not elites/bosses). The constant strength buff spams on soo many enemies mean that defend cards and builds that focus more on wearing the enemy down or waiting on better card draws are severely weaker vs how those builds worked in the first game. The random "?" events also tend to feel a lot more punishing in this game than they did in the first game and make it way less fun to go for them. The character balancing is also out of wack, The Regent in particular feels way too difficult to get a working build going with him vs the other characters, and The Necrobinder also struggles quite a bit. I keep seeing all these players in the discussions talking about their runs on Ascension 10 when I can barely finish Ascension 1 on any character, I don't know what kind of hardcore players this game is made for but I have put quite a bit of time into Slay the Spire 1 and also some hours into this game and I still cannot find any sort of reliable method of progressing. I get this game is meant to be challenging but, the fact that there is still no button to redo a turn/battle to try to get better, the severe amount of randomness in the game often deciding if you get to win/lose a run and the ridiculous scaling of enemies where they just spam strength buffs every other turn makes this game impossible for me to enjoy and I really hope the devs sort this stuff out and go for a better design throughout early access development.

Some good changes from the first game: the graphics look nicer, having integrated multiplayer instead of requiring a mod to do that like in the first game is neat, the addition of multiplayer cards makes the game more interesting to play in coop than just 2 people playing Slay the Spire in the same run and you get to interact as well as share stuff with the other players, the new creature designs look neat and give a nice change from the first game's creatures.

If you liked the first game I would recommend waiting for a while until the game is almost done or out of early access, its current state is in my opinion a giant mess and a shell of what the first game was. If you have never played the first game I would recommend trying that one instead, its way better in almost every way.

在某种程度上来说，一般游戏的好评率低于60%不必多说就是往垃圾游戏靠边站，但偏偏有几个游戏，打破了我们的认知。某卡的三某杀或者某些二游以及今天的主角，杀戮尖塔2，说句实在的，虽然游戏截止目前依旧是褒贬不一，但游戏也是真的好玩，至少说游戏很让人上头，抛开官方的骚操作不谈，这个游戏他本身确实是好玩的。

第一次知道杀戮尖塔这类游戏还要从她不美死说起，那时候看了一个段子，对象生日了送了一款杀戮尖塔的桌游（说实话挺心动的）但人家不满意，随后各种以杀戮尖塔展开的离奇故事发生了，道歉可以但不能拿杀戮尖塔开玩笑，也是那之后她不美死！深深的映入我的脑海里~

其实一开始并不能理解为何这么一款游戏的受众会有如此之多,但架不住游戏确实有趣。本作是一款卡牌游戏，玩家需要在一场场爬塔冒险中，通过不断选择路线、遭遇随机事件、获取卡牌与遗物，来构筑自己的专属牌组。而作为一款肉鸽游戏来说，杀戮尖塔带给玩家的可以说是每一局都是全新的游戏体验，几个角色之间除了流派不同之外也是各有特色，比如铁甲战士的叠甲流、猎人的毒杀流、机器人的球闪流，每一种玩法都能带来截然不同的策略乐趣。

不过一代版本一代神，就目前来说当前版本每个角色的强度都是不相同的，如果是新手的话个人建议铁血战士，难度低上手快，主打的就是攻防都高；等这个玩厌了之后可以选择亡灵召唤师，个人感觉这个角色的套牌上手难度也不高，很适合新人玩家使用。至于说老手适合什么角色，都是老手了，也不需要咱指指点点。

而作为一款卡牌肉鸽游戏，本作有着丰富的遗物，药水，卡牌体系等着玩家发掘使用，就论肉鸽属性来说游戏是算比较丰富的，而且在每次对战结束，都会有卡牌金币选择，在精英对战之后还有道具药水强化卡组。游戏分为三层，第一层的难度会相对简单一些，可以趁着这个优势去找精英发育，后两层敌人的数值提升就不好打了。

游戏支持三人联机，个人建议大家开语音游玩，因为三人费用和卡组都是独立的，大家可以商量一下谁先上buff，谁负责输出，如果说没有沟通各打各的，可能原本可以一波流硬生生多打几个回合。但是开麦之后游戏难度下降不说，配合的好乐趣也直线上涨。

最后总结游戏是好游戏，但是期待加个成就，就更有兴趣玩了。

If I could I would rate it neutral.  First, this game is beatiful and I did not follow the genre, maybe it was the first game that opened up the genre for the mainstream - I only bring it up here because of the obvious sales numbers.  

I played several others before this one and I have to say the events are fun but the unlocks often feel lacking, some of the monsters in later parts are really annoying and basically need to be hard countered which often hamperes your deck in other ways then, a deck beeing to large often starts to run badly.

But the worst in my opinion is the balancing of the classes.  It basically comes down to how easy a class can stack block to leave room to build on combos.  
The best in that regard is the golem(defect), with very few cards he can generate block passively which can hardly be dimished by the enemy.
Second would be the hunter(silent) I believe, then the summoner(necrobinder) and I would say - far off are the ironclad and regent.  Infuriatingly so.  

I have 10+ games on both and never managed to finish the campaign.  Those two classes have no means build in to support block, you have to build up a strat entirely through cards from ground up and are at the mercy of rng always feeling behind the scaling of the area you are in.  Very susceptable to enemy mechanics.  
It is probably meant this way, but that is not for me.  I feel like other games handle this issue better or are a bit more lenient.  I hope to see changes in the future, I will surely come back to this game in a few months down the line and adjust my review in given time.

Ein entscheidender Frustfaktor des Spiels ist die Art, wie der Schwierigkeitsgrad gesteigert wird. Statt den Spieler dafür zu belohnen, dass er besser wird und seine Fähigkeiten ausbaut, werden genau diese Fähigkeiten reduziert, um die Herausforderung zu erhöhen. 作为逻辑上难以自洽从而不让我看好的经典游戏新作最终因为朋友亟需联机体验给我送了一份。但实际游玩体验正如我预测的那般，并没有因为人多导致输出上限高了点什么，反而让下限低得不成样子。更何况，作为自来水宣发爆炸的出圈大作，这游戏在面对汹涌而来的大量新接触的玩家群体时自然而然犯了最容易也最致命的设计错误：难度曲线设置不合理。如果作为单人游戏，面对高难的情景，光是依靠设计师和玩家出题解题对抗就足够给玩家带来成就感了，但多人游戏不同，它太难了，并且玩家很容易把问题归结到队友而不是自己身上。而他一局游戏时长在30-50分钟之间，只需要大概两局，你们就能完美错过退款时限了。
先不说多人玩家在面对高难情景难以通过从而弃坑这件事，单人玩家的体验也没好到哪去。游戏里限制构筑的地方太多了，很多牌的联动性被人为取消，作为润滑物甚至机制必须的遗物获取难度飙升，出现前期打不过精英→拿不到遗物没有大提升→后期依然打不过精英这样的死循环出现。甚至一些怪物设计本身就在限制特化卡组构筑。设计师似乎没有明白，pve模式下用轮椅卡组并不会有什么问题，用轮椅通关的人大概率还会去尝试自己给自己上难度，设计师要做的是保证有足够多的可玩卡组，包括轮椅，而不是一股脑把轮椅全扔了然后留一个机制粪怪孤芳自赏，何况不久之后的吸血鬼爬行者正反手教学了所谓卡牌rouge应该是什么模样。
再说回新的多人模式：经济系统孤立，发育曲线不一致，机制不重叠这些问题根本没有得到解决，玩家反而面对是比单人模式更硬的怪，输出也变成了aoe，你没法养一个沙包帮你扛伤等你启动。明明有方尖碑，为了吾王这一类联机神作珠玉在前，你们设计团队不知道后发的优势到底用在了哪里。
唯一值得称赞的是你们把创意工坊及时端上来了，一些恶心人的内容可以通过mod规避。不过既然已经开放了mod，那我需要决定的只有在一代里玩二代还是在二代里玩一代这样简单的问题就可以了，反正你只是更新了一些完全没有联动的角色，那我回一代去玩纸片人和古夫大帝好像也没有什么问题，甚至一代依然可以通过mod来联机。你们的发行商要是会来事，在创意工坊端出来之前就应该先把一代给下架了再说。
最后说一点关于卡牌rouge以及一大类独游设计的困境，很多时候某些东西小众是有小众的道理的，为了迎合大众化做破圈，最后大概率落得一地鸡毛。游戏行业真的是馋疯了才要了命地挖这些老ip来续命，我也是闲闷了才天天搁这淘老游戏玩。说来说去，之前卖游戏那一套归根结底都是老ass和生活对线去了，炒冷饭的东西骗newass进来啃两口赚的钱也够厂商养这一大群做年货搞外包的欧美老白男。现在这年头谁还有闲钱出门挥霍啊，打两把游戏又省钱又消磨时间，这些厂商端上来的玩意骗骗玩手机和封闭主机生态的小孩和老登就算了，对付这群硬件软件都是自己搞的理工系30来岁中登真的不太够看。与其沉浸在自己的艺术品里，不如想想这群没事只会玩游戏的笔电男大笔电中登还得活个二三十年，到时候再端这样的东西上桌被喷完暴毙可能也没有翻身机会了。电影厂商能输给《牛来》，游戏界的牛来看着也已经不远了。

So after half of a year into early access the game is not in a good place. There is no hope left for improvement. I got suckered in, so might as well list some problems to help people avoid this pitfall of a product.

-The developers introduced multiplayer, and with it balancing problems for themselves: the cards and the enemies stats now need to account for not only single but two, three and four players each as well.

-Yu-Gi-Oh styled counter and floodgate card balancing and enemy design: always seeking to prevent the player from playing one way or the other, countering entire playstyles (like shivs or sly from Silent, souls from Necrobinder, claws and orbs from Defect).

-Funneling the players into building a deck around rushdown or OTK, via nerfing and punishing defensive cards, most of the bosses of this game are DPS races.

-Data chart based nerfing and buffing centered on the Ascension 10 difficulty, while ignoring bias in the data samples, alternative playmodes.

-"YOU WILL HAVE FUN ONLY OUR WAY" mentality from the developers, empty promises of new content, only two updates on main branch, sending a picture of a feet and then going on vacation.

You can get unlucky and I've definitely gotten mad at insane low-rolls, but if you make quality decisions throughout the run you can mitigate the RNG, ESPECIALLY on A0. That's the fun of the game, rolling with the punches. You aren't going to be able to force the same strategy every run. You take what you're given and come up with the best solutions on the fly, it's not a bullet-heaven do your cool combo on the enemy game, it's supposed to be hard!

Slay the Spire 2 feels like it manages to iterate on almost everything that was good about the first game - the new characters are fresh, the old characters revitalized, the general variety and design are even stronger. Another great change is fewer Ascensions that scale faster, only 10 compared to 20. A10 is also a lot easier than A20 was, but that's really personal preference.

Of course, co-op adds so much to the game as well, and really does multiply the already high replayability of the game. Easy recommendation.

Right now I think the game needs some balance changes. going from STS 1 to 2 its night and day in terms of enemy strength.
STS 1 punishes you for messing up
STS2 punishes you for doing anything. 
Almost every enemy can:
Debuff you
buff itself
give you gunk cards (the ones you either cant get rid of, hurt you if they're in your hand at turn end)
and armor themselves

Not to mention its almost hard to find an enemy that does UNDER 10 damage on average, even in the earliest stages of a run. leading to a LOT of unavoidable damage to your health.

Overall the game feels difficult but not in a fun way. instead of a run ending because maybe i misplayed or maybe my items and deck werent good enough, instead its runs where not a single relic i have matters because a boss stuffs my draw pile full of gunk cards for attacking it or the enemy simply hits harder every single attack, even though it starts already hitting for 30 damage.

If it was this difficult because im running ASCENTS that'd be one thing, but this is BASE DIFFICULTY. maybe im just bad but from other reviews it doesnt seem im alone here.

Im STILL gonna give it a positive review tho, cause i loved the first game, and im hopeful that as this game continues to develop itll get a bit better balanced for goobers like me to be able to learn the base diffs better. 
Plus it IS also still REALLY fun when you get a build that is just SO stupidly good that even the bosses capable of hittin you for 40+ a turn cant even stop you.

このゲームは現在に対するアンチテーゼである。

昨今の世の中はYouTube shortsやtiktokなど、手軽に知識を得られるコンテンツであふれている。幅広い知識の獲得という面では一見プラスに捉えることができるが、本来の私たち人類の歩みとはかけ離れている。はるか昔、私たちの古き友人は雷によって生み出された未知の物質、炎に恐る恐る手をかけた。彼らの迷いと勇気があったおかげで、我々は今日、料理を行い、電力を生み出し、ゴミを処理することができている。学びだってそうだ。本来、知識とは挑んだ困難の報酬として在るべきものである。

　このゲームはそんな我々の失われた「挑戦する心」を試している。あなたはきっと、デッキを構築していく中で慣れればなれるほど、軸を考え、無駄を省こうとしてしまうであろう。そしてその顛末として、自分の望む結果にならないとゲームを批判するに至ってしまう。しかし私から言わせれば、そんなものは自ら可能性を狭めているに過ぎない。新しい構築に挑めば、見たことのない組み合わせを試していれば、もしかしたら今までにない方法でクリアできたかもしれない。その少しの勇気を忘れないで欲しい。

　そうして試した友にこそ新たな「道」は現れるであろう。このゲームは君の勇気と挑戦を試している。さあわたしたちは君の挑戦を待っている。

The core gameplay and art style remain top-notch, but the numerical balance and enemy designs are deeply frustrating.

Inflated Stats & Harsh Checks: Bosses and elites feel like brute-force DPT checks rather than tactical puzzles. Enormous HP pools and absurd per-turn regeneration instantly invalidate slower, defensive, or control-oriented decks before they can even set up.

Punitive Enemy Design: Instead of engaging mechanics, enemies either deal unavoidable Chip Damage just to wear you down through full block, or slam you with 30–35 raw damage. This severe lack of margin for error completely destroys deck-building creativity, forcing players into a handful of hyper-optimized meta builds.

Mismatched Expectations: A multiplayer mode should lean into hilarious, chaotic party-game energy (random bullsh t go). Forcing players into hyper-punishing min-maxing during co-op ruins the fun of playing with friends.

The foundation is solid, but until the balance team tunes down the artificial difficulty, the negative review stays.

On the surface, it is a strong upgrade and face-lift from Slay the Spire 1: everything looks sharper and feels better (even in Early Access!). This is THE definitive roguelike deckbuilder. Multiplayer is an amazing touch on an incredible game, and I have spent hundreds of hours playing alone and with friends (A0 to A10 on a variety of characters), and the game still feels like it has more to offer. The developer's amazingly supportive stance towards the modding community further ensures that Slay the Spire 2 can remain fresh hundreds of runs in.

I am not without a few minor complaints for the game: a few enemies feel unbalanced to fight. Phantasmal Gardeners, Decimillipedes, Infested Prisms, Entomancers, and Globe Heads (especially Infested Prisms) can feel like "HP tax" enemies. Some enemies feel like they are designed to counter certain builds, and while I appreciate deterrence against a "one size fits all" solution to combat during a given run, I feel that some more tweaking is required to get these types of enemies right.

Slay the Spire 2 builds on the wonderful base of the first game. Building a deck, upgrade and transforming cards, gathering relics, potions, and knowledge of how to tackle each fight is the name of the game. Animations are beautiful and a nice upgrade from the first game. And 4 player co-op! What a blast!

Fun game! I bounced pretty hard off the first Slay the Spire and never played much of it. The sequel, on the other hand, has totally captured me. I was surprised to find that this was the case given how similar the two are! StS2 has, I think rightly, been described almost like an elaborate DLC than a sequel as such. Not much has changed: the basic game structure is identical, with a randomly-generated map of encounters, turn-based card combat, deck building challenges, etc. Even several of the characters and most of their cards are identical. But there are enough changes that the difference is, at least for me, significant.

Part of this is that StS2 is much easier. I am not good at strategy games and never got much of a foothold in the first StS. The sequel, however, has felt much more fun and manageable at the lowest difficulties. I have heard that the highest difficulty settings are likewise easier than their counterparts in the first game, which might be either a plus or a minus depending on your taste. 

The main factor that I find significantly different, however, is the energy economy. Where in the first Slay the Spire, upon defeating a boss, the player nearly always offered a reward that would increase the amount of energy (used to play cards) available per turn in exchange for a small penalty, this effect is much rarer in this game. That means, at least for me, that it is much more manageable to plan out a deck. Knowing with some reliability what resources you'll have available throughout the game, and having those not change too much from beginning to end, makes trying things out early on and planning for the endgame much easier. I like it. 

On more minor notes, the art has gotten a real upgrade, with all kinds of fun animations and more detailed character work in general. I already liked the aesthetics of the first game, and the sequel is nothing but a strict improvement. There is also a multiplayer mode in this one, which makes for a very fun party game if perhaps not for a terribly serious strategic challenge. 

Basically: it's good. If you liked the first game, you're likely to also like this one. If you didn't like the first game, you might also like this one if your dislike was coming from a place of finding the variability of energy availability overwhelming like I did. If you disliked it for any other reason, this one probably still isn't for you. If you missed the first game and are interested in trying out Slay the Spire, might as well see what all the fuss is about! I doubt you'll be disappointed with this game even in early access.

Man, this is sort of sad to write about. I got this game and immediately fell in love. Was able to play with some of my friends. We all love deck building games. Its certainly a nice change of pace from the competitive games on the market currently. Initially, we had no complaints. The game was just hard enough to make it enjoyable. If you lost, sometimes it was due to the RNG nature of the game, not getting the cards you need, sometimes it was playing the wrong hand. There were a multitude of acceptable reasons why we didnt complete a run. But when we did, it felt great. We took about a 2-3 month long break and when we returned to our ascension 7 run, the game was punishing and impossible. We would go on these god runs, getting the cards we need for the decks we enjoy playing the most. We would get to certain enemies, particularly the elite enemies in act 2 and the bosses in act 3, and no matter how you played it, they were TOO hard. One boss in particular is doing 30, then 40, then 60 damage in consecutive turns before you could get to your 5th, 6th, or 7th hand. And its not like you can alt F4 and  re-run it because the game (as much as it makes you believe its RNG) is all predetermined. No matter what we did, how we played our hands, or how many relics we obtained in the previous battles, we ALWAYS lose. 

Mega Crit, if you're reading this, you have a lot of work to do. The game went from one of the most surprising, fun, game of the year worthy games this last spring (IMO), to being unplayable in a singular patch. Not only that, its bland. No new characters, no new levels, no new cards or relics. Maybe, just maybe it would be tolerable if we had any of those other things, but even then, when we have to quit for the night after going on 3-4 runs, the most common thing we say is "screw this game". That is not what you want your player base to be saying about a game  that is already limited by being early access with only  5 playable characters, bland music, and intolerable fights that are predetermined from the start to beat you into the ground and THAT much closer to uninstalling. 

For those of you thinking of buying this game, if you would have asked me if the game was worth it back in the spring at $25, I would have told you it was one of the best $25 games on the market, hands down. Now? Save your money, just want for the game to release fully so they can figure this nonsense out. The developers currently are swinging like a pendulum with their "fixes", and its ruining the game, much like the developers of other companies who patch their game into being unplayable and ultimately out of existence. Praying that doesn't happen to this game so that you, the person reading this, can enjoy what we thought was the best deck building game on steam.

結論　難しくてA10を安定クリアできない理由は圧倒的な知識不足です。YouTubeやtwichを見て知識を増やしたら間違いなく勝てます。

意識する事

今のデッキでエリートに勝てる？
このショップで買うのはカード？ポーション？レリック？削除？
焚火で休憩する？それとも強化する？
３択のうち、最もデッキを強化できるエンシェントレリックはどれ？
複数体いる敵はどの順番で倒す？
残りのデッキを確認して、このターンはアタックする？守る？この戦闘で一番被ダメが少なくなる選択肢は？など

カードとレリックの組み合わせが多すぎて、このプレイ時間でも知らない構築、使いこなせないカードが沢山あります。
自分が見てる何人かの配信者の方は明らかに自分より上手くて「とても運ゲーとは言えない」とよく思います。
例えいくつかのコンボを覚えても、そのコンボが綺麗に決まる様にカードやレリックを取得できることはまずありません。
それでも知識を増やしていくと、たとえYouTubeで見たことなくても「この組み合わせも効果的なのでは？」と自分で考えられるようになるので、自然と勝率は上がっていきます。

まずは強いネオーレリックを覚えましょう。
一層エリートをボスまでにできれば３体、最低２体を倒しましょう。
そのために１層はほぼ全てカード報酬をスキップせずに獲得しましょう。
それそれのボス、エリートの行動、対策を頭に入れましょう（なんとなくでもいいので把握しておく事が大事で、特にダブルボス戦の被ダメが大きく変わります）
三層はボスに勝てる可能性が少しでもある選択肢を選びましょう（ボスまでたどり着く事ではなく倒す事が目標なので、ラメ、クロスボウ、大きなパラソルなどのランダム性が強い選択肢も検討）

まとめ
正直、A10はプレイしてる人口の上位１％に満たない層向けの難易度になってると思います（0.1%とか0.01%とかかも）。
ただ、知識さえつければ問題なく勝てて楽しめるようになるので、好きだけど勝てないから嫌いになりそうって方は他の人のプレイ動画を参考にしてプレイする事をおススメします。

本评测发布于8月22日，如果后面改好了会补发好评：①游戏机制：目前的杀戮尖塔2五个角色的强度完全不一致，可玩性也完全没法比，战士就仿佛安东尼的星主人，塔2就是为战士量身定制的；猎人是一款见到棱柱沙漏就会自动死亡的角色，遇到状态与诅咒卡也只能像安圣被法一样齁齁啊啊啊啊了；骨妹更是机制多，但是多个机制之间完全没有联动，仿佛安圣拥有猪的脑子，洞螈的躯干，霸王龙的手臂，树獭的腿部，骡子的生殖能力；储君是一个缺点明显的角色，星星以及锻剑为他带来了极高的数值输出与防御，但是这些数值都是后发收益，同时储君也不具备优秀的过牌能力，永远都在下一回合，就像安圣的妈妈小时候答应给他买游戏机，结果永远都在下一个学期一样；机器人本身能力牌就不如前面几名角色，唯一有趣的状态牌机制，随着压缩牌的削弱，变得几乎不可玩或者低收益了，机器人肯定是上辈子铁人叛乱狠狠地法了安圣并且法的时候还漏电了以至于这辈子的两世轮回都要被安圣踩在脚底下了。②游戏更新：我承认，游戏刚出的时候循环版本我玩的不亦乐乎，每一局我都想方设法地达成循环，但是因为玩家爽安圣不爽定律，玩家每次达成无限，安圣都会被法一次定律，游戏变得越来越不好玩，安圣把有意思的金卡进行频繁地削弱，并且无聊地进行一点两点数值地改动，以方便他的盛碗虫（石头）（16）主人能够刚好打爆玩家；现版本安圣肯定是希望大家组各种针对性的大卡组去应对他设计的“有趣”的各种怪物了，但是安圣开创这个幽默均卡时代，又不上升卡牌的数值，反而在不断地削弱以及加强怪物的伤害，你就告诉我，来生这张卡召唤6消耗，在二层连一只盛碗虫或蟑螂都防不住，这张卡还有什么存在的必要吗，奥斯提这类似于壁垒的机制在塔二完全没有用处，你得防的住才是壁垒，玩家角色羸弱的攻防数值对上怪物超高的攻击与血量，就像安圣现在用了最小尺寸的斐济杯发现竟然还能像风箱一样通风于是迁怒于玩家。③核心问题：感觉塔2的角色机制还是无法脱离塔1的框架，安圣畏畏缩缩给角色设计数值，却大方地给怪物提供机制与攻防，双方已经几乎匹配不上了；其次，我认为安圣已经完全不玩游戏了或者不玩高难度了，他只是一昧的观看通关率以及卡牌使用率来进行修改，以至于删去了许多原本十分趣味性的内容，他已经忘记游戏的初心是让玩家玩的快乐而不是一昧的想方设法折磨玩家，希望安圣浪子回头以至于不用被我法。

最初這遊戲是非常好玩的，可以自由構建不同的卡組。但他馬的現在完全變樣了

1. 數值亂砍：這遊戲這平衡，那怕找個小學生來做都不至於做成這樣，原本好用的卡就了了無幾，還要把好用的卡都削了，導致隨便在第一章遇到一個稍微強一點的怪就會被打成孫子。
2. 卡牌之間連動性差：有些卡的效果根本毫無關連，運氣好的時候可能開局就贏了，反之則要把把重開洗卡，不懂這樣好玩在哪，純老虎機模擬器。
3. 卡削了怪沒削：卡的數值一直在變低，然後怪越做越難，多人只要有一人拉跨直接不用玩重開，打擊一下才6，第一章隨便一隻怪就可以開場打個16，甚至還要一打多，用腳做的平衡都不至於做成這樣。

我可以理解想要增加難度變得更有可玩性，可是這樣的改動只會增加煩躁感而已，在一個這種運氣拿卡遊戲，好用的卡又了了無幾，到頭來變成在賭開局，想像一下玩個鐵血衛士，開局拿到雙倍格檔，然後接著連著幾場甚至幾十場戰鬥都不給你高格檔的卡，加上數值又被削了，所以選擇就哪幾張，很多時候就是選不到根本選不到，那心情就像吃了達憤一樣，巨難受，這遊戲我認為叫他答辯遊戲都算抬舉他了。

I thouroughly enjoyed the first Slay the spire but I cannot recommend this sequel.

The difficulty noticably higher than the first game and, whilst that's not necessarily a negative on it's own, the way this difficulty is implemented feels less "challenging" and more just "unfair"

All enemies; boss, elite and regular, hit much harder and more frequently even in Act 1, resulting in a lot of unavoidable damage as you simply cant produce enough block to reliably tank it all. This is exasperated by more enemies than the first game having damage scaling, even some regular enemies, turning a lot of fights into a race where massive burst damage feels like the only viable option. Bosses especially deal stupid amounts of damage-20, 30, 40, sometimes even 50 damage multiple turns in a row with no chance of reliably blocking most of it and giving you no break between attacks to actually hit back.

In the first game, enemies would only perform one action per turn. Here they often perform two- simultaneously attacking and debuffing you, or blocking and buffing themselves among other nasty things. This essentially means the enemy gets two turns at once, combined with the overall damage increase across the board it's easy to get overwhelmed.

There are several new enemy effects which can cripple your run. Regular enemies that permanently lower your max hp if you cant block them or permanently stealing one of your cards if you fail to kill them quickly enough. This feels less difficult and more just mean.

Perhaps the most egregious issue I personally had was that a lot of boss and elite enemies have mechanics that punish you for playing cards, such as taking significant chunks of damage for each card, locking you out from playing more than one card a turn, or rapidly choking your deck with status cards so you cant even draw your deck (one particular regular enemy gives you ten status cards on the first turn and then repeats this every few turns after).
   The result is that you will often lose not because you made a bad deck or played your cards in the wrong order, but because the game simply denies you from even having access to your deck at all. You lose through no fault of your own because you are unable to play the game.

Until the difficulty is rebalanced I would recommend avoiding this game.

平心而论，觉得“Snakebite”（蛇咬）梗很有趣的人，智商实在低得可怜。这东西的价值被严重高估了；只要前额叶皮层功能正常，就会发现这种“娱乐”既缺乏新意，也难以持久。还有那张牌的“保留”（Retain）关键词，它巧妙地渗透进了各种讨论之中——仿佛一旦不幸刷到相关帖子，这词儿就会像魔咒一样在玩家脑海里挥之不去。真正的粉丝对此嗤之以鼻；他们有足够的智力水平去理解，这些关键词不过是些哗众取宠的噱头，既不用心，又毫无笑点。因此，那些会对“Snakebite”梗发笑的人，确实是彻头彻尾的蠢货——当然，他们肯定无法欣赏那种关于开放测试（open beta test）平衡性的深度探讨；而这本身其实是在隐晦地致敬《杀戮尖塔1》（Slay the Spire 1）里的那张“Beta”牌——我敢肯定，这群人里绝大多数根本没玩过这款游戏。一想到那些脑子不灵光的蠢货，在看到一张真正高价值的卡牌在屏幕上展开时，一脸茫然地抓耳挠腮，我就忍不住暗自发笑。真是群傻瓜……我真同情他们。顺便说一句，我并没有打“Snakebite”唇钉（Snakebite Piercing）。没错，你是看不见的。那是留给特定观察者欣赏的——而且即便如此，我也只能假设她的智商与我相差在5点以内（当然，肯定是比我低）。

這段評論為體驗1.0至2.5主線內容的簡評。

1.0時期的敘事其實算是蠻吸引我的，有種以前坐在電視前看卡通頻道的感覺，在眾多二遊都選擇謎語人和偏宏大的敘事中，絕區零的快節奏單元劇算是有抓住我的眼球，並且偏卡通的美術和浮誇的動畫表現也是絕區零的一大特點。但這種敘事方式有個致命的缺陷，主線中不可能顧及所有角色，讓很多角色的劇情和人物塑造只能透過外傳形式的代理人異聞去補，並且最重要的，每個版本的劇情不管是分開還是合併看都看不出編劇想陳述的主題，而這問題直到雲歸山之前都還可以無視......

雲歸山篇也就是2.0到2.5，這個篇章對絕區零而言絕對是集所有缺點為大成的章節。雖然敘事還是有一點1.0的影子，但由於編劇貌似還想講不止於快節奏單元劇的內容，所以整體劇情品質成了講了很多但又什麼都沒講的窘況，整體劇情結構在單元劇的前提上又要加入角色背景等加強角色人設的部分，看似要改善1.0的問題但反而使整體時長更長以及章節主題顯得更加飄忽不定。其次則是玩法，絕區零是快節奏的動作戰鬥+線性地圖，這種單調玩法完全無法支撐雲歸山篇的敘事風格，在整體劇情時長已經大於1.0時期的情況下很快就會讓玩家感到不耐煩，何況文本呈現還是維持嘎啦給木的方式以及CG過場也沒有增加的情況更加劇雲歸山篇的不堪。

直到2.5也就是雲歸山篇的大決戰劇情，2.5等於是一次將絕區零的所有缺點一次引爆。2.5的整體劇情時長很明顯是多於先前版本的，然而劇情重心卻將大概80%的時間都放在師姐葉瞬光身上，另一個版本主推角色照的部份在主線中以一種極其怪異的方式呈現，之後卻又簡單的自述帶過。而接下來的大決戰劇情節奏完全一團糟，首先包含雲歸山師傅儀玄在內所有正反派角色降智，以及之後又唐突接上反派邦布的老套"對人類很失望"之類的毀滅宣言，然後被主角團沒幾句給反駁到回不了嘴，我第一次看到立場這麼鬆的反派，最後則是橫跨1.0到2.5的最終大反派邪教幹部莎拉，從雲歸山篇中間開始戲份就大減，直到2.5最後就突然和始主合體成最終王，完全沒有任何的解釋，整個雲歸山篇就此變成一個沒有主題的難看章節。

絕區零其實在美術和音樂都有不錯的表現，尤其在動畫動作的表現更是突出，但戰鬥系統以一個動作遊戲而言有點簡單，以及劇情敘事的問題又大到不能忽視，是個很可惜的遊戲。

絕區零
2.5/5

ZZZ лучше чем Genshin Impact, но даже в Genshin Impact меня не так сильно скамила гача. Это гача игра, поэтому главная претензия именно к ней. Мало того, что легендарный персонаж может выпасть с 85+(!!!) крутки, так еще это может быть проигрыш 50/50. Когда я в самом начале столкнулась с этим (я играю с релиза), то так сильно расстроилась, что на время бросила игру. Конечно, я потом возвращалась, чтобы снова получить такой "щелчок по носу" и снова разочарованной уйти. Ладно, сделали возможность выбрать какие персонажи могут выпасть при проигрыше, как сделано было в Honkai: Star Rail. Но что по итогу? Персонаж выпал с 89 крутки. Это безумие. И на оружке проиграла 50/50 потратив на это тоже около 80 круток. Я F2P и я определенно не хочу тратить деньги на то, чтобы гача дальше скамила меня, но уже на реальные деньги, а не только игровую валюту. Я читала другие отзывы и из-за них у меня создалось впечатление, что это конкретно гача жадная, а не у меня какой-то "неудачный аккаунт". 
Честно говоря, дизайны тоже стали вызывать разочарование. Мне нравились дизайны 1 сезона и даже 2 немного. Но под конец 2 сезона дизайны стали как-будто деградировать. Новый персонаж, Ремиэлла Дан, по началу была не плохой по моему мнению что дизайном, что сама по себе. Когда я увидела геймплей ее, то мне показалось это веселым и мне даже захотелось выбить ее с Велиной, которая мне изначально не понравилась из-за дизайна немного. Но когда Ремиэлла упала мне с 89 крутки, а потом поиграв с ней 2-3 дня, то поняла, что единственный хороший ее наряд - это скин. Донатный скин. Не пляжный даже, который справедливо донатный, а черный. Это взбесило меня сильно, ведь ее белый наряд УРОДЛИВЫЙ. Серьезно, я поняла что мне настолько сильно не понравился ее наряд, что наряд Велины показался на фоне Ремиэллы лучше. Даже у Промеи наряд не так плох. С одной стороны, это моя вина, что я не подумала еще немного хорошо, прежде чем крутить, а с другой стороны сделать уродливый наряд, а потом 2 платных скина, по моему мнению, свинство. Мне кажется, что будущие дизайны новых персонажей в следующих версиях будут, скорее всего, такими же уродливыми как у Ремиэллы и, вероятнее всего, будут прогревать на платные скины. То, что мужских игровых персонажей мало можно тоже отметить, хотя честно говоря это меня не так трогает, ведь некоторые из них тоже уродливые по моему мнению. Мне также показалось, что хоё не боятся экспериментировать с внешностью мужских персонажей, но как будто боятся сделать нечто похожее с женскими персонажами. Еще для меня большой минус дизайн Нормы, пока как на Чжао еще можно прикрыть глаза. 
По поводу сюжета могу коротко и ясно сказать, что не интересно вчитываться или углубляться. Я согласна с тем, что есть интересные моменты и даже есть желание почитать, а не просто нажать на кнопку скипа. 

Попробовать поиграть можно, но сильно заморачиваться с игрой не стоит. Донатить тоже не рекомендовала, особенно учитывая жадность гачи и душные игровые режимы, который могут быстро сделать персонажа слабым только для того, чтобы продать новую вайфушку до следующей вайфушки.

[/b] 

[b] E assim nasce: ZZZ! [/b] 
Zenless Zone Zero desde sua criação foi um jogo muito diferente, tanto na proposta, quando na jornada em todos seus aspectos. Ele não é um jogo mundo aberto mas sim linear mas que contém sua exploração por mais que bem básica, sua jogabilidade não é um RPG de turno mas sim extremamente frenética e contagiante para cada agente (personagem) em que você joga! E a história tem seu valor (apesar de nem sempre ligarem tanto), e trás mais afeto e carinho por cada personagem que você consegue ou avança na história!

Começando pela sua jogabilidade: [b] ACELERADA! [/b]
 O combate desse jogo é muito [b] GOSTOSO! [/b] Você se sente imparável e a cada som de [i] parry [/i] que você faz, mais te envolve na luta e mais stun você gera no inimigo! Não vou me aprofundar muito no combate porque ele pode variar bastante dependendo do seu inimigo, podemos enfrentar: [i] Etéreos mostruosos com armas um pouco fatais, saqueadores brutamontes ou com armas prontas pra mirar em ti ou até grandes hordas e bosses em conjuntos pra te atrasar um pouco na luta, em geral, [/i] [b] TEM DE TUDO PRA ENFRENTAR DO UNIVERSO DO JOGO! [/b] 

[i] Falando um pouco de outros aspectos, que seria a gameplay 'puzzle', [/i]  ela é deveras legal no início mas de fato, o que mais empolga é sim sua gameplay mais rápida que é o combate, às vezes controlamos os [i] bangboos [/i] (robôs e máquina do universo do jogo) que por si só sua gameplay é um pouco mais lenta e baseada em plataforma (que é meu gênero favorito de gameplay), mas que de fato é muito simples e não se compara nem um pouco com a gameplay principal. 

[i] Entretanto, [/i]  os desenvolvedores buscaram melhorar sua jogabilidade e tentaram a tornar mais interessante em zonas abertas e até adicionando mecânica novas e um combate mega-simples para se testar em eventos na história ou eventos fora da sua linha principal! O que já se mostrou um bom avanço, mas, que de fato o combate ainda é sua maior atração e holofote dentro da gameplay.

 Falando um pouco da gameplay ainda mas já dentro de outro tópico, ZZZ tem provavelmente uma das [b] MELHORES ESTÉTICAS POSSÍVEIS E UMA AMBIENTAÇÃO FANTÁSTICA! [/b] 

[i] Um foco na fantasia urbana, ZZZ é um mundo fantasioso mas explora um estilo muito cívico com culturas bem diversas mas que possuem suas semelhanças com nossa realidade! [/i] E para mim, [b] é o ponto forte desse jogo quando se olha pela primeira vez! [/b]  Em seus primeiros capítulos, a gente vê cenários, zonas principalmente habitáveis que, tem sua caracterização urbana mas com sua clara, pegada futurística e avançada pela sua história voltada na narrativa. 

[b] Os NPCS ajudam MUITO nessa imersão, [/b] e em cada cenário que se volta, ele te leva um pouco daquele lugar e conta sua história por [i] objetos, ações e atitudes de cada cidadão que mora naquela zona. [/i] Onde ainda na primeira temporada da sua história, temos uma região totalmente nova e fora da Nova Eridu que habitamos, que conhecemos novos agentes com seus visuais, costumes e habilidades que somente poderiam ser daquele lugar! Não gostaria de dar [strike] spoilers, [/strike] mas na nova cidade da 3.0, a Roscaelifer, sua estética é a melhor apresentação possível para uma nova mudança grande que era o costume de uma vida urbana! [i] Uma cidade no céu, com tecnologia extremamente acima do que vimos, mas que contém sua forma urbana e pacífica de viver, sendo voltada ao steampunk o que nos leva a se interessar e a revelar partes de sua história no passado, e viver seu futuro com novas mudanças! [/i]  Então posso declarar que sim: [b] A AMBIENTAÇÃO É UMA DAS MELHORES COISAS PRODUZIDAS NESSE JOGO! [/b]
 
[i] Agora, falando da maior atração, coisa que nos jogos da miHoyo, é sua chamariz de jogadores e que aqui não é nada diferente também... [/i]

[h3] PERSONAGENS [/h3]

[i] Primeiramente, [/i] [b] o jogo é separado por equipes, ou melhor, facções. Cada uma possui seu estilo de vida, princípios, habilidades e, principalmente, sua função dentro do jogo. [/b]

A primeira facção que conhecemos e a melhor, aliás, são as [b] Lebres Astutas. [/b] Na sua composição inicial temos [i] Nicole Demara, Anby Demara e Billy Kid, que também são a capa do jogo (especialmente a Anby). [/i] [b] E COMO PODERIA SER MELHOR?! [/b]

[b] A apresentação das Lebres Astutas é, para mim, uma das melhores formas de introduzir os personagens de ZZZ. [/b] Temos Nicole, uma líder mercenária esperta, durona e pilantra; Anby, uma combatente mais quieta, mas extremamente carismática, inteligente e inocente, além de ser [i] FANÁTICA POR HAMBÚRGUERES; [/i] e, por último, mas de jeito nenhum menos importante, [i] BILLY KID! [/i] Um robô construto com duas pistolas, brincalhão, carismático e amado por geral!

E é justamente com eles que somos apresentados ao mundo de ZZZ e aos Phaeton. Como em outros jogos da Hoyo, controlamos um protagonista, nesse caso, podemos escolher entre os irmãos Belle e Wise. Eles são Proxies, basicamente guias ilegais que ajudam agentes a atravessar as esferas, enquanto escondem suas reais identidades.
Os dois já foram conhecidos como Phaeton, mas precisam recomeçar e, ao longo da história, descobrir mais sobre seu passado, seus mistérios e as relações que construíram antes dos acontecimentos do jogo. Isso cria uma narrativa que consegue misturar ação, emoção, terror e drama.

E, falando dos agentes, os personagens são incríveis! Cada um possui detalhes únicos tanto em seu design, que é ABSOLUTAMENTE ESPETACULAR, quanto em sua personalidade. Temos ladrões, híbridos, cantores, astros, policiais, investigadores, construtores, membros de gangues de motoqueiros e MUITO MAIS!

Você acaba criando bastante afeto por eles, e aquela dopamina sobe quando finalmente aparece um S na tela e você consegue o personagem que tanto esperava no banner! Além disso, cada agente possui uma gameplay diferente, com suas próprias conexões, funções e sinergias, fazendo com que a escolha da equipe também exija um pouco de estratégia.

No fim, os personagens são uma das maiores atrações de ZZZ, não apenas pelo visual (que cá entre nós), é uma das coisas mais faladas, mas pela personalidade, história e pela forma como cada um consegue se encaixar no universo do jogo.
 
É isso! Existem alguns pontos negativos que eu poderia criticar, como os diálogos mais estáticos, onde os personagens ficam apenas falando enquanto uma caixa de texto aparece, bem parecido com visual novel. Não acho ruim, mas às vezes isso quebra um pouco o ritmo frenético depois das lutas e afeta a imersão.

E tenho que agradecer por sempre ouvirem a comunidade. ZZZ é, para mim, um jogo maravilhoso, principalmente pelo seu gacha, que considero bem justo. É viciante? SIM. Mas dá para jogar praticamente tudo sem gastar sequer UM REAL, já que eventos e modos dão bastante policromo. É SÉRIO, você respira e ganha policromo, cara!

Enfim, obrigado por lerem até aqui! Já devo ter umas 200 horas e continuo jogando sem parar KKKKK.

Até logo, moradores de Nova Eridu! =)

端的に言うと、これはアクションゲームではない。
研鑽なんてないし、試行錯誤なんかないし、敵を倒した達成感なんてものもない。
あくまでも、キャラの性能で殴るだけの従来通りのホヨバゲーである。
アクションゲームが苦手な人は心配する必要はないし、得意なら財布のひもの緩め方次第で無双できる。
ゆえに、私のような「楽しくアクションゲーがやりてぇなぁ」って感じのスタンスの人間が一番合わない。
下手なりの努力ってやつがエンドコンテンツでは全く通用しない。かといってそれ以外の戦闘はあくびが出るほどつまらん。なんなら要らないくらいに時間の無駄。
つまるところ、まともなアクションを求めるならエンドコンテンツしかない。しかしエンドコンテンツは持ち物検査と接待があるだけ。好きなキャラによる攻略もできないことはないが虚狩りを好きにならない限りは基本的に理論値を求められると思っていた方がいい。
あと、個人的に気になっているのはスコアアタックばっかりで敵を倒すことが目標になっていないせいでイマイチ達成感がないことと、ステージバフの内容が実質デバフ紹介になっていること。

It's a pretty good game, I enjoy it deeply. The developers are very passionate and keep improving the game. 

If you don't like gatcha game, this will not change your mind. It is definitely not a game for children.

STORY: It has up and down but it pretty decent over all. If you like anime, you will like this as well. They've added a lot more cinematic shots during the story after 3.0, which drastically increase the enjoyment during story missions.

ART: Top notch. Character design, environment, music, etc, I don't think I've ever seen someone complaining about it. 

COMBAT: It is simple but satisfying. In general, the gameplay loop is breaking enemy stance and all in during the break window. The hardest part is resource management. Which agent to  on-field to gain energy, buff timer, when to break, accumulate anomaly to stun enemy out of big move to save time. But it only matters in endgame modes, you can just smash buttons during story and events.

Наиграв в игру под 90 часов с самого первого дня выхода игры (36 минут я пытался свой аккаунт из клиента присоединить к Стиму) мне определенно есть чего сказать.

Скажу сразу,за эти 90 часов я ничего не добился. Т.к для меня эта игра была очень долго проходняком,к которому мне было или лень прикасаться,либо не хотелось вообще. Но причины этого будут затронуты в конце моего обзора. Я прошел лишь 1 сезон и первую главу 3 сезона (вот это разброс...). И у меня лишь несколько s-ранговых персонажей. Но перейдем к составляющей игры.

Дизайны персонажей:
Такая вещь,как дизайны опеределенно меняется от человека к человеку,но я могу сказать,что моим друзьям и мне самому понравились дизайны персонажей. Сохраняется стабильность в дизайне агентов,нет чего-то уж очень плохого  (Геншин,камень в твой огород кидаю). 

Локации:
Здесь я не смогу нахваливать так же,как и в разделе "Дизайны персонажей". Т.к локации мне не настолько зашли,как в том же Эндфилде. Иногда прослеживается пустота в локациях и коридорность (хотя,эта игра не претендует на открытый мир).

Персонажи:
Персонажей много (а также титечек). У практически каждого есть своя история связанная с падением старой столицы или какое у них было детство. Есть и просто персонажи пустышки,как моя любимая Бёрнис. Если обобщать,то у каждого будет свой любимчик. 

Музыка:
Я полностью согласен с тем мнением,что Sān-Z гений. Ведь создать такую музыку надо постараться. Сделать мемные Burning Desires и Tuni Giant,но в то же время Come Alive отдающую юношеским максимализмом и Prophecy,которая противопоставляется Come Alive,ведь несёт нарратив взрослого видения на то,что сейчас с миром. И да,та самая музыку из круток.... Это смак.

Сюжет:
Аспект,который я считаю второстепенным в гача проектах. Но здесь мне он реально понравился (опустим тот факт,что я первую главу 1 сезона всю прочитал,а потом начал скипать диалоги). Хоть я и принимаю тот факт,что в нем присутствуют рояли в кустах,но он мне нравится. Ведь игры для меня в первую очередь развлечение,а ZenlessZoneZero с этим хорошо справляется. 1 сезон является для меня лучшим,что случалось со мною в гача играх. И жаль,что это затмевает 2 сезон,но все мы понимаем,что китайскую арку надо просто перетерпеть. И понимание этого сбавляет горечь потерянной атмосферы и эмоций от 1 сезона. Про 3 сезон я могу сказать,что он подаёт признаки того,что будет хорошим. Первая глаза мне очень зашла. Но продукт в стадии разработки,так что дальше одного предложения не пойдем.

Фансервис:
То,что есть в каждой гачи игре. Здесь фансервис выведен в абсолют и мне это нравится. Говоря про эту вещь вспоминают то,что многим не понравилась юбка горничной из Снежной,а мне понравилась. Look, I'm not a gatcha enjoyer [i]generally[/i]. I start em sometimes, but unless I get drawn in, I fall off really quickly. Most are... basically just reasons to look at Okay-Ish character design that emphasizes big tits with a lot of gambling-like mechanics slapped on to produce dopamine and get you to spend money. I don't really agree that it [i]is[/i] gambling because you're often never going to get nothing in return, but that's mostly semantics. It's a fairly predatory system and it often fails to draw me in.

ZZZ has managed to be substantially more involved than most if not all of the other even just live service games I have ever played. I could talk about the consistent content updates, the surprising amount of work they put in to even keep older characters viable and buff them when the meta gets stronger (which, in fairness, is any effort at all), and the honestly fairly generous amount of stuff they give you. Those things, for a gatcha, are great. But I wanna focus on what has actually kept me engaged.

As a game, Zenless has a really, really fun combat system. It's button-mashy, but very flashy and well animated, and reliant on quick flashes and sound cues to react defensively, and you bring in three characters at a time. Importantly, [i]none[/i] of these characters are the same. Any two characters, even if they share the same attribute and role, will play differently. They have different animations, different uses, different places in different party compositions. Hell, if and when ZZZ reuses body types, the effort they put into the uniqueness of each playable character's animations and style makes it extremely difficult to even notice. This makes each one feel genuinely fresh and unique, which is very important for a game sort of ultimately about collecting characters. I mean, you'd think, but this is actually the first one I've seen do it, so...

The result of this extra effort is there's actually relatively few characters as well, at least for a game that's been out this long. I actually consider this a positive, again, the quality far outweighs quantity.

Also, for some reason, the Zenless writers are like... on some ♥♥♥♥. I dunno, I can't explain it. The game as a whole is post-apocalyptic, but it's so deep into it that the post-apocalypse is everyone's norm. Everyone is dealing with some kind of trauma, or horrible fear, or has some deep dark past, but it's never their forefront. It's always something that just happened to them, and you find out about, and then... you just know. It's why they are who they are, but they're... still just people and they're living their lives. And weirdly it takes all these superhuman anime hunks and babes and turns them into remarkably human characters.

The writing isn't all a hit, sometimes it really drags on and says the same thing 37 times in a row, but some of the stories have been genuinely heartbreaking. Some characters I've disliked massively, only to actually get to know them as characters and have a turn around on them because now they make sense. It helps that the voice acting is also generally superb, though I'd be remiss not to say that I think there's been some issues with SAG-AFTRA in the past, though I've heard a lot of back and forth on that and it might have been cleared up by now. Every now and then a line in a new update will just... not be VA'd though? 

Generally, especially as just a free game you can just start, I think there's nothing to lose and everything to gain to give it a try. It's bouncy and fun and genuinely a very good video game long before the gatcha elements come into play.


Oh right also uh the character design is pretty good? I like that everyone jiggles like jello, not just the girls. Could use more male characters. If you are a fan of sex you'll probably like most characters. yeah okay that's my thoughts.

Люблю желе, особенно когда оно трясётся. 
Очень вкусно ниже прикрепляю рецепт:
Желатин — 20 г
Сок (апельсиновый, вишнёвый, яблочный) — 500 мл
Сахар — по вкусу (если сок кислый, сахара может понадобиться меньше)
Вода — около 100 мл (чтобы замочить желатин)
Фрукты или ягоды для украшения (по желанию)
Замочите желатин. Отлейте примерно 50–70 мл сока в небольшую миску. В оставшуюся часть всыпьте желатин и оставьте набухать при комнатной температуре на 15–20 минут. 
Подготовьте основу. В сотейнике смешайте оставшийся сок с сахаром. Прогрейте смесь 2–3 минуты на среднем огне, пока сахар полностью не растворится. 
Растворите набухший желатин. Когда желатин хорошо разбухнет, распустите его. Можно сделать это на водяной бане (на минимальном огне, постоянно помешивая) или в микроволновке короткими импульсами (раз в 15 секунд доставайте и перемешивайте). Важно: не доводите смесь до кипения — от этого желатин теряет желирующие свойства. 
Соедините. Влейте распущенный желатин в тёплый сок и тщательно перемешайте до однородности. 
Разлейте по формам. Если хотите, разложите по креманкам или стаканам ягоды, кусочки фруктов или другие украшения. 
Застывание. Уберите желе в холодильник минимум на 4–6 часов, а лучше на всю ночь — так оно точно хорошо схватится.
